skills.description: This is the skill of using one's fists to strike at an opponent's upper body and torso, while protecting oneself from similar blows. This skill uses the Arms Law Martial Arts Strike Attack Table and may not exceed the damage done by an equivalent Striking Degree 1 attack.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: See Martial Arts Companion.

skills.name: Brawling
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to combat in which there is no organized melee (tavern brawls, riots, etc.). Targets are chosen on the basis of proximity and blows are exchanged in an essentially random fashion. This skill allows one to better handle oneself in such situations. Sometimes a character will find himself in combat without a weapon. If it is a general melee situation (i.e., combatants are using weapons designed to kill each other), such a character may make ?Martial Arts? attacks. He may not use Brawling attacks in such a situation. If such a combatant has a substantial object in his hands capable of blocking a weapon blow (e.g., a stool, a mattress, a log, a body), he may even be given a shield bonus for the item. In such a case, a GM may even allow the combatant to make a ?club? attack. In a similar manner, a combatant may ?parry? with suitable terrain features (e.g., dodge around a tree, duck under a large branch, step behind a door). As always, the GM is the final judge as to the appropriateness of such ?parrying? situations. In a brawl (i.e., a general fracas, the combatants are not using killing weapons; e.g., a barroom brawl), an unarmed character can make Brawling attacks or Martial Arts attacks as he chooses. If the character chooses to make Brawling attacks, the Arms Law (p. 71) Brawling Attack Table 3.3 should be used with Brawling criticals. The benefit of such a choice is in the relative non-lethality of Brawling attacks.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Bribery
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for offering a bribe to an individual in the proper and unobtrusive manner. At the GM's discretion, this may also allow the identification of bribable individuals; the GM may also allow the use of this skill to help in identifying persons likely to have been bribed by the evidence of some unusual behavior.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Bribing an individual who is actively seeking a bribe. <li>Easy: Bribing a low ranking clerk to provide a minor service or advantage. <li>Light: Bribing a low ranking guard not to notice a minor offense. <li>Medium: Determining how receptive a target is to a bribery attempt. <li>Hard: Bribing a petty diplomat for longterm political gain. <li>Very Hard: Determining if a particular person has been bribed. Bribing an officer of the law not to notice a major offense. <li>Extremely Hard: Bribing a judge or other individual whose actions are watched closely. <li>Sheer Folly: Bribing an individual who is under oath and believes strongly in that oath. <li>Absurd: Bribing a fanatic.
skills.notes: The goal of bribery is the exchange of money (or some other form of payment) for political or legal influence. Bribery also implies that it is not legal to purchase the favors being requested. Legal transactions should use the Trading skill. The difficulty of a bribery manoeuvre is dependent on two key factors. First is the receptiveness of the target. The other is the risk involved for the person being bribed. If the favor requested is minor, the chance of discovery small, and the punishment minor, a bribery attempt is trivial. This skill is much easier in a society rife with corruption.

skills.name: Calligraphy
skills.description: The art of fine handwriting.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Easy: 6 ranks in the written language.<li> Medium: 4 ranks in the written language.<li>Hard: 2 ranks in the written language.<li>Extremely Hard: 0 ranks in the written language.
skills.notes: A character may wish to use this skill to produce official or legal documents. May add a bonus to certain influence skills or communication skills. The difficulty is based on the familiarity of the calligrapher with the written language used.

skills.name: Camouflage
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus in hiding or concealing an item or another person by using the natural attributes of the surrounding environment.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Camouflaging a tiny object, no larger than a small knife. <li>Easy: Camouflaging a small object, no larger than a sword or military radio. Camouflaging a tiny creature (e.g., a mouse). <li>Light: Camouflaging a man-sized object. Camouflaging a small creature (e.g., a dog). <li>Medium: Camouflaging a person. This allows the target to manoeuvre through moderate cover at one half of normal movement and still receive the benefits listed above. The amount of cover may modify this ability by up to two levels of difficulty in either direction. <li>Hard: Camouflaging a large object, up to the size of a tent. <li>Very Hard: Camouflaging a large creature (e.g., an elephant). See above. <li>Extremely Hard: Camouflaging a huge object, up to the size of a small house. <li>Sheer Folly: Camouflaging a huge creature (e.g., a Dragon-although it could be smelled a mile away). <li>Absurd: Camouflaging an immense object (e.g., a castle).
skills.notes: Camouflage is used to prevent casual observers from noticing a person or object. It involves using disguise, coloring and natural obstructions to prevent the object from being seen. This skill will only prevent a casual observer from noticing the camouflaged item; a more rigorous search will almost always be successful. More comprehensive skill is gained from Hiding and Hide Item. Any Alertness or Awareness ? Senses manoeuvre made to detect a camouflaged object is 1-3 difficulty levels more difficult (depending on the success of the Camouflage manoeuvre). Whereas this skill does not thwart a concerted search effort, it does allow the camouflaged to hide objects of considerable proportions. It also allows the camouflaged to hide other people, thereby making it more difficult for them to be seen (regardless of hiding ability). Larger objects are more difficult to conceal. In addition, any object that calls attention to itself or is unusual in any way (e.g., a music box) is more difficult to conceal.

skills.name: Cartography
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to the analysis, preparation and use of advanced maps and mapping techniques, using cartographic tools. This skill complements the skill of Navigation.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Designing a map of a tiny geographical region, for example, a city park. <li>Easy: Designing a road map of a village or hamlet that includes the roads, paths and a couple of buildings. <li>Light: Designing a map of a small geographical region (e.g., a county) that includes contours, major paths and roads, and land ownership. <li>Medium: Designing a road map of a small town or city that includes the important buildings and features. <li>Hard: Designing a map of a large geographical region (e.g., a barony) that includes all prominent features including terrain. The GM's map of the area is probably drawn at this level. <li>Very Hard: Designing a road map of a large city or capitol that includes every building and many minor features (such as sewer entrances - the thieves always ask). <li>Extremely Hard: Designing a map of a huge geographical area (e.g., a kingdom or subcontinent). Many campaign settings include maps of this scale that can be recreated by a cartographer. <li>Sheer Folly: Designing a map of the known world. The creation of this map may take a lifetime of work. <li>Absurd: Designing a map of another dimension where the rules of time and space (dimensions) are not the same as the cartographer's home plane.
skills.notes: Cartography is the art of creating an accurate and detailed map. Unlike mapping, this skill allows a character to generate a professional quality map. The distances will be accurate and to scale, altitude information may be included, contours drawn, etc. This skill is very time-intensive, but the result is a map that can be easily understood by others. Difficulty of this skill is determined by the detail the cartographer wishes to add to the map. The larger the scale of the map, the more difficult the cartography manoeuvre (since large distances are harder to measure). To produce a map that includes information that is not purely geographic (e.g., a map of imports and exports) requires other appropriate knowledge. Note that a successful skill roll indicates that the cartographer produced a map of average quality for the time period. In a medieval setting, the map may still have serious flaws.

skills.name: Caving
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for determining the natural course and lay of a cave or cavern (passage or chamber). It gives a bonus when attempting an unassisted manoeuvre in a cave.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Traversing through a well-known and well-maintained underground passage with minimal turns and intersections. <li>Easy: Exploring a cavern that is safe. The only dangers present are loose footing and uneven floors. <li>Light: Traversing through a well-maintained, but unfamiliar underground passage with some turns and intersections. <li>Medium: Finding one's way out of a small cavern complex (provided that the spelunker never got lost). Exploring a cavern that has some hidden dangers such as sink holes or sudden ledges. <li>Hard: Identifying one's depth below ground, and whether or not the ground is level. Traversing a poorly maintained underground passage with many twists and turns, as well as some obstacles (rivers, chasms, etc.). <li>Very Hard: Determining the size of a large cavern by testing the echoes. Identifying unnatural disturbances, which might indicate the presence of sentient beings. Exploring a cavern rife with dangers. <li>Extremely Hard: Finding one's way out of a large cavern complex or labyrinth after getting lost. This might include such techniques as following air drafts and always moving to higher ground. Traversing a poorly maintained underground passage with which the spelunker has no experience. The passage may have numerous turns and branches as well as frequent obstacles. <li>Sheer Folly: Exploring a cavern on the verge of collapse. If this manoeuvre is not successful, the spelunker triggers the collapse of the cavern and should begin praying. <li>Absurd: Traversing the tunnels of an active volcano, in which many of the tunnels are still filled with molten lava.
skills.notes: The Caving skill allows the spelunker to manoeuvre safely in caves and caverns. This includes identifying dangers, determining one's location, finding an exit, etc. A manoeuvre should be made once for every cavern (and adjoining caves) while exploring. This manoeuvre should be made every 4 hours while traveling underground. A successful roll indicates that the inherent dangers of the area have been avoided and that the spelunker has not gotten lost. If the manoeuvre fails, the spelunker may become lost and/or injured. Partial Success and Near Success provide the spelunker with a chance to recover before becoming lost. Getting lost is more likely while traveling, damage is more likely while exploring.

skills.name: Chain Armour
skills.description: Each armour type has a Moving Manoeuvre Penalty (MMP) associated with it for untrained individuals. This penalty modifies Moving Manoeuvre rolls. The different armour subcategories are divided into five groups based upon the composition of the armour: type 1-4 = No Armor; subcategories 5-8 = Soft Leather; subcategories 9-12 = Rigid Leather; subcategories 13-16 = Chain; and subcategories 17-20 = Plate. There are no Moving Manoeuvre Penalties associated with No Armor, and therefore there is no need to apply skill ranks towards it. The Soft and Rigid Leather skills are both found in the Light Armor Skill Category; Chain is found in the Medium Armor Skill Category; Plate is found in the Heavy Armor Skill Category. Every encumbering armour has a minimum manoeuvre penalty associated with it. The skill bonus for manoeuvreing for a group of armour subcategories reduces the maximum penalty for manoeuvreing until the minimum manoeuvre penalty is reached. This limit represents the fact that weight and constriction of the armour will always hinder the character to some extent. These minimums may vary for certain superior or magical suits of armour. In addition, each armour type has a Quickness penalty associated with it. An Armor Quickness penalty can reduce or cancel a combatant's Quickness stat bonus for his DB (see RMFRR p. 33). It will not reduce a combatant's overall DB below the level that it would be at with a zero Quickness stat bonus.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Careful drop. <li>Easy: Standing while in AT 1-6 or 9. <li>Light: Rapid drop. Standing while in AT 10 or 13. <li>Medium: Standing while in AT 7, 14, or 17. <li>Hard: Standing while in AT 8, 11, or 12. <li>Very Hard: Standing while in AT 15, 16 or 18. <li>Extremely Hard: Standing while in AT 19. <li>Sheer Folly: Standing while in AT 20. <li>Absurd: Diving for cover.
skills.notes: The GM may require the character to make manoeuvre rolls for various activities in combat. The most common examples are standing up and dropping to the ground. It should be difficult to injure oneself by standing. It merely takes time. Conversely, a drop or dive is always successful, but the character may be injured in the process (+0 Fall).

skills.name: Channeling
skills.description: This is the skill of transmitting power between two willing individuals over any distance, provided that contact can be made. The transmitter of the power must be able to see the receiver or know his exact location (direction and distance, or a specific place). The receiver must know exactly when the power is coming. For example, if a Cleric was at a certain altar at a certain time (midnight of full moon) ready to receive a spell, then another spell user (or deity) could use Channeling to send him a spell (if he knew where the altar was and the correct time). This could occur when a Cleric is on a vital mission and his god decides to aid him. Characters may channel to each other. It is important to note that the spells a 'Channeling' spell user (e.g., Clerics, Animists, etc.) acquires normally through worship and the use of intrinsic power points are not subject to this rule. Similarly, the development of the Channeling skill will not allow others to gain a Channeling spell user's intrinsic spell ability. This skill applies to extraordinary channeling.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: In an epic campaign, it is not unusual for gods to meddle in the affairs of mortals. If the GM allows it, characters can attempt to communicate with their deities directly. It is a Sheer Folly manoeuvre to contact one's deity and an Absurd manoeuvre to request a favor. In addition, there is a cumulative penalty of -100, every time after the first that a character requests a favor. This penalty decreases by 20 for every level the character gains after incurring the penalty. Hence, a character can request a favor once every five levels without any additional penalty.For more details see the Channeling Companion.

skills.name: Chi Powers: Buddha's Palm
skills.description: Chi Powers are limited to Martial Artists in that they give the Martial Artist an extraordinary ability that can be considered beyond normal humanistic limitations. There are some Chi Powers, which are slightly beyond the scope of human achievement, and there are others that are impossibly beyond the scope of human achievement. It is imperative the GM reviews the Chi Powers to determine if they are applicable to his world. Some GM's like a more realistic setting while others don't mind the Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon worlds.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: If a player of Gamemaster wishes to develop new Chi Powers skills, keep in mind several guidelines that were used in the creation of all the Chi Powers skills presented. No Chi Powers skills give automatic combat capabilities to unskilled practitioners. These skills are used in concert with other combat skills that the wielder possesses. All Chi Powers skills require a significant investment in time and effort to learn. No chi Powers skill should create a spell effect that is greater than an average 10th level spell presented in Spell Law.

skills.notes: This skill allows the character to focus his inner energy to resist attacks. The type of attack that this skill resists must be chosen when this skill is first developed (e.g., Edged weapons, Concussion weapons, Unarmed attacks, etc.). The character can harden his body to this type of attack through practice and inner strength. This skill requires taking a 20% preparation action in the round immediately prior to the use of this skill (or during the snap action phase of the same round). Then the character must make a static maneuver. If successful, the individual may half the concussion damage delivered from the attack and reduce the severity of any critical by two levels of severity. If the critical result is an 'A' critical, treat it as an 'A' critical modified by -40 (modified rolls less than zero result in no effect). If the critical result is a 'B' critical, resolve it as an 'A' critical modified by -20 (modified rolls less than zero result in no effect).

skills.name: Circle Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for manipulating and using magical circles in conjunction with spells. It also allows a spell user to pursue non-magical research in defining and identifying new circles to add to his repertoire of spells.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Identifying which creature a protective circle is designed to be used against. <li>Easy: Identifying the approximate power of a circle (i.e., how difficult it was (or would be) to create). Designing a minor protective circle, which blocks the appropriate 1st level spirit). <li>Light: Identifying the skill of the person who designed the circle. Designing a lesser protective circle, which blocks the appropriate 2nd or 3rd level spirit). <li>Medium: Identifying the realm of a spell circle. Designing a greater protective circle, which blocks the appropriate 4th-8th level spirit). Learning a very low level (1-5) circle spell. <li>Hard: Identifying from which spell list the spell imbedded in a circle originated. Designing a major protective circle, which blocks the appropriate 9th-l5th level spirit). Learning a low level (6-10) circle spell. <li>Very Hard: Identifying the individual who designed a circle, provided his work has been encountered by the character before. Designing a powerful protective circle, which blocks the appropriate l6th-24th level spirit. Learning a medium level (11-15) circle spell. <li>Extremely Hard: Identifying which spell is imbedded in a circle. Designing a very powerful protective circle, which blocks the appropriate 25th-35th level spirit. Learning a high level (16-20) circle spell. <li>Sheer Folly: Identifying the level of a spell imbedded in a spell circle. Designing a very powerful protective circle, which blocks the appropriate 26th-SOth level spirit. Learning a very high level (2 1-50) circle spell. <li>Absurd: Identifying a circle that contains an unknown spell or protects against an unknown spirit. Learning an extremely high level (51+) circle spell.
skills.notes: Circles are typically used to provide protection from Demons, spirits, or other ethereal beings. This skill allows a character to identify the circles produced by others (either magical or protective). A character may also be able to design and implement his own circles. If this is the case, the difficulty of the manoeuvre determines the maximum level of spirit that can be prevented from entering the circle. If the spirit's name is known, the protective circle will be more effective. If the GM is using other magical circles, the character may be able to glean more information from the circle. If Essence Companion is being used, an essence spell-caster can produce a circle even if he doesn't know the spell being imbedded if he has studied another spell-caster's circle. A spell user automatically knows a number of circle spells equal to the number of ranks he has in Circle Lore squared. Additional circles must be encountered and studied. Option: If the GM is not using Essence Companion, allow Symbol Lore to be used to create a circle or a symbol.

skills.name: Cleansing Trance
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for purification rituals to help remove outside energies and influences that linger on an object, item, person, etc. The use of this skill enables the user to rid himself of the touch of curses and hexes. Skill must be used within 5 minutes/rank of the Cleansing Trance skill in order to benefit the user at all. Otherwise the only way to be cleansed is from a spell or a person with a higher skill rank in Cleansing Trance. Physical prodding allows one to make a static maneuver to leave the trance, as does a painful strike (modify by +25).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Purifying a minor transgression that was never actually committed, merely contemplated (e.g., desiring a second glass of wine with dinner). <li>Easy: Purifying a minor transgression that was committed with good intentions (e.g., lying to a criminal to prevent him from performing a crime). <li>Light: Purifying a transgression that was purely mental in nature (e.g., lust). <li>Medium: Purifying a transgression that harmed another (e.g., striking a loved one in anger). Cleansing a very low level (1-5) curse. <li>Hard: Purifying a major transgression that was not performed (e.g., desiring to kill another). Cleansing a low level (6-10) curse. <li>Very Hard: Purifying a major transgression that seriously injured another (e.g., murder) provided the transgression was justifiable. Cleansing a medium level (11-15) curse. <li>Extremely Hard: Cleansing a high level (16-20) curse. <li>Sheer Folly: Purifying a major transgression committed with malice (e.g., torture, rape). These actions cannot be justified. Cleansing a very high level (2 1-50) curse. <li>Absurd: Cleansing an extremely high level (51+) curse,
skills.notes: A Cleansing Trance removes all traces of impure thoughts, transgressions and curses. It is used by holy people and spiritualists to keep their souls pure. The more serious the transgression or curse, the more difficult it is to regain inner harmony. Such inner peace is important to attain salvation or remain in the favor of one's deity. The GM may wish holy persons to lay hands on members of their faith and use this skill to purify them. All difficulty levels should be increased by two unless the target's belief/faith is absolute.

skills.name: Climbing
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for climbing manoeuvres over relatively short distances through the use of handholds, etc. This could range from the ability to climb sheer surfaces to climbing a ladder. Poorer handholds or greater speed will increase the difficulty of the manoeuvre, Note that extended climbs may require the use of the Scaling skill. There are two major factors that determine the difficulty of a Climbing manoeuvre: the grade (angle) of the climb and the frequency of handholds. This skill is strenuous, but allows rapid ascents. Add one difficulty level if the surface is sandy, two if wet, three if oily and four if icy.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Climbing stairs (in combat). <li>Easy: Climbing a ladder or knotted rope. <li>Light: Climbing a rope or 45'incline. <li>Medium: Climbing a 60'incline or tree with low-hanging branches. <li>Hard: Climbing a stone wall (i.e., there are frequent hand-holds). <li>Very Hard: Climbing a rough wall (like a cliff face) or tree trunk. <li>Extremely Hard: Climbing a smooth wall (designed to have minimal hand-) or 120'stone surface. <li>Sheer Folly: Climbing a 120'smooth surface or 135'stone surface. <li>Absurd: Climbing upside-down along a stone surface.
skills.notes: No Notes

skills.name: Contacting
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for locating individuals of influence or knowledge within an urban environment. It includes knowledge of where such individuals may be found as well as information involving how they might be reached (e.g., locating a crime boss or fence, politician, etc.). This skill is the equivalent of Scrounging except that it operates for individuals or locations. Note that actual interaction with such persons are covered by the skills in the Influence skill category.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Locating the city guard or other constabulary. Locating a minor church official, generally a lay person. This person cannot perform rites or blessings. <li>Easy: Locating a petty official, someone who can process paperwork andelse. Locating a merchant that provides common services. <li>Light: Locating a merchant that provides goods of above average quality. Locating a church official who can perform ceremonies and absolve minor transgressions. <li>Medium: Locating a minor fence, one willing to trade in goods that cannot easily be traced and are not particularly valuable. Locating an official with enough influence to provide minor services (e.g., a permit, guild membership, etc.). <li>Hard: Locating a minor military official. Such a person has access to some confidential tactical information, but not to strategic information. Locating a major church official. This person has influence in religious decisions and may even have some spell-casting abilities. <li>Very Hard: Locating a person willing to sell goods that are illegal, but can easily be smuggled. Locating a fence willing to deal in valuable goods that can be traced (e.g., jewelry). <li>Extremely Hard: Locating a spell user willing to cast spells for a fee. Locating a high-ranking government official with real influence. <li>Sheer Folly: Locating a military officer with access to important confidential information. Locating a fence willing to deal in unique items (e.g., art objects, magical items, etc.). <li>Absurd: Locating a person willing to sell goods that are illegal, difficult to smuggle, and dangerous to possess (e.g., explosives). Locating a church leader. This person controls parishes for a large area and has real influence within the church.
skills.notes: The results of this skill are obvious; either contact is made or not (although Absolute Failure might indicate that contact is made with someone who only claims to be influential). The difficulty of the manoeuvre is dependent on the amount of influence being sought and the risk involved in having the influence. (Most crime bosses are hard to contact because of the danger inherent to their status.) The size of the city does not modify the difficulty of the manoeuvre, There are fewer people in small villages, but there is less influence and people tend to know one another.

skills.name: Contortions
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for manipulating one's body in order to move through small openings or absorb sudden crushing impact (other than falls). This skill also helps one escape from bonds, etc.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Touching one's own toes. <li>Easy: Performing feats of agility like bending over backwards. <li>Light: Removing a shoulder from its socket. <li>Medium: Absorbing an impact (and reducing the critical by one severity). <li>Hard: Escaping from leather bindings. Drinking from a glass held in one's feet. <li>Very Hard: Escaping from rope bindings. Removing a blindfold (while bound). <li>Extremely Hard: Escaping from cloth bindings like a strait jacket. <li>Sheer Folly: Removing a gag. <li>Absurd: Escaping from chains.
skills.notes: There are three primary uses of this skill: Absorbing an impact (such as a collision). This reduces the critical by one severity; Escaping from bonds; Squeezing through an opening. No manoeuvre is required if the opening is the same size as the character. For every 10% difference in a single dimension, the difficulty is increased by one. (For example, a 6' tall humart is attempting to limbo under a pole that is 4' above the ground. This would be a Medium manoeuvre since the human must reduce his height by 31-40%.)

skills.name: Control Lycanthropy
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for controlling one's lycanthropy. Note that this skill may only be developed by an individual already infected with an active form of lycanthropy. This skill may be used to prevent the onset of a lycanthropic change, to control one's bestial nature during such a change, or to initiate a change at will.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: The human's closest friend/love/lifetime goal is threatened. <li>Light: A close friend of the human is in danger. <li>Medium: The beast is hungry. <li>Hard: The beast's interests are in danger of being compromised. This depends on the beast's outlook. <li>Very Hard: The lycanthrope is in danger of being damaged. <li>Extremely Hard: The human's desires contradict those of the beast. Absurd: The lycanthrope is in danger of dying.
skills.notes: Every time the moon rises or day breaks (or whatever trigger situation GM decides upon), a lycanthrope must make a transformation roll. A lycanthrope can also concentrate for 1 round and make a transformation roll. Any or all of the lycanthrope's Control Lycanthropy skill bonus can be added to or subtracted from a transformation roll. If the result is positive, the lycanthrope takes on (or remains in) human form. Otherwise, the lycanthrope takes on (or remains in) beast form. Modifiers: [Full moon:-100] [Half moon:-50] [New moon:0] [No moon:0] [Daybreak:+100] [Daylight outdoors:+50] [Daylight indoors:+25] [Daylight underground:+10] [See a friend wounded:-25] [See a friend killed:-50] [Taken hits:-50] [Taken a critical:-50] While in beast form, the lycanthrope can make a control roll to influence the actions of the beast. This roll is referenced on the Self Control Static Manoeuvre Table SM-7.19 (p. 142). The difficulty of the manoeuvre is dependent on how stressful the manoeuvre is. The most difficult should be used if multiple situations exist (e.g., if the beast is hungry and the only potential victim is a friend; the control manoeuvre is a Medium manoeuvre).

skills.name: Cooking
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to cooking or preparing food. This skill bonus may also be used when detecting bad food, or preparing/neutralizing dangerous food ingredients.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Preparing a simple dish (e.g., a sandÝwich). <li>Easy: DeterminÝing if an ingreÝdient has gone bad (provided it is not obvious). <li>Light: Preparing a dish when all of the ingredients are readily available and fresh. <li>Medium: Preserving a food. Brewing normal beer (i.e., without any extra ingredients), <li>Hard: Selecting the wine most appropriate for a given meal. Preparing a dish when some of the ingredients must be substituted. Inventing a new dish that uses a specific ingredient. The remaining ingredients must be readily available. <li>Very Hard: Preserving meat while in a makeshift camp. Preparing an exotic dish when there is a ready supply of dried (or preserved) ingredients. <li>Extremely Hard: Brewing a beer that has a very specific flavour. <li>Sheer Folly: Inventing a new dish that uses a specific collection of ingredients (e.g., a recently slain Wyvern and a handful of wild mushrooms and berries). <li>Absurd: Preparing an extremely exotic dish when nearly all of the ingredients must be substituted for other ingredients.
skills.notes: The ultimate goal of the cook is the preparation of some food. The difficulty of the manoeuvre is dependent on how elaborate or exotic the food is to be. This stems from the difficulty in. obtaining fresh ingredients. Note that exotic is dependent on one's culture. Asian food is not exotic in Asia.

skills.name: Corpus Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for the identification and recognition of the corpus catalysts.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Counterfeiting
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for creation of false but believable writings or illustrations or records from scratch. It is used to falsify bank records and accounts, change testimony records to misrepresent the facts, etc. Also includes the ability to simulate official documents, official currency (coined or paper moneys), stocks and bonds.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Counterfeiting a coin when the value of the coin depends on its weight. (In other words, the counterfeiter is merely affixing some stamp on the coin that means very little.) <li>Easy: Counterfeiting a note from one's mother. <li>Light: Creating a document that looks official, but does not actually change any records. For example, counterfeiting a bank statement (but not a bank transaction). <li>Medium: Modifying an official document by replacing the original with an altered copy. <li>Hard: Counterfeiting money when little has been done to prevent such an attempt. Minor counter-measures might include milling the edges of coins. <li>Very Hard: Counterfeiting a complete collection of papers that effectively create a new identity. This might include a record of birth and/or marriage as well as a passport. <li>Extremely Hard: Modifying an official document directly. Any changes are made directly to the document itself. <li>Sheer Folly: Counterfeiting money when extensive measures have been taken to prevent such an attempt. Such counter-measures might include a water-mark, special paper, and detailed art. <li>Absurd: Counterfeiting official documentation when an original has never been seen. The counterfeiter must guess what the document should look like.
skills.notes: The difficulty of a Counterfeiting manoeuvre is dependent largely. on the amount of care that went into preventing someone from counterfeiting a particular document. Such techniques include watermarks, special dyes, intricate emblems, etc, Generally, the more important a document is, the harder it is to counterfeit. Money is particularly difficult to counterfeit since it is watched carefully. A counterfeiter must be careful not to pass too much bad money in a specific area, or the money will inevitably be discovered. The act of counterfeiting money was often considered to be treasonous, a capital offense.

skills.name: Culture Lore
skills.description: This skill provides information about the beliefs, rituals, or other information about a specific culture. Note that skill for each culture or race must be developed separately. All characters begin with ranks in Culture Lore for their own culture.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Knowledge of major holidays/festivals and when they occur. Knowledge of common stereosubcategories. <li>Easy: Knowledge of how all major and some minor holiÝdays are celebrated. Knowledge of most everyday pracÝtices/rituals (e.g., shaking hands as a greeting). <li>Light: Knowledge of the background of most holidays. Knowledge of all everyday practices as well as some more rare practices (e.g., toasting a host). <li>Medium: Knowledge of most social protocols and their origins. As an example, read any Miss Manners colÝumn. <li>Hard: Predicting which cultural traits will be expressed by an individual with whom you are intimately familÝiar. <li>Very Hard: Knowledge of how various sub-cultures inÝteract and why. This includes knowledge of how best to alleviate any tensions. <li>Extremely Hard: Predicting which cultural traits will be exÝpressed by an individual who has been closely observed. <li>Sheer Folly: Knowledge of the cultures from which a given culture evolved. This includes an intimate understanding of how these cultures view each other now and how best to alÝleviate any tensions. <li>Absurd: Predicting which cultural traits will be expressed by an individual who has been described to you.
skills.notes: This skill provides characters and players with information about a single culture. This allows the character to understand and mimic various customs and habits. This skill is useful for blending in as well as for predicting behavior (or at least understanding it). All characters begin with enough ranks to be familiar with the common customs of their own culture, but not enough to understand the origins of such customs.

skills.name: Dancing
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for performing dances. It may also apply to any circumstances in which complex and/or precise footwork is necessary (e.g., negotiating a pattern on the floor, performing certain magical rituals, etc.).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Warming up. Ballet: Moving through the positions. A plait (or bend). Tap: A flap (heel-toe-heel). <li>Easy: Portraying sensuality in ballroom dance. Ballet: A glissade (or glide). Tap: Keeping a flatfooted rhythm. Trenches (like a goose step). <li>Light: Portraying power or anger in tap. Tap: Keeping a toe rhythm. <li>Medium: Portraying grace/sensuality in ballet. Ballet: A pirouette (or turn); a grand j'ete (or grand leap), <li>Hard: Telling a story in ballet, Portraying joy. Ballet: A tour ch'ete (or kick w/ half-turn). Tap: Wings (using the side of the feet). <li>Very Hard: Portraying a simple emotion (fear, anger, sorrow). Ballet: Consecutive pirouettes. <li>Extremely Hard: Portraying a complex emotion (such as jealousy). Ballet: A controlled kick/extension. A lift. <li>Sheer Folly: Portraying a logical sequence of emotions within a story. Ballet: A leap compounded with a roll, <li>Absurd: Portraying an emotion that is antithetical to a particular style of dance (e.g., portraying despair via tap).
skills.notes: The goal of the dancer is a work of art. Towards this end, many manoeuvres are performed, many of which may be very athletic. However, art is stressed over athleticism. Self control, elegance and grace are all characteristics that influence the quality of the art. Many dances also attempt to convey a story or emotion. The difficulty of such an attempt depends on the style of the dance, Sensuality is expressed by ballet, power or anger by tap. The extent to which a dancer can entertain (or influence) his audience depends on the difficulty of the manoeuvres he performs and the grace with which he performs those manoeuvres. In general, however, the greater levels of entertainment are only possible if more difficult manoeuvres are attempted.

skills.name: Death Trance
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to causing oneself instantaneous and painless death
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Practicing. Medium: Instantaneous death. Absurd: Dying for a short period of time (up to 1 minute per skill rank), and then recovering.
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Demon/Devil Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recognizing, and identifying the major powers and abilities of extra-dimensional beings, and information pertaining to Demons and Devils (land, items, etc.).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Identifying a creature as a Demon in its true form. <li>Easy: Knowledge of the major subcategories of Demons and their general differences. This includes Demon lords. <li>Light: Identifying a specific type of Demon in its true form. Knowledge of most Demons general abilities. <li>Medium: Knowledge of each type of Demon's specific abilities, Knowledge of Demon hierarchy; status is roughly approximate to a Demon's type. <li>Hard: Knowledge of the structure of Demon society and which Demons are likely to be encountered in each other's presence. This includes knowledge of who the Demon generals are (those Demons who work closely with the Demon lords). <li>Very Hard: Knowledge of which Demons bear enmity towards other Demons. This might allow one actually to survive an encounter with a large number of Demons (while in the Pale, for example). <li>Extremely Hard: Knowledge of Demonic history as well as all of the major Demons, including their names and personalities. <li>Sheer Folly: A complete understanding of the intricacies of Demonic culture, goals, and habits. This level of understanding might threaten a character's sanity. <li>Absurd: Knowledge of a specific minor Demon, by name alone.
skills.notes: This skill provides a character and player with information about Demons, their abilities and their activities. Successful use of this skill may allow a player to read certain portions of Creatures & Monsters (or at least receive a summary from the GM). This skill is useful in identifying Demons and their motivations, attack patterns, etc. A scholar may even be able to recognize Demonic activity from indirect evidence (e.g., an increase in mental illness).

skills.name: Detect Traps
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for detecting inanimate traps or ambushes. Note that this skill is not 'automatic'; the individual must state that he is searching for signs of a trap or ambush for this skill to come into play.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Traps triggered by a rope strung across a corridor. <li>Easy: Traps triggered by pressure plates. <li>Light: Traps triggered by weight. <li>Medium: Traps triggered by turning a door knob or opening a latch. <li>Hard: Traps whose effect spans a large area (e.g., a collapsing wall or flooding room) unless the trigger is listed above. <li>Very Hard: Gas traps. <li>Extremely Hard: Traps whose trigger is on the other side of a door. <li>Sheer Folly: Traps whose trigger is specific to a given individual. <li>Absurd: Traps whose trigger is specific to a given individual and well removed from the trap.
skills.notes: The difficulty of this manoeuvre depends on the amount of effort that went into hiding the trigger. In addition, small threats are generally harder to perceive than larger threats (although most thieves don't expect a wall to fall on them). This skill also requires a very close examination of the location/object. This skill cannot be performed from more than a couple of feet away.

skills.name: Diagnostics
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for determining the medical condition of an individual. Skill must be learned for a particular race, or type of creature. One must pick the skill in either general diagnosis, or diagnosis of a specific race. General diagnostics skill of 6 ranks or higher allows certification of simple medical practice on all races (use of field equipment and healing drugs). Diagnostics skills for a specific race of 12 ranks or higher is required for surgical certification (and reasonable competence).
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: See Healing, Section 4.0.

skills.name: Diplomacy
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for operating successfully in a complex, bureaucratic foreign environment, such as a foreign royal court or any other large foreign government structure. Tact, negotiation, and deceit are all facets of diplomacy. It is used for the conducting of relations between nations. It is important to note that this skill provides a bonus for using the proper protocol in an unfamiliar situation and impressing a person in authority. This applies to situations ranging from an audience with the High King to an involuntary meeting with the Prince of Thieves. For operating within a familiar government system, refer to Administration,
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Relating to a foreign court whose government and culture is nearly identical to your own. <li>Easy: Negotiating a deal when you are willing to give up nearly everything (e.g., a near unconditional surrender). <li>Light: Relating to a foreign court with which you are very familiar; you have spent a great deal of time with their people. Determining what your opponent is least likely to concede. <li>Medium: Negotiating a deal when both sides need to make minor concessions. <li>Hard: Relating to a foreign court whose people and customs are unfamiliar to your own. Determining what your opponent is most likely to concede. <li>Very Hard: Negotiating a deal wherein the other side must clearly make concessions and your concessions are minor in comparison. <li>Extremely Hard: Relating to a foreign court whose customs are not only alien to your own, but often repulsive. Forcing your opponent to offer some concession based on his own philosophical and cultural norms. <li>Sheer Folly: Negotiating a deal wherein the other side must make all of the concessions. Note that demanding an unconditional surrender is not difficult if the opponent has been completely demoralized. <li>Absurd: Relating to a government whose people are truly alien (e.g., a first contact situation).
skills.notes: This skill is used both to relate with foreign officials and governments and to manipulate them. It is often considered more civilized to settle a dispute with a war of words (diplomacy) than with an armed conflict. When attempting to manipulate a peer, many rounds of intense negotiations may be necessary. The game of give-and-take requires skill, tact and nerves of steel. When attempting to relate within a foreign system, the difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on how different the system is from one's own. The difficulty of a manipulation manoeuvre depends on how much one is willing to give up. When negotiating, each side should make a manoeuvre roll to determine how much the other side should give up. If both manoeuvres are successful, and both sides agree, the negotiations are complete. If only one side is successful, they can declare the negotiations complete if they are satisfied with the results (or depart in disgust -their position strengthened). If neither side was successful, the negotiations are a disaster. Both diplomats must swallow their ego in order to continue.

skills.name: Directed Spells
skills.description: The skills in this category provide bonuses to directed spell attacks utilizing the elemental form to which they apply. For example, skill in fire directed spells would give a bonus to all Fire Bolts (regardless of range). Skill may be developed separately for each such spell. Developing this skill with such a spell must be able to cast it without the need of a spell casting static manoeuvre at least once a day, either intrinsically or from an item or runes.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: Modifier: [3x Defender's Qu stat bonus (as a penalty): -30 to 0] [Full Cover: -60] [Partial Cover: -30] [Static Target: +30] [Wall Shield: -30] [Full Shield: -20] [Normal Shield: -15] [Target Shield -5] [No Helmet: +5] [Full Helmet (covers face): -5] [Range: -75 to +35]

skills.name: Direction Sense
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for determining which way is north or any specific direction, without the aid of navigational instruments. Skill is useful for determining direction while underground, during the darkest night without stars, moon, or other night-lights.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: The natural magnetic field can be felt strongly, with no obstructions. Obstructions include any significant source of metal, like a building, ore mine or suit of heavy armour. <li>Easy: The natural magnetic field is disrupted by a companion in heavy armour. <li>Light: The natural magnetic field is disrupted by a storm. <li>Medium: The natural magnetic field is disrupted by the presence of a nearby ore deposit. <li>Hard: The natural magnetic field is disrupted by wearing heavy armour. <li>Very Hard: A weak magnetic field is masking the natural magnetic field. <li>Extremely Hard: The natural magnetic field has been deliberately obscured, but not masked with another magnetic field, <li>Sheer Folly: A strong magnetic field is masking the natural magnetic field, <li>Absurd: The magnetic field has been deliberately obscured and masked.
skills.notes: This skill is a semi-conscious ability that is always in operation. It is generally based on some mineral deposit in the body responding to the planet's magnetic field. This ability operates regardless of meteorological conditions. The manoeuvre roll is made more difficult if there are magnetic fields present that mask or obscure the natural magnetic field. There is an extra penalty of -50 following teleportation to an unfamiliar area. This penalty disappears after acclimating for ten minutes to the new area.

skills.name: Disarming Traps
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus in identifying and disarming, but not locating, an inanimate trap.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Triggering a trap safely. For example, turning a door knob without grabbing the portion of the knob in which a needle is hidden. <li>Easy: The trap can be triggered and blocked or diverted in some way. For example, covering the hole out of which a dart flies. <li>Light: Disarming a trap that you designed. <li>Medium: Disarming the trap requires removing a counter-weight. The trap's natural position is not activated. This often includes pit traps and rotating walls. Once the counter-weight is removed or disabled, the trap's components cannot move. <li>Hard: Disarming a lever-based trap. For example, a pressure sensitive plate that causes a lever to move, activating the trap. <li>Very Hard: Disarming the trap requires disabling a spring or other similar mechanism. Traps that propel darts or arrows are one example. <li>Extremely Hard: Disarming the trap requires removing a trigger. Removal of a trigger usually causes the trap to be sprung, so the trigger must be disabled without activating the trap. The natural state of the trap is active (e.g., a bomb or gas capsule), the trigger prevents activation. <li>Sheer Folly: Disarmingthetrap requires removing a trigger that is attached to another trigger such that one trap is triggered if the other is disabled. Both triggers must be disabled simultaneously. <li>Absurd: Disarming the trap requires an elaborate collection of mirrors, pulleys, and/or counter-weight-such a trap is ridiculously complex and very volatile.
skills.notes: The difficulty of a Disarming Traps manoeuvre is dependent entirely on the complexity of the trap. Some traps can simply be triggered safely. Other traps may require an elaborate system of counter-balances. Once a trap has been discovered, it is usually fairly obvious how difficult it will be to disarm the trap (although some cruel trap designers may make it appear as if the trap is simpler to disarm than it is). If there is any doubt, an additional Detect Traps manoeuvre can be made to deter-mine the complexity of the trap. Note that Detect Traps may reveal the trigger, but not the trap itself. The victim may not know the level of danger he is facing.

skills.name: Disarm Foe (Armed)
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to remove a foe's weapon with one's own. If successful, the opponent must make a successful RR based on the targetÒs skill ranks with the weapon being used versus the attackerÒs number of skill ranks in Disarm Foe (Armed). If the RR is successful, the disarming attempt fails. If it fails, the opponent is disarmed. There are 4 separate skills for the user to develop: 1-Handed, 2-Handed, Pole Arm and Two Weapon Combo. These refer to the type of weapon being used to disarm the target.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: See Martial Arts Companion.

skills.name: Disarm Foe (Unarmed)
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to remove a foes weapon with one's bare hands. If successful, the opponent must make a successful RR based on the targets skill ranks in the weapon used vs. the attackers number of skill ranks in Disarm Foe (Unarmed). This is an entirely different skill from Disarm Foe (Armed). If the RR is successful, the character performing the manoeuvre takes a B critical of the type appropriate to the weapon. If the RR fails, the character performing the manoeuvre may disarm the opponent, either discarding or acquiring the opponentÒs weapon. There are 4 separate skills for the user to develop: 1-Handed Edged, 1-Handed Concussion, Two-Handed, and Pole Arm. These refer to the type of weapon that the target is wielding.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: See Martial Arts Companion.

skills.name: Disguise
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to change one's appearance (not his actual shape or weight) by application of cosmetics and other props.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Adding a new facial characteristic that does not conceal one's identity in any way (e.g., a wart or beauty mark). <li>Easy: Appearing to belong to a specific group of people (e.g., soldier, pirate, etc.). The character's identity is not changed (except that his friends might not expect to see him in such garb). <li>Light: Partially appearing to be another type of creature/race. The disguise does not intend to fool the target/audience, only to portray key characteristics of the creature/race. For example, adding whiskers and white floppy ears in order to portray a rabbit. <li>Medium: Completely altering one's identity so as to appear to be someone else. This might include adding facial hair, changing one's age, etc. <li>Hard: Completely altering one's identity to that of a representative of a specific group of people (e.g., a sailor, noble, etc.). The disguise masks the character's actual identity. <li>Very Hard: Designing a costume that convincingly alters a character's race or gender from a distance of 10'or more. Closer inspection may reveal certain flaws in the disguise. <li>Extremely Hard: Assuming the identity of a specific individual whose appearance is vaguely familiar to the target/audience. This might include disguising oneself as a ruler in order to deliver a speech. <li>Sheer Folly: Designing a costume that can convince a target/audience that the character is a specific individual whose appearance is very familiar to the target/audience. The disguise is good enough to pass all but the closest scrutiny. <li>Absurd: Designing a costume that can convince a target/audience that the character is a monster of some sort even under close scrutiny. For example, the character appears to be a hairless, gray alien.
skills.notes: This skill allows a character to appear to be someone he is not. In many cases, the disguise is intended to conceal one's own identity, but a skilled disguise artist can make someone appear to be a specific individual. Combined with Acting, this skill allows a character to assume a new identity. The difficulty of the manoeuvre is dependent on how radically one's appearance is being altered and how convincing the disguise must be.

skills.name: Distance Running
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for maintaining one's speed over long distances at slow to moderate paces, including pacing one's resources (exhaustion point expenditure) and running in a safe and non-injurious manner.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Easy: Pavement, open road, <li>Light: Smooth trail. <li>Medium: Poor trail. <li>Hard: Open plains. <li>Very Hard: Broken ground, forest. <li>Extremely Hard: Soft ground (e.g., snow, desert, etc.), hills. <li>Sheer Folly: Mountains.
skills.notes: This skill is used when manoeuvring at a strategic level. It is not useful in tactical (round-by-round) situations. The base strategic movement rate is given in RMFRP Table T-5.2 (p. 67). A Distance Running manoeuvre is made when attempting to manoeuvre at paces faster than a walk, but slower than a sprint. (It is not possible to sprint for hours.) The base exhaustion rate for walking is 2 per hour; this assumes occasional rest stops. Thus, the base exhaustion rate for jogging is 4 per hour and the base rate for a run is 10 per hour. (Hence an average human can run for 4 hours and cover a distance of 20 miles, assuming he rolls quite well.) Modifiers: [Walking:-1 difficulty] [Running:+1 difficulty] [(A manoeuvre roll must be made every hour.)] [Uphill:+1 difficulty for every 5'] [Downhill:-1 difficulty for every 10'] (Grades > 30' cannot be traversed using this skill.)

skills.name: Divination
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for foretelling the future or perceiving unknown quantities/qualities with the use of divinatory means and methods (e.g., crystal balls, tarot cards, sticks, tea leaves, gleefully rooting around in the steaming entrails of freshly dead animals...ahem... sorry...dice, palms, etc.). Each method must be learned separately. Skill can also be used to scan the past and present.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Past: 12 hours; Future: 10 min <li>Easy: Past: 1 day; Future: 30 min. <li>Light: Past: 1 week; Future: 1 hour <li>Medium: Past: 2 weeks; Future: 6 hours <li>Hard: Past: 1 month; Future: 12 hours <li>Very Hard: Past: 3 months; Future: 1 day <li>Extremely Hard: Past: 6 months; Future: 1 week <li>Sheer Folly: Past: 1 year; Future: 1 month <li>Absurd: Past: 1 year+; Future: 6 months
skills.notes: A successful Divination manoeuvre gives the diviner a symbolic representation of the future. The results are invariably vague and imprecise. The GM should study horoscopes, fortune cookies, or Nostradamus for inspiration. In general, it is important that the GM not reveal any specific information. (For example, it is not appropriate to tell the diviner that he will travel to Burnwood tomorrow. Rather, the GM might indicate that the diviner sees a journey in the near future. There are ashes and a branch present. In this way, if the players do not go to Burnwood, the GM can reinterpret the divination such that it comes true anyway. For more detail see GM Law and the Mentalism Companion.) The difficulty of the manoeuvre is based on the span of time to be divined. that the divination result need only relate to the span of time divined in some way. The events divined, may actually occur at any time; divination is an imprecise art at best.

skills.name: Divination Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to recalling the meaning of a given divinatory result using standard or specialized systems of interpretation. This skill must be developed separately for each method of divination.
skills.difficulties-summary: No notes
skills.notes: This skill must be developed separately for each method of divination.

skills.name: Diving
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for controlled falling manoeuvres. This can range from controlling the direction of an extended fall to diving into water safely from a great height (up to 20'/skill rank if a successful manoeuvre roll is made or 30'/skill rank if the diver enters the water feet first).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Diving up to 1'/skill rank into water. Every 180'rotation per 10'fallen adds one complexity. For example, a 10'dive with one somersault (360') and a half turn (180') would add 3 difficulty levels. <li>Easy: Diving up to 5'/skill rank into water. Diving off a bridge (or out a window, off a building, etc.) onto a static target. Hopefully, there is a waiting hay bale or dumpster. If the manoeuvre is successful, the character may halve the distance of the fall when determining damage. Acrobatics and/or Tumbling may reduce this even further. <li>Light: Diving up to 10'/skill rank into water. <li>Medium: Diving up to 20'/skill rank into water. Diving off of a bridge onto a slow moving vehicle (e.g., a cart). <li>Hard: Diving to a specific location from a great height (e.g., while skydiving) to a static location. For every 20'fallen, the diver can alter his horizontal distance by 1'/difficulty level above medium. For example, while falling 1,000', a character needs to manoeuvre 150'along the ground. This manoeuvre will be Extremely Hard. A diving manoeuvre cannot alter a fall by more than 5'per 20'fallen (an Absurd manoeuvre). <li>Very Hard: Diving off a bridge onto a moving vehicle ( e.g., a truck or horse). <li>Sheer Folly: Diving off a bridge onto a fast vehicle (e.g., a train or Dragon).
skills.notes: The greatest challenge a diver faces, is performing his manoeuvre before his fall ends. The amount of time that one spends in the air is very short. A 15' fall takes a single second. In five seconds a person can fall hundreds of feet. The diver must complete his rotations in this span of time. The difficulty of a diving manoeuvre is determined by the amount of movement the diver must perform. Additional complexity is introduced if the diver needs to control the direction of his fall in order to land at a specific point.

skills.name: Dowsing
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for locating underground water sources through the ground. The water will be directly under the character's feet when the skill has successfully been used.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Next to a lake. <li>Easy: In a jungle or swamp. (The water might not be potable, but that's a different problem.) <li>Light: Sensing the flow of an underground stream. <li>Medium: In a temperate forest. <li>Hard: In a grassy plain or savanna. <li>Very Hard: Sensing the location of a spring; digging is thereby avoided. <li>Extremely Hard: In an arid climate. Since the dowser can sense water only (and not snow or ice), this includes tundra climates. <li>Sheer Folly: Sensing a hot spring; spas pay well for dowsers able to do this. <li>Absurd: In a desert that has not seen rain in decades
skills.notes: This skill can be used anywhere, but it is most useful when there is no obvious source of water. Unfortunately, this skill is more difficult when there is less water in the area. Note that in many cases, a failed manoeuvre does not mean that water is not present, merely that the water is further from the surface than some other location.

skills.name: Drafting
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to draw an item, object, diagram, etc. This is not freehand drawing; specialized drafting equipment (squares, triangles, compasses, etc.) is used to make accurate and precise drawings (normally to scale).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Drawing basic geometric shapes. <li>Easy: Drawing advanced geometric shapes (e.g., ellipses, cones, etc.). <li>Light: Drawing the layout of a simple dwelling (i.e., the building exists, the drafter is generating an accurate map of the building). <li>Medium: Generating the blueprints for a simple dwelling. <li>Hard: Drafting a simple object with a small number of moving pieces. <li>Very Hard: Generating the design of a simple object or average dwelling. This might include a house or catapult. <li>Extremely Hard: Drafting an object with multiple moving pieces that interact with one another. For example, a clock. <li>Sheer Folly: Generating the blueprints for a complex object or dwelling. Examples include a fortress built on a slope or a ballista that reloads itself. <li>Absurd: Generating the blueprints for an extremely complex object. A building might have secret passages that cross on multiple levels and rooms that span partial stories (creating crawlways and other access tunnels).
skills.notes: Drafting has two main applications: Generating a detailed and accurate representation of an actual object and generating a blueprint from which an object can be designed. difficulties-summary arise when the object is highly irregular or complex. When Drafting is used to generate a blueprint for the creation of some object, the Drafting skill is only useful in generating the blueprint. The actual design of the object requires some other skill (e.g., Architecture, Engineering, Gimmickry or Machination). If the blueprint is accurate, the object can be designed with a minimum of flaws. Partial and Near Successes introduce flaws that must be adjusted for by the carpenter.

skills.name: Dragon Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recognizing and identifying the major powers and abilities of Dragons, and information pertaining to Dragons (e.g., lands, items).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Identifying whether a creature is a Great, Lesser, or Minor drake. <li>Easy: Identifying the approximate age of a Great Drake. Knowledge of the abilities common to each of the major classifications of Dragons (Great, Lesser and Minor). <li>Light: Identifying a specific type of Dragon. Knowledge of most Dragons'general abilities (e.g., the petrifaction ability of a Basilisk) including its preferred climate and terrain. <li>Medium: Knowledge of each type of Dragon's specific abilities. This includes the frequency with which a Dragon can use its abilities. Knowledge of Dragon culture, religion, and status. <li>Hard: Specific knowledge pertaining to Dragon society and customs. This includes the appropriate protocols to prevent a Dragon from eating you on sight. <li>Very Hard: Knowledge of Dragon sub-cultures and conflicts. This provides a character with an understanding of Draconic motivation. <li>Extremely Hard: Knowledge of Draconic history as well as all of the major Dragons, including their names and personalities. <li>Sheer Folly: A complete understanding of the intricacies of Draconic culture, goals, and habits. This level of familiarity with Dragons might enable a scholar to predict a Dragon's reaction to a certain situation. <li>Absurd: Complete knowledge of a Dragon given its name.
skills.notes: This skill provides a character with information about Dragons, their abilities and their activities. Successful use of this skill may allow a player to read certain portions of Creatures & Monsters (or at least receive a summary from the GM). This skill is useful in identifying Dragons and their motivations, attack patterns, etc. A scholar may even be able to recognize Draconic activity from indirect evidence (e.g., a slow decline in the wealth of an area).

skills.name: Dreamworld Control
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to attempts to fully enter and to quickly depart the Dreamworld. When fully within the Dreamworld, the skill allows an individual to use real world skills in the Dreamworld. However the skill in question is limited by the Dreamworld Control skill bonus.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: This skill does not allow the use of real-world magic inside the Dreamworld

skills.name: Dreamworld Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to recognizing, navigating and understanding the Dreamworld. It provides knowledge on the inhabitants, geography, natural laws and so forth of this mystical plane.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Dream Control
skills.description: This skill allows the dreamer to have one dream on the specified topic and to remember the dream upon awakening. A failure may result in an unremembered dream or a very vivid dream on some other topic (at the Gamemaster’s discretion).
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: See Mentalism Companion 16.3.2

skills.name: Dream Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to attempts to interpret dreams within the framework of a given culture, using personal, cultural and archetypal content as the basis for comprehension. This skill also encompasses knowledge concerning dream incubation and other rituals associated with sleep and dreams for that particular culture.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Driving
skills.description: As in Riding, skill ranks in Driving must be developed separately for different subcategories of vehicles. Vehicles are defined as animals pulling such objects as wagons, carts, sleighs, etc. One skill rank allows basic understanding of the controls; subsequent ranks reflect increased ability and some quickness in manoeuvres.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Accelerating one pace category (e.g., from walk to jog). <li>Easy: Turning up to 15~. <li>Light: Slowing down one pace category (e.g., from run to jog). <li>Medium: Controlling a vehicle that brushes against anÝother (either intentionally or not). Turning up to 30~. <li>Hard: Swerving around a small object (e.g., a cat or wheel). Slowing down two pace categories (e.g., from run to stop). <li>Very Hard: Controlling a vehicle that collides with anÝother (either intentionally or not). Turning up to 45. <li>Extremely Hard: Swerving around a large object (e.g., a person or another vehicle). Slowing down three pace categories (e.g., from sprint to walk). <li>Sheer Folly: Making a right-angle turn. <li>Absurd: Slowing down four pace categories (e.g., from sprint to stop).
skills.notes: Animal powered vehicles are, in general, not particularly manoeuvreable. It is not possible to make right angle turns with such a vehicle. When the horses turn, the rear of the cart continues moving straight ahead until it is pulled into the curve. The difficulty of a Driving manoeuvre is dependent on two factors: the speed of the vehicle and how sharp the manoeuvre is. Also, smaller vehicles (like chariots) are more manoeuvreable than larger wagons. The size of the vehicle may modify the difficulty of the manoeuvre by one level. The following examples assume that the vehicle is moving at a walking pace. Faster paces result in correspondingly more difficult manoeuvres. Partial and Near Successes indicate that the vehicle either skids in the direction in which it was traveling or begins to fish-tail. A Failure indicates that no change in direction is made; the animal ignores you. Absolute and Spectacular Failures may indicate that the vehicle crashes or rolls (as appropriate). Note that animal-powered vehicles cannot manoeuvre faster than a sprint. It takes one round to accelerate one pace category (e.g., from jog to run). % of Activity used for Driving defines modification Modifier: [5%: -30] [10%: -25] [20% -20] [30%: -15] [40%: -10] [50%: -5] [60%: 0] [70%: +5] [80%: +10] [90% +15] [100%: +20]

skills.name: Drowsing
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to lazing about, drifting in and out of sleep, and falling asleep in uncomfortable or socially inappropriate places.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Falling asleep at night. <li>Easy: Falling asleep while listening to a dull speech, lecture, sermon, etc. The character must be sitting. <li>Light: Falling asleep while supine wearing leather armour. <li>Medium: Falling asleep while riding at a normal pace. Falling asleep during a discussion in which you are not participating. <li>Hard: Falling asleep while standing. <li>Very Hard: Falling asleep while supine wearing metal armour. Falling asleep while lying on rocky terrain. <li>Extremely Hard: Falling asleep while walking at a normal pace. <li>Sheer Folly: Falling asleep in the middle of a great deal of commotion (e.g., during a heated argument, or while bombs are detonating). <li>Absurd: Falling asleep during a combat.
skills.notes: This skill is very useful for characters that need to remain awake for extended periods of time. In general, a character loses one exhaustion point every hour he is awake. Thus, an average human can remain awake for 40 hours before collapsing from exhaustion. The Drowsing skill allows characters to take cat-naps in order to extend this amount of time. (It also annoys teachers.) A character can normally not sleep while some other distracting activity is going on. The Drowsing skill makes this possible. For example, a group of soldiers is traveling 24 hours a day. They take turns napping while riding in order to remain more alert. It only takes one half hour of sleep to recover all of one's exhaustion points. However, after each insufficient rest period (usually 6-8 hours), the rate of exhaustion point loss is increased by a factor of one. (For example, after 3 cat-naps a characters loses 4 exhaustion points per hour until he catches up on sleep.) A Drowsing manoeuvre can be made to fall into a light sleep, from which one can wake up easily. A failed manoeuvre can be interpreted in two ways: the character has fallen into a natural sleep, or the character failed to fall asleep (GM choice).

skills.name: Duping
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for speaking quickly, convincingly, and confusingly in order to get a victim to do something they would not ordinarily do. This skill usually may be used on only one person at a time.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Convincing someone to allow you to do something that is normally allowed, but appears suspicious. <li>Easy: Distracting a guard for a brief time to allow another person to perform some action unnoticed. The guard's Alertness skill can still be used, but not any Awareness ?Senses or Awareness ?Searching skills. <li>Light: Convincing someone to allow you to bend the rules (e.g., allowing a janitor to remain in a building to finish a task even though the building should be secure). <li>Medium: Convincing a guard to allow you past a low-security checkpoint. <li>Hard: Distracting a guard and convincing them to leave their post long enough for someone else to slip by. (Don't you think you should make sure that nobody is lurking in the alley?) <li>Very Hard: Convincing someone to do something that is blatantly illogical or contrary to obvious facts. Suckering people into a pyramid scam is one example. <li>Extremely Hard: Distracting two or three guards at the same time. <li>Sheer Folly: Convincing someone to do something that will cause them serious harm (e.g., drink a vial of cool, refreshing acid...uh, water). <li>Absurd: Convincing someone to take your place at the gallows.
skills.notes: This skill is useful when attempting to convince another that some action is reasonable, when in fact it is not. The difficulty of a Duping manoeuvre is dependent on how outrageous the action is. This skill can also be used to distract someone by causing the target to focus on the duper, and not on some other person or activity. This skill differs from Bribery in that Bribery does not attempt to disguise the nature of the action. When bribing, it is obvious to the target that he should not allow the activity, but he is overcome by greed. This skill is distinct from Seduction in that Duping appeals to rationality rather than emotionality.

skills.name: Engineering
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for knowing major facts about engineering of the appropriate technical level known to the culture. Also provides a bonus for attempts to utilize that knowledge in new engineering projects. A GM may require different subcategories of Engineering to be treated as separate skills.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Determining how a simple device works (e.g., a lever, pulley, magnifying glass, etc.). <li>Easy: Determining how a compound device works (e.g., a telescope, elevator, etc.). <li>Light: Determining whether or not a simple device can be used to solve a particular problem (without simply attempting the potential solution). For example, the engineer might calculate whether or not a pulley system is powerful enough to move an elephant. <li>Medium: Designing a new device to solve a particular problem (e.g., moving a large object from one place to another). Streamlining a process or system to improve efficiency. <li>Hard: Determining whether or not a complex device can be used to solve a particular problem (e.g., can a catapult propel a water-filled balloon over a fire such that the balloon breaks in mid-flight). <li>Very Hard: Designing a new device to solve a general class of problems (e.g., designing an aqueduct that can deliver water to any number of locations). <li>Extremely Hard: Determining the most efficient system to address a given problem (with respect to a particular variable: money, time, etc.). <li>Sheer Folly: Designing a complex device whose component parts can be interchanged in order to address a wide variety of problems (e.g., a telescope with interchangeable and reversible lenses such that the device can magnify and reduce). <li>Absurd: Inventing a new branch of engineering that tackles a distinct collection of related problems.
skills.notes: Engineering combines aspects of mathematics, physics and invention. It provides a theoretical knowledge of devices and processes. An engineer understands how and why things work (but not necessarily how to build them). Engineers also try to produce systems that are maximally efficient. Knowledge of engineering allows characters to determine what a device does, design new devices or streamline systems. The difficulty of an Engineering manoeuvre is dependent on the complexity of the device and the obscurity of the theory behind an item.

skills.name: Evaluate Armour
skills.description: Provides a bonus for determining the value and quality of armour.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Determining whether an artifact or common item has a greater bonus. <li>Easy: Determining whether an artifact or common item has a better manoeuvre modifier. <li>Light: Comparing two suits of armour (of the same type) and determining which suit of armour has a better DB modifier. <li>Medium: Comparing two suits of armour (of the same type) and determining which suit of armour has a better manoeuvre modifier. <li>Hard: Determining the specific DB modifier. <li>Very Hard: Determining the specific manoeuvre modifier. <li>Extremely Hard: Determining any special abilities inherent to a suit of armour. This does not include any magical/spell abilities. <li>Sheer Folly: Determining any minor flaws. <li>Absurd: Determining inherent magical/spell abilities in an item. (Attunement is much easier.)
skills.notes: This skill is used to determine the inherent bonuses and abilities of a suit of armour. The manoeuvre becomes more difficult when its abilities/value are hidden or not apparent. This skill does not require that the evaluator wear the armour (and thereby be subjected to the risk of curses, imbedded spells, etc.).

skills.name: Evaluate Metal
skills.description: Provides a bonus for determining the value and quality of metal objects in worked, refined or raw conditions
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Determining the value of a collection of coins. <li>Easy: Determining the value of a pure metal based on its weight. <li>Light: Determining the value of an ore based on its weight and purity. <li>Medium: Determining the value of a piece of jewelry with little artistic value (e.g., a plain gold band). <li>Hard: Determining the value of an average piece of jewelry. <li>Very Hard: Determining the value of an intricate piece of jewelry whoseis based largely on the craftsmanship. <li>Extremely Hard: Determining the value of a piece of jewelry with cultural and historical significance. <li>Sheer Folly: Determining the value of a badly damaged piece of jewelry. <li>Absurd: Determining the value of a piece of jewelry constructed from a metal never before seen.
skills.notes: This skill is often used to determine the value of jewelry. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on the state of the metal. Unrefined metals are easier to assess since the quality of craftsmanship is not important. Damaged goods are even more difficult to assess since the cost of repair must be included in the calculation.
