skills.name: Evaluate Stone
skills.description: Provides a bonus for determining the value and quality of stone objects in worked, refined or raw conditions. This skill is also used to evaluate gems.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Determining the value of a processed stone used only for construction (e.g., a brick, a slab of granite). <li>Easy: Determining the value of a quarry that produces stones for construction (e.g., limestone, granite, etc.). <li>Light: Determining the value of an unrefined gemstone. <li>Medium: Determining the value of a clean, but uncut gemstone. <li>Hard: Determining the value of an average cut gemstone. <li>Very Hard: Determining the value of an intricate gemstone, whose craftsmanship is superb. <li>Extremely Hard: Determining the value of a piece of a gemstone with cultural and historical significance. <li>Sheer Folly: Determining the value of a badly damaged gemstone (although repair is rarely possible). <li>Absurd: Determining the value of a stone never before encountered.
skills.notes: This skill is often used to determine the value of gems. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on the state of the stone. Raw, uncut stone is easier to assess since the quality of craftsmanship is not important. Damaged goods are even more difficult to assess since the cost of repair must be included in the calculation.

skills.name: Evaluate Weapon
skills.description: Provides a bonus for determining the value and quality of weapons.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Determining whether an artifact or common item has a greater bonus. <li>Easy: Determining whether an artifact or common item has a better manoeuvre modifier. <li>Light: Comparing two weapons (of the same type) and determining which one has a better OB modifier. <li>Medium: Comparing two weapons (of the same type) and determining which one has a better manoeuvre modifier. <li>Hard: Determining the specific OB modifier. <li>Very Hard: Determining the specific DB modifier (if any). <li>Extremely Hard: Determining any special abilities inherent in a weapon. This does not include any magical/spell abilities. <li>Sheer Folly: Determining any minor flaws. <li>Absurd: Determining inherent magical/spell abilities in an item. (Attunement is much easier.)
skills.notes: This skill is used to determine the inherent bonuses and abilities of a weapon. The manoeuvre becomes more difficult when its abilities/value are hidden or not apparent. This skill does not require that the evaluator hold the weapon (and thereby be subjected to the risk of curses, imbedded spells, etc.).

skills.name: Faerie Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recognizing and identifying the major powers and abilities of Faeries, and information pertaining to fairies (e.g., lands, items, etc.).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Identifying a creature as a Faerie (assuming it is in its true form). <li>Easy: Knowledge of the major subcategories of Faeries and their general differences. This includes Faerie queens. <li>Light: Identifying a specific type of Faerie in its true form. Knowledge of most Faeries'general abilities. <li>Medium: Knowledge of each type of Faerie's specific abilities. Knowledge of the Faerie court and the role each of the fey races plays in that court. <li>Hard: Knowledge of the structure of fey society and which Faeries are likely to be encountered in each other's presence. This includes knowledge of who the most prominent Faeries are. <li>Very Hard: Knowledge of which Faeries bear enmity towards other Faeries. The struggles between the Seelie and Unseelie Courts are legendary in their scope. <li>Extremely Hard: Knowledge of fey history as well as all of the major Faeries, including their names and personalities. <li>Sheer Folly: A complete understanding of the intricacies of fey culture, goals, and habits. This level of understanding might threaten a character's sanity. <li>Absurd: Knowledge of a specific Faerie, by name alone.
skills.notes: This skill provides a character with information about Faeries, their abilities and their activities. Successful use of this skill may allow a player to read certain portions of Creatures & Monsters (or at least receive a summary from the GM). This skill is useful in identifying Faeries and their motivations, attack patterns, etc. A scholar may even be able to recognize fey activity from indirect evidence (e.g., an increase in unexplained magical phenomena).

skills.name: Familiar Mastery
skills.description: This skill is used by a spell user to train his familiar
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: This skill must be developed separately for each specific familiar that a spell user has (which means this skill cannot be gained until the character actually has a familiar to work with). For every rank developed in this skill

skills.name: Fauna Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recognizing and identifying the major animal forms within a specific area, region and climate. May be developed either in-depth for a specific area or as general education in fauna/ zoological trends. Several different regions/climates may be developed simultaneously, provided that research materials are available. Note: This skill may be used for learning about specific species as well, providing great detail on the characteristics and habits of a particular type of animal.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Identifying the animals in a region that are encountered on a regular basis (e.g., birds and dogs). Very little is known except that they exist. <li>Easy: Identifying the most common animals in a region. This provides distinctions between families of animals, but not genus or species. For example, a character may know that rabbits, wolves and bears are common, but not what type of bear. <li>Light: Identifying all animals that are common to a region. The character can differentiate between some animals at the species level. For example, the character can recognize the differences between a black and brown bear. The character is also aware of general information pertaining to the animal's family (e.g., herbivore or omnivore, natural enemies, etc.). <li>Medium: Identifying animals that are uncommon in a given region. The character can differentiate many animals at the species level. He is also aware of specific information pertaining to the animal's family (e.g., hours of activity, number of offspring, etc.). Knowledge of how animals are grouped into orders is also available (thereby providing information of what similarities exist). <li>Hard: Identifying animals that are rare in a given region. The character is also aware of general information specific to the species (e.g., what type of seeds a bird eats, etc.). Knowledge of animals at the class level is also available. <li>Very Hard: Identifying the insects and other small fauna native to a region. The character also has information specific to a species (e.g., hunting techniques, general abilities from Creatures & Monsters). Knowledge of animals at the phylum level is also available. <li>Extremely Hard: Identifying the animals that can be found in similar climates and terrain in other areas of the world. The character also has specific knowledge of the animals encountered (including specific information found in Creatures & Monsters). SheerFolly: Identifying the animals that can be found in a similar climate, or similar terrain in other areas of the world. The character also knows the general culture/social behavior of the animals with which he is familiar. Absurd: Identifying the animals native to the planet. The character is familiar with nearly all details of these animals. The character may even have some familiarity with the wildlife of other planets or dimensions.
skills.notes: This skill provides a character with information about animals, their abilities and their activities. Successful use of this skill may allow a player to read certain portions of Creatures & Monsters (or at least receive a summary from the GM). This skill is useful in determining what animals can be found in a particular area and in providing information about those animals.

skills.name: Feint (armed)
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to trick your opponent to react to a false melee attack and weaken his defenses. A successful feint manoeuvre may result in a temporary reduction in the total DB of the target. To determine the success of the feint attempt, take the amount of the character's Feint skill bonus committed to the attack and make a static manoeuvre roll. The opponent's total usable OB (e.g., his Ob before delegating parry or special attacks) is subtracted from this roll. Then refer to the Manoeuvre/Movement Table in Rolemaster Standard Rules, using the Extremely Hard column. If the result is a number, this number is subtracted from the target's normal DB
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: A Feint manoeuvre may negate some or all of a target's DB due to shield bonus (including magical shields), parrying actions, skills that increase the DB of the target, or the target's quickness modifier. Any positional DB or inherent DB of a target will not be reduced by a Feint manoeuvre. Examples of positional DB are fighting from higher ground or being behind some sort of cover. An inherent DB could be general magical protection or high quality armour, both of which cannot be affected by a feigned attack. If the feint manoeuvre is successful, half of the OB committed for the feint is regained for the normal melee attack. If the feint fails, all OB shifted to the feinting manoeuvre is lost for this round. However, the player must still make his attack action. If the character develops Situational Awareness: Feinting, he may apply this skill bonus against Feinting attacks made against him in addition to any other modifiers.

skills.name: Feint (unarmed)
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to trick your opponent to react to a false melee attack and weaken his defenses. A successful feint manoeuvre may result in a temporary reduction in the total DB of the target. To determine the success of the feint attempt, take the amount of the character's Feint skill bonus committed to the attack and make a static manoeuvre roll. The opponent's total usable OB (e.g., his Ob before delegating parry or special attacks) is subtracted from this roll. Then refer to the Manoeuvre/Movement Table in Rolemaster Standard Rules, using the Extremely Hard column. If the result is a number, this number is subtracted from the target's normal DB
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: A Feint manoeuvre may negate some or all of a target's DB due to shield bonus (including magical shields), parrying actions, skills that increase the DB of the target, or the target's quickness modifier. Any positional DB or inherent DB of a target will not be reduced by a Feint manoeuvre. Examples of positional DB are fighting from higher ground or being behind some sort of cover. An inherent DB could be general magical protection or high quality armour, both of which cannot be affected by a feigned attack. If the feint manoeuvre is successful, half of the OB committed for the feint is regained for the normal melee attack. If the feint fails, all OB shifted to the feinting manoeuvre is lost for this round. However, the player must still make his attack action. If the character develops Situational Awareness: Feinting, he may apply this skill bonus against Feinting attacks made against him in addition to any other modifiers.

skills.name: First Aid
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for applications of emergency aid or treatment (limited to type of creature), such as attempts to halt or slow bleeding or damaging deterioration. It is suggested that, provided with the proper tools or bandages, a character using first aid could stop up to 5 hits/round of damage without resorting to a tourniquet. Used normally in the field without the benefits of a proper medical facility or elaborate equipment.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Easy: Performing the Hymlec manoeuvre to dislodge an object stuck in someone's throut. <li>Light: Stop Light Bleeding (1-2 hits/rnd). Each attempt takes 1 round. If patient undertakes strenuous activity in the first day of recovery, bleeding may resume. <li>Medium: Stop Light Bleeding (3-5 hits/rnd). Each attempt takes 1 round per 2 hits/rnd of bleeding. If patient undertakes strenuous activity in the first day of recovery, bleeding may resume. <li>Hard: Tourniquet. Bleeding on a limb at 6-10 hits may be stopped with a tourniquet in three rounds. Until the wound is healed, the tourniquet must be released every four minutes and 3 hits/ rnd taken for 5 rounds. <li>Very Hard: Splinting a Broken Bone. Splinting does not heal a fracture, but it does make it possible to transport the patient without risk of further injury. If a fracture is not splinted, any movement will require a medium manoeuvre roll each hour to avoid taking 1-10 hits of additional damage. The manoeuvre difficulty will increase by one level for each pace beyond a walk attempted during the hour. Special checks may be made for any normal moving manoeuvres required. <li>Extremely Hard: Giving mouth to mouth to a patient who has stopped breathing. <li>Sheer Folly: Emergency Childbirth, minor sports injuries, excessive trauma <li>Absurd: Helping with disturbing behaviour.
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Fletching
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for making an arrow out of available wood, metal, paper, and/or feathers. With this skill, sophisticated subcategories of special purpose arrows may be crafted (such as hunting, armour-piercing, message, howling, poison bearing, etc.).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Fashioning an arrow that flies half as far as a normal arrow (ranges are halved). <li>Easy: Fashioning an arrow designed for target practice. (This arrow inflicts Krush criticals of two less severity.) <li>Light: Fashioning a poor quality arrow (-5 OB). <li>Medium: Fashioning a normal arrow. <li>Hard: Fashioning an armour piercing (+5 vs. AT 13-20) or hunting (+5 vs. AT 3-12) arrow. (These arrowheads are -5 vs. all other armour subcategories.) <li>Very Hard: Fashioning an arrow that spins while it flies (due to curved feathers). (This arrow increases the severity of any critical by one, and can be combined with an armour piercing or hunting arrow.) <li>Extremely Hard: Fashioning a superior arrow that flies 50% farther than a normal arrow (-5 OB). Fashioning an arrow with a hollow tip. This can be filled with poison or modified to cause the arrow to whistle while in flight. <li>Sheer Folly: Fashioning an arrow that flies twice as far as a normal arrow. (-5 OB). <li>Absurd: Fashioning an arrow that is designed to be shot with a second arrow, thereby allowing an archer to shoot at two targets.
skills.notes: The goal of Fletching is the production of one or more arrows. The difficulty of this manoeuvre is dependent on how specialized the arrow is supposed to be. The skill is further modified by how straight the shaft must be. There will always be some variation, but high quality arrows minimize this quantity. It is also very difficult to fashion an arrow that serves multiple purposes since one function (e.g., armour piercing) comes at the expense of some other feature (e.g., an edged arrowhead that causes maximum damage).

skills.name: Flora Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recognizing and identifying the major plant forms within a specific area, region and climate. May be developed either in-depth for a specific area or as general education in flora/botanical trends. Several different regions/climates may be developed simultaneously, provided that research materials are available. This skill may be used for learning about specific species as well, providing great detail on the characteristics and habits of particular subcategories of plant.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Identifying the plants in a region that are encountered on a regular basis (e.g., grass and trees). Very little is known except that they exist. <li>Easy: Identifying the most common plants in a region. This provides distinctions between families of plants, but not genus or species. For example, a character may know that oaks, grass, and wildflowers are common. <li>Light: Identifying all plants that are common to a region. The character can differentiate between some plants at the species level. For example, the character can recognize the differences between a red and white oak. The character is also aware of general information pertaining to the plant's family (e.g., leaf and root structure). <li>Medium: Identifying plants that are uncommon in a given region. The character can differentiate many plants at the species level. He is also aware of specific information pertaining to the plant's family (e.g., when they bloom, average size, etc.). Knowledge of how plants are grouped into orders is also available (thereby providing information of what similarities exist). <li>Hard: Identifying plants that are rare in a given region. The character is also aware of general information specific to the species (e.g., how nutritious the plant is, etc.). Knowledge of plants at the class level is also available. <li>Very Hard: Identifying the fungi and other small parasites native to a region. The character also has information specific to a species (e.g., amount of sunlight and water needed, general abilities from Creatures & Monsters). Knowledge of plants at the phylum level is also available. <li>Extremely Hard: Identifying the plants that can be found in similar climates and terrain in other areas of the world. The character also has specific knowledge of the plants encountered (including specific information found in Creatures & Monsters). SheerFolly: Identifying the plants that can be found in a similar climate, or similar terrain in other areas of the world. The character also knows the general distribution of the plants with which he is familiar. Absurd: Identifying the plants native to the planet. The character is familiar with nearly all details of these plants. The character may even have some familiarity with the plant life of other planets or dimensions.
skills.notes: This skill provides a character with information about plants, their abilities and their activities. Successful use of this skill may allow a player to read certain portions of Creatures & Monsters (or at least receive a summary from the GM). This skill is useful in determining what plants can be found in a particular area about those plants.

skills.name: Flying/Gliding
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for flying or gliding through the use of natural or artificial wings (e.g., feathered wings, parachute, hang-glider, balloonist, etc.). Doesn't include powered aircraft of any type. If a character has no skill ranks in Flying/Gliding, any Flying/Gliding manoeuvres he attempts receive a special -75 modification.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Flying. A manoeuvre roll is made to determine how far the character is able to fly this round. While flying a character cannot manoeuvre at a pace faster than a sprint. Accelerating one pace category (e.g., from a walk to a jog). <li>Easy: Climbing. While climbing a character cannot manoeuvre at a pace faster than a jog. Decelerating one pace category (e.g., from a jog to a walk). Accelerating two pace categories (e.g., from a jog to a sprint). Greater acceleration requires a dive. <li>Light: Diving. Only while diving or swooping can a character attain a pace of fast sprint or dash. While diving, a character can accelerate as much as is desired without making an additional manoeuvre roll. (If the dive is successful, the acceleration is successful). Once the dive is completed, the character will automatically slow down one pace category per round until manoeuvreing at a sprint. <li>Medium: Turning up to 90?. Decelerating two pace categories (e.g., from a sprint to a jog). Landing as a 20% manoeuvre. (Landing is normally an automatic full action that occurs the round a character decelerates from a walk to stopped.) <li>Hard: Swooping close enough to the ground to make an attack at the bottom of the dive. The character is allowed to make an attack using his entire OB; he cannot parry, but retains his natural DB. If this manoeuvre fails, the character crashes. Turning up to 120?. <li>Very Hard: Turning up to 150?. Decelerating three pace categories (e.g., from a sprint to a walk). Pulling in one's wings in order to swoop through a tunnel, window, etc. The character automatically decelerates one pace category per turn. <li>Extremely Hard: Turning up to 180?. Executing spins or rolls. This is flashy, dangerous, and of little practical value. <li>Sheer Folly: Turning up to 270?. Decelerating four pace categories (e.g., from a dash to a jog). <li>Absurd: Turning up to 360?. Hovering.
skills.notes: The goal of a Fiying/ Gliding manoeuvre is the successful (safe) completion of an in-air manoeuvre. Unlike Acrobatics, Flying/Gliding allows a character to change direction while in the air. The difficulty of a Flying/Gliding manoeuvre is determined by the amount of precision required in order to manoeuvre. A gentle bank or shallow dive pier (and safer) than a sharp turn. Note that many methods of flying are unable to execute manoeuvres that involve hovering or changing direction suddenly. In most cases, it is not possible to stop manoeuvreing while flying. A character that ceases to make forward progress begins plummeting towards the ground. Some creatures (like Air Elementals) are able to control their movement completely and are therefore not required to make a manoeuvre roll.

skills.name: Foraging
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for finding any local source of potable water or edible plants and animals. Includes basic food acquisition such as gathering or fishing.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Finding water in a rain forest. <li>Easy: Finding water in a temperate or moist area. <li>Light: Finding food in a forest, jungle, or coast. <li>Medium: Finding food in a grassy plain or swamp. Finding water along a salt-water coast. <li>Hard: Finding food and water in a savanna. <li>Very Hard: Finding food and water while above the timber line. <li>Extremely Hard: Finding water during the dry season of an area whose climate alternates between monsoons and droughts. <li>Sheer Folly: Finding food and water in a desert (this includes a tundra setting). <li>Absurd: Finding food and water in a desert of dust.
skills.notes: This skill is crucial to wilderness survival. Combined with the Survival skill, a character can survive indefinitely in the wilderness. This skill provides a character with a supply of water and vegetables (plants). Fishing and clamming are also covered by this skill. Set Traps and Hunting are more useful for obtaining meat. The difficulty of this manoeuvre depends on the amount of food and water that is readily available. The manoeuvre is also modified by the number of people that need to be fed. These examples assume that only one person is being fed (and that one strategic turn, 4 hours is spent gathering). Each additional person increases the difficulty by one.

skills.name: Forgery
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to replicate specific objects, works of art, etc. Where counterfeiting is the skill of producing a believable copy of something, forgery represents the ability to reproduce a specific item. Note that this skill must be developed for a specific type of item, such as signatures, art, weapons, etc.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Producing a forgery that can fool someone with no knowledge of the subject (painting, art, etc.) who has never seen the object being copied. <li>Easy: Producing a cheap imitation to sell in souvenir shops. <li>Light: Producing a forgery that will pass a cursory comÝparison. <li>Medium: Producing a forgery that will fool someone familiar with the subject who does not look closely. <li>Hard: Producing a forgery that will pass a close examiÝnation by most people familiar with the original (but not an expert). <li>Very Hard: Producing a forgery that will only be discovÝered by an expert who examines the work closely. <li>Extremely Hard: Producing a forgery that can only be discovered if an expert compares the forgery to the original. <li>Sheer Folly: Producing a forgery that cannot be discovÝered without some form of scientific evidence (e.g., dating the materials, magic, etc.). <li>Absurd: Producing a forgery that experts believe to be the original instead of the actual original.
skills.notes: The difficulty of a Forgery manoeuvre is dependent largely on the quality of the forgery. A simple forgery is easy to create, but will be noticed by any casual observer. Only experts can catch well-done forgeries.

skills.name: Frenzy
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to attempt to go into a state of single-minded, unpredictable rage, which results in an additional +30 to melee OB, the ability to take twice normal concussion damage and the ability to deliver double melee concussion, hit damage. While in frenzy, a character has no DB other than the armour bonus, gets no shield bonus, and cannot parry. The static manoeuvre (i.e., preparation) for frenzy takes one round. Once in a frenzied state, the berserker may make a static manoeuvre each round in order to resume his normal state. Once frenzied, the berserker will continue to fight until there is no one left standing except himself, at which time he receives a +30 modification to static manoeuvres to end the frenzy. While frenzied, the berserker may attempt (with an Awareness roll at a -30 modification) to distinguish friend from foe.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: While enraged or in despair. <li>Easy: While angry or sad. <li>Light: While irritated or annoyed. <li>Medium: While in a tense situation that could possibly result in armed conflict. <li>Hard: While in a situation being solved diplomatically. <li>Very Hard: While happy. <li>Extremely Hard: While facing a pathetically inferior opponent. <li>Sheer Folly: While in a state of bliss. <li>Absurd: While magically calmed.
skills.notes: The difficulty in entering a frenzied state depends on the character's emotional state. This can be augmented with the use of certain drugs. (The Norse were known for eating a particular mushroom.)

skills.name: Gambling
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus when playing any game with a significant element of luck. Also includes cheating as a form of improving one's luck at any game.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Easy: Using a small mirror to see an opponent's hand. Medium: Stacking the deck while shuffling. <li>Hard: Palming a card. <li>Very Hard: Switching dice. <li>Sheer Folly: Sliding dice. (This prevents them from rolling, allowing the cheater to control the result.)
skills.notes: At its most basic level, this skill provides a knowledge of various games of chance including card games, dice games, casino games, etc. When this skill is used without cheating, players make a basic manoeuvre roll; the player rolling highest wins. In this case, gambling skill represents knowledge of the odds. If the game is based purely on chance, then the players should simply compare die rolls. When cheating, a player should choose the manoeuvre difficulty. If the manoeuvre is successful, all other players must make an Alertness manoeuvre of the same difficulty to detect the cheater. If the cheater is not caught, he can modify his next gambling manoeuvre by the amount indicated on the Technical/Trage General Static Manoeuvre Table SM-7.25 (p. 145).

skills.name: Gimmickry
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for making plans for an uncommon or not yet invented item. The character does not receive materials or other essentials for the production of item (such as mathematics, laen, wood carving, etc.). The GM must approve the creation of any such item.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Making trivial repairs. <li>Easy: Temporarily tweaking an object in order to improve some aspect (e.g., allowing a crossbow to shoot 10% further). There will almost always be some disadvantage (e.g., -5 OB). <li>Light: Making minor repairs. <li>Medium: Altering a device to significantly improve performance, at the cost of safety and durability. <li>Hard: Making normal repairs. <li>Very Hard: Converting one object into another object (e.g., converting a compass into a magnifying glass). <li>Extremely Hard: Repairing a badly damaged object. <li>Sheer Folly: Merging two unrelated items into one (e.g., a ballista and a telescope). <li>Absurd: Repairing a nearly destroyed object.
skills.notes: Gimmickry is a skill that provides a character with a great deal of flexibility. Only the player's imagination (and his character's skill) limits the possible results of a gimmickry manoeuvre. The GM must carefully analyze any proposal. The use of Gimmickry is always tied to some other skill (like Engineering or Mechanition). If the character has an insufficient understanding of any pre-requisite skills, no Gimmickry manoeuvre can be made. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on the character's other skills, the culture and technology, and how disruptive the invention would be to the game (e.g., inventing a portable explosive might make physical barriers irrelevant). Note that protosubcategories inevitably have many minor flaws. This skill can also be used to provide temporary repairs or alterations to an object (jury-rigging). If the GM allows this, the Gimmickry manoeuvre does not have any pre-requisites. The character can simply attempt to make the repairs/modifications by making a manoeuvre roll. Whatever the result, jury-rigging is a temporary solution.

skills.name: Glyph Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for drawing appropriate glyphs for use with the Glyphs spell list.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: Each rank of Glyph Lore allows the character to draw a glyph that can be used with the same rank spell from Glyphs. This skill also gives the caster a chance to decipher what spell a specific glyph is designed to hold and the general parameters of the spell.

skills.name: Healing Trance
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for increasing one's healing rate. The individual using this skill goes into a coma. Healing rate is increased/decreased by the amount the static manoeuvre roll is over 100 as a percentage times the racial healing rate (see RMFRP Section 24.1). Physical prodding allows one to make a static manoeuvre to leave the trance, as does a painful strike (modify by +25).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: An isolated and sound-proof room. <li>Easy: A quiet room in which all of the occupants are sleeping. <li>Light: A still setting with some noise, but no activity (e.g., in a peaceful glen). <li>Medium: A relatively sedate setting in which there is some activity, but it is muffled. <li>Hard: While in a room where two people are having a conversation. <li>Very Hard: An active setting in which there is a great deal of movement. <li>Extremely Hard: In a noisy or disruptive environment (e.g., during an argument). <li>Sheer Folly: In an extremely noisy or distracting environment (e.g., while being bombed or shot at). <li>Absurd: While in melee.
skills.notes: The difficulty of a Healing Trance manoeuvre depends on the level of noise and activity in the immediate surroundings.

skills.name: Heraldry
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for designing or recognizing the particular heraldic crests (coats-of-arms) specific to a given culture. Separate cultures must be developed separately.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Identifying a common crest as local. RecognizÝing the king's crest. <li>Easy: The ability to reproduce the most common crests in the area. <li>Light: Knowledge of the rulers that use a specific comÝmon crest. <li>Medium: The ability to reproduce all common crests and some rare crests. Identifying the general alignÝment of a group based on the crest they display. <li>Hard: Identifying uncommon crests and knowledge of those groups'affiliations. <li>Very Hard: The ability to reproduce an uncommon crest. <li>Extremely Hard: Identifying a personal crest and knowlÝedge of the family-head that uses that crest. <li>Sheer Folly: Identifying an individual by his crest. <li>Absurd: Identifying the coat-of-arms of a foreign family that visited the area years ago.
skills.notes: This skill allows a character to gain knowledge about the heraldic crests of a specific region/culture. The GM may want to provide the player with specific information before play begins. Knowledge of heraldry also implies a general understanding of politics. Crests are used to identify friend from foe. Thus, a herald can identify his enemies and allies if they are displaying a banner. In addition, coats-of-arms are used to trace lineage. As families branch and merge, their symbols also evolve. A herald is familiar with the genealogy of an area. Common crests are those displayed by lords and rulers. Uncommon crests are worn by organizations and merchant families. Personal crests are unique to a family name, but families that are closely connected will have similar crests.

skills.name: Herb Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recognizing/identifying herbs.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Knowledge of category (e.g., bone repair, muscle repair, etc.). <li>Easy: Knowledge of climate/locale codes (e.g., m-U). <li>Light: Knowledge of form/prep (e.g., flower/ingest). <li>Medium: Knowledge of specific effects (e.g., heals 1-10 hits). <li>Hard: Knowledge of market value. <li>Very Hard: Knowledge of addiction factor. <li>Extremely Hard: Identifying an herb in its prepared state. <li>Sheer Folly: Knowledge of the combined effects of two herbs in the same category. <li>Absurd: Knowledge of the combined effects of two herbs in different categories.
skills.notes: The difficulty of locating an herb is indicated in RMFRP (p. 149). That provides the difficulty of finding such an herb in the wild. The number associated with the difficulty of finding a given herb indicates its rarity. If a character has 4 ranks in Herb Lore (i.e., knowledge level 3), he is familiar with rewk (t-D-3), including how to prepare it. He knows that yavethalion (m-O-5) provides concussion relief and that akbutege (s0-2) heals 1-10 hits.

skills.name: Herding
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for gathering, befriending, or manipulating herd animals. Skill normally deals with one coherent group (herd) of animals at a time. This skill must be developed separately for each different type of animal.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Moving a herd to familiar pasture. <li>Easy: Moving a herd in a straight line. <li>Light: Negotiating corners. Gathering the animals into a herd in order to begin moving them. <li>Medium: Convincing a herd to return to an enclosed space. <li>Hard: Preventing any of the animals from moving too close to some danger (as perceived by the herder, not the aniÝmal). For some reaÝson, some animals seem driven to fall off of ledges or cliffs. <li>Very Hard: Fleeing a dangerous situation. (The herd tends to scatter.) <li>Extremely Hard: Convincing a herd to stampede in the direction of a minor threat. <li>Sheer Folly: Keeping a herd together while fleeing from a Demon or other awesome creature. <li>Absurd: Convincing a herd to approach a Dragon or other awesome creature.
skills.notes: This skill allows a character to manoeuvre a group of animals according to his will. This skill is most useful for manoeuvreing herbivores, although any animal that travels in a pack can be herded. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on how contrary to the animal's instincts the manoeuvre is. Eating is instinctual, charging an opponent is not. Modifier: [Character has a properly trained herd dog: +20]

skills.name: Hiding
skills.description: Hiding is the ability to conceal one's presence by remaining still within a place of concealment, using silence, shadow and camouflage; Stalking is the same ability used when moving.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: There are ample places to hide that provide complete concealment. A warehouse of empty crates and a cluttered attic are two examples. <li>Easy: There are many locations that provide at least 75% cover. For example, behind a curtain, in a large basket, or under a bed, or in a natural cavern. <li>Light: There are many locations that provide 50% cover and ample deep shadows or other dark cover. A dense forest or jungle, or a garbage-filled alley are two examples. <li>Medium: There are some physical obstructions (e.g., pillars, curtains, etc.) as well as ample dark corners/ cubbyholes. <li>Hard: There are a many locations that provide 25% cover and many locations with partial cover (like bushes or smoke). For example, a mature forest, or a pavilion. <li>Very Hard: There are no physical barriers, but there are many locations that obscure observation (e.g., tall grass, stained glass or paper walls). <li>Extremely Hard: There are no solid objects behind which to hide, but there is some cover provided by less dense objects. For example, hiding in a green-house or behind a picket fence. <li>Sheer Folly: There are no physical obstructions, but there are some irregular features that cast shadows. The smoke provided by a campfire might also be used. <li>Absurd: Hiding in an otherwise empty room.
skills.notes: The difficulty of a Hiding manoeuvre depends on the quality of the hiding place. The cover being used by the skulk may be solid or translucent; it is easier to hide behind a rock than in a shadow. This skill includes choosing a hiding place that is not obvious (e.g., behind a potted plant). A Hiding manoeuvre is modified by the Alertness bonuses of all potential observers. If the manoeuvre is successful, no Alertness manoeuvre should be made unless someone moves very near to the hidden character. Other Awareness skills can still be used to locate the thief, however

skills.name: Hiding Items
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to hide an item from other beings.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Hiding a small supply of an herb or poison (less than 1 ounce). <li>Easy: Concealing a razor blade, lock pick, or other tiny implement. <li>Light: Hiding a moderate supply of herbs or drugs (up to 1 pound). <li>Medium: Concealing a small knife so that it is not found in a cursory search. <li>Hard: Hiding a collection of documents (up to 50). <li>Very Hard: Concealing a dagger or other small weapon. <li>Extremely Hard: Hiding an irregularly shaped object, like a banana. <li>Sheer Folly: Hiding a living creature like a small cat. <li>Absurd: Concealing a sword or other large weapon.
skills.notes: The difficulty of this skill depends on the size of the object being hidden. This skill supposes that the item is being hidden on one's person. The character may desire to smuggle some goods or conceal a weapon. Hiding an object on another person increases the difficulty by two levels. Hiding an object somewhere else requires use of the Camouflage skill. If this skill is successful, the object will not be found unless the character is searched carefully. An Absolute Success indicates that even a careful search will not locate the item.

skills.name: History
skills.description: This skill provides knowledge about the past. One may develop this skill in general World History (subject to the available learning materials i.e., if knowledge about the other side of the world is not available it may not be learned) although the information will be far less specific, focusing instead on the broad strokes of history. If this skill is developed in the history of a particular region or subject, the information will be far more specific. In essence, the smaller the focus of the skill, the greater the level of detail and accuracy. Developing skill in the history of the Kingdom of Harran, for instance, might provide information about the rulers and the great events in the kingdom's past; skill in the history of the Guild of Architects in the city of Jeppod would likely include all of the names of the guild's officers, the by-laws memorized by heart, etc. This skill encompasses military history as well.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Familiarity with an event within the area of study (e.g., a nation's birth, wars, etc.). <li>Easy: Familiarity with the most famous people involved in an event (e.g., kings, generals, etc.). <li>Light: Knowledge of the events that influenced and shaped an event (e.g., how a war started, major battles, etc.) <li>Medium: Insight into the interrelations between events (e.g., a depression influencing a leader's decision to declare war). <li>Hard: Knowledge of the minor characters'involvement in the event (e.g., aides, heroes, etc.). <li>Very Hard: Relating historical events to current affairs in order to gain insight into problem resolution or behavior prediction. <li>Extremely Hard: Knowledge of the details of an event (e.g., troop movements). <li>Sheer Folly: Accurately and concisely integrating all asÝpects of an event into a useful summary such that others can share the insight. <li>Absurd: Knowledge of the minutiae of an event (e.g., which individuals were where on a battlefield).
skills.notes: This skill provides characters with historical information. The GM may want to provide some information prior to play. This information is useful in understanding current affairs, identifying historical landmarks and points of interest, and successful time travel. In order to determine the difficulty of a History manoeuvre, the significance of the event in question must first be determined. A character with an equivalent knowledge level is familiar with the event. The amount of additional information the character is aware of depends on the manoeuvre attempted. For example, a character with knowledge level 4 is able to attempt a Medium manoeuvre about an event with significance 5 (e.g., a minor war), and can attempt a Light manoeuvre (difficulty 3) in order to determine the cause of the conflict.

skills.name: Horticulture
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for growing flowers, fruits, fungi and vegetables. It includes the feeding, care, and harvesting of such plants.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Growing plants that are native to the area and require no special attention (e.g., grass). <li>Easy: Growing wildflowers or fruit in a controlled manner. Such plants tend to overpower their competitors for nutrients and water (e.g., raspberries). <li>Light: Growing flowers that are native to the area that require some special attention (e.g., regular watering, fertilizing, etc.). <li>Medium: Growing a cash crop under normal conditions. This includes watering, fertilizing, weeding, and harvesting the crop. <li>Hard: Growing a magical herb in natural conditions. The herb must be native to the area. The yield of salable product is generally quite low. <li>Very Hard: Growing a plant from a different climate/ region in a controlled environment (e.g., a greenhouse). <li>Extremely Hard: Maintaining a garden that is always in bloom (by mixing plants of different subcategories whose reproductive cycles differ). Kings pay handsomely for such gardens. <li>Sheer Folly: Growing a magical herb under unnatural condition (e.g., indoors). <li>Absurd: Growing a plant that requires bizarre conditions. For example, a flower that requires nitrous oxide to mature.
skills.notes: This skill combines elements of gardening and farming. The character is able to maintain a garden or crop using this skill. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on the hardiness of the plant in the local climate. (Grass is a resilient plant, but not in a desert.) Plants that are not native to the area are more difficult to care for.

skills.name: Hunting
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to Hunting manoeuvres. Note that tracking and recognizing game is covered by other skills; this skill gives bonuses to the actual hunt, including setting up blind runs, leading and driving game, etc.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Finding game in a stocked preserve. <li>Easy: Finding game in an area where most of the natural predators have been killed. <li>Light: Finding game in a young forest. <li>Medium: Finding game in a mature forest; the lack of undergrowth limits the supply of food. <li>Hard: Finding game in a plains. <li>Very Hard: Finding game in an area that has been hunted heavily (or the game scared off by impending danger). <li>Extremely Hard: Finding game in a tundra or other sparsely populated region. <li>Sheer Folly: Finding game in a normal desert. <li>Absurd: Finding game in an especially arid desert.
skills.notes: This skill is used to find game and manoeuvre it into a position where it is within range of the hunter. This skill does not include bringing down the game, or trapping the game, merely identifying good hunting locations. If the manoeuvre roll is successful, the hunter has found game at long range (roughly 200-300'). Every 50' difference modifies the manoeuvre by one. Results above or below Success indicate more plentiful/larger or less plentiful/ smaller game. difficulty level (to a maximum of 2). The hunter can try once every strategic turn (4 hours). A successful manoeuvre indicates that the hunter has found enough game to feed 4 people (if he can kill it). Results above or below Success indicate more plentiful/larger or less plentiful/ smaller game. Modifiers: [Night: -20] [Day: 0] [Dusk/Dawn: +10]

skills.name: Hypnosis
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for placing a willing individual into a trance where they are responsive to suggestions. An unwilling individual receives a +50 RR bonus. Such an individual can be told to forget that they have been placed under hypnosis. He can be primed to perform some type of task which is triggered by a word, a gesture, a person, etc.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Inducing a hypnotic trance in a target that desires to be hypnotized. <li>Easy: Causing the target to perform a simple action (e.g., touch your nose). <li>Light: Inducing a hypnotic trance. <li>Medium: Accessing unconscious memories. Causing an individual to perform a complex action (e.g., pretend like you are driving a car, sing a song, etc.). <li>Hard: Causing the target to forget everything that transpired while in a trance. Forcing the target to tell the truth. <li>Very Hard: A post-hypnotic suggestion that involves a simple action. For example, the target will bark every time he hears the word, dog. <li>Extremely Hard: A post-hypnotic suggestion that involves a complex action (one that involves multiple actions). For example, traveling to a specific location. <li>Sheer Folly: A post-hypnotic suggestion that is dangerous or contrary to the target's beliefs (e.g., murder). <li>Absurd: A post-hypnotic suggestion involving bodily harm or death.
skills.notes: This skill is most useful on persons willing or desiring to enter a hypnotic state. The hypnotist must first induce a hypnotic state in the target. At this point the hypnotist is able to cause the individual to perform various actions or access unconscious memories. Post-hypnotic suggestions are the most difficult manoeuvres.

skills.name: Interrogation
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for extracting information from an intelligent source. This may or may not include causing discomfort to the target. However, if a target is discomforted and the Interrogation manoeuvre fails, the target may suffer a major injury or death. In such a case the target should roll a RR vs. a level 10 attack. If the target fails the RR, the GM must determine the extent of the damage?using the target's Co/SD/Co stat bonus as an indicator of how susceptible he is to injury.This skill not only applies to torture but also includes the ability to piece together scattered fragments of information received.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Gleaning relevant information from an articulate and cooperative subject. <li>Easy: Determining if the subject is deliberately withholding information. (This does not imply guilt, however.) <li>Light: Extracting useful information from an incoherent, but cooperative, subject. <li>Medium: Obtaining clues from an uncooperative subject. Such clues generally provide non-information (e.g., the murder weapon is not in the fireplace). <li>Hard: Piecing together information from a number of sources, none of whom are particularly observant. Most witnesses at a crime scene seem to fall into this category. The testimony is often contradictory or in-accurate. <li>Very Hard: Obtaining actual information from an uncooperative subject (e.g., the location of the murder weapon). <li>Extremely Hard: Obtaining clues from an intelligent subject that has a personal stake in the result of the interrogation (e.g., he is the murderer, the information will be used against his people, etc.). <li>Sheer Folly: Obtaining information from an intelligent subject that has a personal stake in the result of the interrogation. <li>Absurd: Obtaining anything from a fanatic. Note that very few people truly qualify. Most people will cave in when severely tortured.
skills.notes: Modifier [Causing discomfort:+10 to +25] The difficulty of an interrogation is dependent on the subject being interrogated. The interrogator will generally ask a series of questions, hoping to catch inconsistencies and implied information. This is useful for criminal investigations as well as more general information gathering. The interrogator must often extract the truth from an abundance of lies. It is not necessarily easy to get information from cooperative subjects. The subject may not be good at expressing himself; it is the interrogator's job to ask the proper questions. It is even more difficult to interrogate a subject who is attempting to cover up or who does not want the interrogator to learn the information.

skills.name: Jewelry-smithing
skills.description: Working with metals and pre-cut gems to produce jewelry.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Jousting
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for using complex lancing (mounted) manoeuvres, such as tilting, skewering rings in a tourney, etc.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Striking a straw man. <li>Easy: Striking an object the size of a large shield. <li>Light: Striking an object the size of a breast-plate. <li>Medium: Striking another rider. <li>Hard: Tossing one's lance to a squire and grabbing another. <li>Very Hard: Striking an object the size of a small helmet. <li>Extremely Hard: Retrieving a handkerchief or garter from the ground. <li>Sheer Folly: Striking an object smaller than an apple. <li>Absurd: Removing a (loose) ring from a finger.
skills.notes: This skill is used when outside of a combat situation. It can be used to unseat an opponent or perform jousting feats of agility. The difficulty of such manoeuvres depends on the size of the target and the speed of the mount. Each pace category above walk increases the difficulty by one. When attempting to unseat an opponent, each participant must make a Medium manoeuvre. If successful, the other must make a Very Hard Riding manoeuvre, or be thrown from the horse. Each pace category above run increases the difficulty of the Jousting manoeuvre by one, the difficulty of the Riding manoeuvre by one, and increases the damage taken from falling. (See Riding)

skills.name: Juggling
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for tossing objects up and manipulating them in such a manner as to keep them up in the air.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: 2 objects. <li>Easy: 3 objects. <li>Light: 4 objects. <li>Medium: 5 objects. <li>Hard: 6 objects. <li>Very Hard: 7 objects. <li>Extremely Hard: 8 objects. <li>Sheer Folly: 9 objects. <li>Absurd: 10 or more objects.
skills.notes: The difficulty of this manoeuvre is dependent entirely on the number of objects being juggled. Apart from entertainment, this skill is not particularly useful. Modifiers: [Irregularly shaped objects:-10] [Sharp objects:-20] [Different objects:-30] [Per pound over 1 lb:-5]

skills.name: Jumping
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for jumping, either from a running or a standing start. The base jump (running horizontal) for the average man of 5'10 is equal to 50 + (2 x St bonus in inches). For every 2 inches above or below this average height, add or subtract one from the base jump. The difficulties-summary listed below assume that the character is running at a dash at the time of takeoff. For every speed category (fast sprint/sprint/run/etc.) below the dash rate, raise the difficulty of the running jump by one (e.g., Hard becomes Very Hard, etc.). The base jump (standing horizontal) for the average man of 5'10? is equal to the base jump (running horizontal) divided by two. The base jump (running vertical) for the average man of 5'10? is equal to (12 + Strength Bonus) in inches. For every 3 inches above or below this average height, add or subtract one inch from the base jump. The optimal speed for a vertical jump with a running start is a run. The base jump (standing vertical) for the average man of 5'10 is equal to the base jump (running vertical) divided by three.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Base Jump x 1 <li>Easy: Base Jump x 1.5 <li>Light: Base Jump x 2 <li>Medium: Base Jump x 2.5 <li>Hard: Base Jump x 3 <li>Very Hard: Base Jump x 3.5 Ext. <li>Hard: Base Jump x 4 <li>Sheer Folly: Base Jump x 4.5 <li>Absurd: Base Jump x 5
skills.notes: Adding somersaults or flips increases the difficulty of the manoeuvre by one for every 180' of rotation.

skills.name: Languages
skills.description: Rolemaster is created for a world with a variety of cultures and languages. There is no such thing as a common tongue or an alignment tongue (though a GM can add them for his world system), although certain professions have developed their own languages for use in research. Each language must be developed individually, with the written and spoken versions of a language each counting separately. Skills in one language normally have little effect on others; however, 'brother languages,' those deriving from an immediate common ancestor, may be an exception. One's skill rank indicates the level of comprehension of a spoken or written language. One's skill bonus with a written form of language serves as a skill bonus to writing attempts using that language. The spoken skill bonus for a language is used to improve communication with someone. A successful static manoeuvre means that the spoken language rank of the person with whom you are communicating is temporarily increased for the purposes of this conversation, to a maximum of the rank developed by the individual performing the static manoeuvre. See the Mentalism Companion.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine:0 ranks. <li>Easy:1 rank. <li>Light:2 ranks. <li>Medium:3 ranks. <li>Hard:4 ranks. <li>Very Hard: 5 ranks. <li>Extremely Hard: 6 ranks. <li>Sheer Folly: 7-8 ranks. <li>Absurd: 9-10 ranks.
skills.notes: The difficulty of a language manoeuvre depends on how many ranks the character is trying to provide to the listener. If the listener has no ranks, this is automatically an Absurd manoeuvre.

skills.name: Leadership
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to inspire and command others to follow you, and to make others believe that you are competent to lead and that you know what you are doing. This includes the ability to raise the morale of those you command.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: 1-10 people. Marching an army. <li>Easy: 11-20 people. Maintaining a formation. <li>Light: 21-40 people. Manoeuvreing an army at a forced march. Attacking an equal or smaller force. <li>Medium: 41-80 people. Attacking a larger force. <li>Hard: 81-160 people. Maintaining morale after suffering 25% casualties. <li>Very Hard: 161-320 people. Maintaining morale after suffering 50% casualties. Maintaining formation while retreating. <li>Extremely Hard: 32 1-640 people. Maintaining morale while facing an opponent with Dragons, Demons, or other awesome creature. <li>Sheer Folly: 641-1500 people. Maintaining morale after suffering 75% casualties. <li>Absurd: 1501+ people. Maintaining morale after suffering 75% casualties from a Dragon, Demon, or other awesome creature.
skills.notes: Leadership is primarily used in two situations. A leader can attempt to recruit/attract an army. In this case, the leader must first raise a small army (Routine manoeuvre), and build from there. He can continue making Leadership manoeuvres to grow his army until he fails a manoeuvre roll, or until there are no more available recruits in the area. (Roughly 1% of a population can be recruited unless the leader is also a ruler. Rulers can recruit up to 10% of the population unless the safety of the nation is at stake.) Leadership is also used to maintain morale. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on the gravity of the situation. Even an excellent leader cannot prevent his troops from fleeing overwhelming odds (unless his troops are fanatics).

skills.name: Leather-crafts
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for working with hides and creating leather goods (e.g., leather armour, bolas, etc.).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Cutting a piece of leather into a simple shape. <li>Easy: Sewing an object that requires a single piece of leather (e.g., a pouch or hood). <li>Light: Dying a piece of leather. Tanning a hide into soft leather. <li>Medium: Sewing an object that requires only a few pieces of leather (e.g., a shoe or vest). <li>Hard: Boiling a hide to produce hard leather. Adding weaving to a simple garment. <li>Very Hard: Sewing an object that requires multiple pieces of leather (e.g., a full suit of armor or a saddle). <li>Extremely Hard: Sewing an object that incorporates hard and soft leather flawlessly (e.g., a breastplate and cape). Sheer Folly: Sewing an object that requires multiple pieces of leather that is waterproof (i.e., can be worn underwater). <li>Absurd: Incorporating leather with some magical substance (like laen). Note that an Alchemist would have to fashion the laen first.
skills.notes: The difficulty of leather-working depends on the number of pieces of leather involved, and the intricacy of the stitching or other work required. Like many crafts skills, this skill assumes that the craftsman has an adequate supply of tools. Without the necessary implements, there is little a craftsman can do. (Increase all manoeuvres by at least 3 difficulty levels.)

skills.name: Lie Perception
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for perceiving lies told by an individual under proximate observation (within 10' and within visual hearing range) by the user of this skill.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: The lie is outrageous. Medium: The lie is plausible. <li>Extremely Hard: The lie is more plausible than the truth.<li>Absurd: The character perceiving the lie has been magically charmed by the liar.
skills.notes: The difficulty of this manoeuvre is identical to the difficulty of the Actirig manoeuvre made to tell the lie convincingly. (For this reason, the difficulty of an Acting manoeuvre can be voluntarily increased.) Modifiers: [Cannot see target:-30] [Familiar with liar:+10] [Knows liar well:+30] [Unfamiliar with liar:-25] [Less than 5 ranks in language:-20] [No ranks in language:-40] [Cannot hear target:-50]

skills.name: Lip Reading
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for reading lips and sign language. Lip Reading is only possible with languages that the lip reader knows and then only to the known spoken skill rank. Special creatures (e.g., the Chicken People) might cause a penalty to be added to the character's bonus due to distinct lack of lips. Line of sight must be maintained with the subject's mouth. Skill is halved for reading the lips of creatures not of the same general type. subcategories could include human, reptile, avian, non-human mammalian, etc.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: The speaker is deliberately directing his words towards the lip reader. <li>Easy: The speaker is a trained actor enunciating perfectly. <li>Light: The speaker is speaking crisply or whispering. <li>Medium: Normal conversation. <li>Hard: The speaker stutters. <li>Very Hard: The speaker is mumbling. <li>Extremely Hard: The speaker's lips make meaningless Modifier motions when he is not speaking. <li>Sheer Folly: The speaker's lips rarely move (e.g., the speaker is under the influence of a narcotic). <li>Absurd: The speaker is throwing his voice.
skills.notes: This difficulty of a Lip Reading manoeuvre depends on the amount of lip movement the lip reader is able to observe. It is interesting to note that one must enunciate to be understood while whispering. Modifiers: [Each foot over 20':-2] [Using a telescope/binoculars:-10]

skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Locate Hidden
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for locating secret openings or hidden objects.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: The object is hidden behind camouflaged netting. The opening is huge (e.g., a barn door or palace gate). <li>Easy: The object was camouflaged only. The opening is large (e.g., double-doors). <li>Light: The object was hidden in an obvious place. The opening is the size of a normal door. <li>Medium: The object was hidden in a secret compartment. The opening is the size of a small door. <li>Hard: The object was camouflaged in its hiding place. The opening is half the size of a normal door. <li>Very Hard: The object was hidden in a well-designed hidden compartment (e.g., inside a padded box with a false bottom). The opening is large enough for a dog. <li>Extremely Hard: The object is in a hidden compartment and camouflaged. The opening is large enough for a cat. <li>Sheer Folly: The object is hidden within an object not normally capable of containing an object (e.g., a hollow loose stone). The opening is large enough for a mouse. <li>Absurd: The object is hidden in a location only accessible through special means (e.g., halfway up a narrow chimney). The opening is large enough for an insect.
skills.notes: Locate Hidden involves careful measurement, combined with an eye for detail. The character is looking for minor discrepancies that indicate that some opening or object has been hidden. If the concealer successfully camouflaged the object, only a Locate Hidden roll will detect it; casual observation will not detect the object. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on either the size of the opening or the level of concealment of the object. The level of concealment depends on how completely the object was hidden. Modifiers:[Searching for specific item:+10] [Has had location described in detail:+20]

skills.name: Locking Holds
skills.description: This skill provides an offensive bonus to render an opponent helpless with an immobilizing technique. This technique is usually only effective while the martial artist is applying constant force and pressure to maintain the locking hold. This skill uses the Arms Law Martial Arts Sweeps Attack table with the Locking Holds Critical Table substituted for the martial Arts Sweeps Critical Table. This skill may not exceed the Degree 1 damage threshold unless a Weapon Style skill of Martial Arts Style skill that allows the user to exceed this limitation accompanies it
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Lock Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recognizing and identifying major forms of locks and similar devices.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Identifying the type of lock (e.g., dead-bolt, sliding bolt, padlock, bar, etc.). <li>Easy: Identifying the type of key (i.e., the general shape). <li>Light: Identifying the strength of the lock. The character can estimate how difficult it would be to destroy the lock. <li>Medium: Designing a mold of the key (from a disassembled lock). Creating a key from this requires a manoeuvre with the appropriate Crafts skill. <li>Hard: Knowledge of the internal mechanics of the lock by observing its exterior. (This could be used to jam the lock as well as pick it.) <li>Very Hard: Designing a mold of the key (from an intact lock). <li>Extremely Hard:Knowledge of how long it would take to pick a given lock. <li>Sheer Folly: Knowledge of what triggers can be attached to a given type of lock. <li>Absurd: Identifying the designer ofthe lock.
skills.notes: This skill is used to identify a lock in order to determine the type of locking mechanism and type of key. Successful use of this skill to identify the internal mechanism (Hard) prior to picking a lock gives a bonus of +40 to the Lock Picking attempt. This skill is also used to determine the strength or other attributes of a lock. Note that the subsequent maneuver bonus should be doubled when using Lock Lore.

skills.name: Magical Language
skills.description: This skill enables characters to learn magical languages. These languages are acquired in the same fashion as are regular languages. These Languages are rarely spoken except in conjunction with spell casting, where they aid the spell's potency. This is the language of Power Words.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: + 1 to a BAR or +5 to an EAR. <li>Easy: Increasing a spell's effective level by 1 (for RRs, durations, etc.). <li>Light: +2 to a BAR or +10 to an EAR. <li>Medium: Increasing a spell's effective level by 2. <li>Hard: Modifying the target's RR by -10. <li>Very Hard: Increasing a spell's effective level by 3. +3 to a BAR or +15 to an EAR. <li>Extremely Hard: Modifying the target's RR by -20. <li>Sheer Folly: Increasing a spell's effective level by 5. <li>Absurd: Increasing a spell's effective level by 10.
skills.notes: Magical languages enable spell users to enhance the effects of their spells. The difficulty of such a maneuver depends on how powerful an effect the spell user desires to attain. Each magical language can affect a specific category of spell lists whose effects are similar (e.g., detection spells, scrying spells, movement spells, etc.). In addition to the suggestions below, there are two standard uses of magical languages that a GM can utilize: <li>Before making a spell casting static maneuver roll, the caster can make an appropriate Magical Languages maneuver. Any resulting subsequent maneuver modifier is applied to the following spell casting static maneuver (i.e., +10 for Near Success, +20 for Success, +30 for Absolute Success). <li>Modify a Spell Mastery maneuver by + 1 for each appropriate Magical Languages skill rank.

skills.name: Magic Ritual
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for enhancing a spell effect or duplicating a spell effect outside of normal spell resolution parameters (e.g., no power point expenditure). GM's are warned that this skill can be easily abused. GM's should understand how magic works in their world before implementing this skill. Magic rituals are not for hack-and-slash campaigns. Think of Celtic witches' incantations or Shamanistic dances and you have a good idea how this skill should work. (Other skills can complement this skill such as Herb Lore, Dancing, Demon/ Devil Lore, Poetry and Singing to make chants, etc.). Be imaginative. Be careful.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: (-20) or lower, 1 round. <li>Easy: (-19) - (-10):2 rounds. <li>Light: (-9) . (-5):3 rounds. <li>Medium: (-4) - 4:4 rounds. <li>Hard: 5-9: 1 minute. <li>Very Hard: 10-14: 5 minutes. <li>Extremely Hard: 15-20: 15 minutes. <li>Sheer Folly: 21-30: 30 minutes. <li>Absurd: 31 or more: 1 hour.
skills.notes: See the Essence Companion, Channeling Companion, Mentalism Companion, and Arcane Companion for more information on magic rituals. This skill can be used to cast ritual spells that do not require Power Points. Subtract the combined levels of the casters from the following sum: Level of the first spell + 2 x Level of the second spell + 3 x Level of the third spell, etc. Reference the result below. The time needed to cast the spell is also indicated. For example, 3 spell casters (all level 10) are attempting to cast a 5th, 10th and 25th level spell. The difference is (25+10x2+5x3-10x3) 30.This ritual would be a Sheer Folly manoeuvre and require 30 minutes to complete. Modifier [Spell user:+5] [Semi spell user:-10] [Non spell user:-25]

skills.name: Mapping
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to making, recognizing and using simple maps. This skill is not capable of producing fully detailed maps like those of a cartographer, but it is sufficient to the task of marking out one's journey well enough to find one's way home.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Maintaining a record of the directions turned. <li>Easy: Including crude distances (e.g., a dagger toss, javelin throw, or bow shot). <li>Light: Allowing for turns that are not at right angles. <li>Medium: Including approximate distances (e.g., 50 paces). <li>Hard: Noting subtle bends or slopes. <li>Very Hard: Including relatively accurate distances. <li>Extremely Hard: Mapping a building with half floors or sub-levels that create the illusion of overlapping rooms. <li>Sheer Folly: Determining the location of secret rooms or openings by noting subtle discrepancies. <li>Absurd: Copying the GM's map.
skills.notes: Mapping allows a character to maintain a crude map. The difficulty of this manoeuvre is dependent on the amount of detail the player wants the GM to provide. More accurate maps require the Cartography skill.

skills.name: Martial Arts Blind Fighting
skills.description: This skill trains the practitioner to use senses other than sight during combat. Normally a character will have at least a -100 modifier to his OB if he is fighting an opponent he cannot see. A successful Blind Fighting static manoeuvre can be used to offset the OB penalty for not being able to see one's opponent. To determine the effect of such an attempt, roll (open-ended) and add the Blind Fighting skill bonus. Then refer to the Movement Manoeuvre Table using the Extremely Hard column. If the result is a number, that number is used to offset the current penalty for vision.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: Successful use of this skill will never increase the wielder's OB, it can only offset penalties due to not being able to see ones opponent. A failure result when attempting this skill will result in the character not being able to take any action this round An extraordinary success when attempting this skill will allow the character to completely offset the penalty for not being able to see his opponent.

skills.name: Martial Arts Striking
skills.description: This skill represents the attacking forms of the hard martial arts. This skill uses the Arms Law Martial Arts Strikes Attack Tables and may not exceed Degree 1 damage threshold. Accompanied by a Weapon Style skill or Martial Arts Style skill, this skill can exceed the Degree 1 limitation. All criticals should be rolled on the Martial Arts Strikes Critical Table
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Martial Arts Style (Advanced)
skills.description: This skill allows the wielder to become more skilled in combat with his chosen weapon. The Advanced Weapon Style skill incorporates the most difficult combat techniques.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: The Advanced Weapon Style skill bonus represents the offensive bonus of the character while using his weapon in the manner prescribed by the weapon style. Each weapon style must be developed separately. Refer to Section 8.0 for more on weapon styles

skills.name: Martial Arts Style (Basic)
skills.description: This skill allows the wielder to become more proficient at fighting with his chosen weapon. The Basic Weapon Style skill incorporates very effective combat techniques.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: The Basic Weapon Style skill bonus represents the offensive bonus of the charac- Part II Section 7.2 Combat Maneuvers ter while using his weapon in the manner prescribed by the weapon style. Each weapon style must be developed separately. Refer to Section 8.0 for more on weapon styles.

skills.name: Martial Arts Style Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recognizing a particular martial arts style. This skill allows the user to anticipate the most common subcategories of attacks of a martial arts style, as well as recognize the respected masters of martial arts styles. Successful lore static manoeuvres may allow the user to anticipate attacks f a person using a martial art style. A successful Martial Arts Style Lore static manoeuvre will give the character a special +2 bonus to his initiative roll for the duration of the combat providing the opponent continues to use the same martial arts style.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: This skill requires 25% activity action in the round that it is attempted. Obscure, secret or forgotten martial arts styles will impose a negative modifier on the use of this skill

skills.name: Martial Arts Sweeping
skills.description: This skill represents the attacking forms of the soft martial arts. This skill uses the Martial Arts Sweeps Attack Table and may not exceed the Degree 1 damage threshold unless accompanied by a Weapon Style skill of Martial Arts Skill. All criticals should be rolled on the Martial Arts Sweeps Critical Table
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Mechanition
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for building and using a machine that already exists. It will be necessary to have the appropriate skills to build the machine. Each type of machine must be learned as a separate skill.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: A simple machine (e.g., lever, pulley, etc.). Medium: A compound machine. (e.g., a telescope, elevator, etc.). <li>Extremely Hard: An intricate machine (e.g., a computer, laser, etc.). Absurd: An alien device.
skills.notes: A successful Machination manoeuvre indicates that the character has built an effective machine. Partial Success indicate that the machine has various flaws or quirks. A vehicle might pull in a specific direction; the roof of a covered battering ram might leak; etc. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on the complexity of the machine being created. This presupposes that the necessary materials are available and that the character has the necessary Crafts skills. Note that this skill implements the designs created by an Engineering or Gimmickry manoeuvre.

skills.name: Meditation
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for an individual entering, leaving, and exploiting a mental trance which the individual can use to help solve problems, increase his chance to successfully cast a spell, aiding in Attunement manoeuvres, etc. (subject to GM stipulation). Physical prodding allows one to make a static manoeuvre to leave the trance, as does a painful strike (modify by +25).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: An isolated and sound-proof room. <li>Easy: A quiet room in which all of the occupants are sleeping. <li>Light: A still setting with some noise, but no activity (e.g., in a peaceful glen). <li>Medium: A relatively sedate setting in which there is some activity, but it is muffled. <li>Hard: While in a room where two people are having a conversation. <li>Very Hard: An active setting in which there is a great deal of movement. <li>Extremely Hard: In a noisy or disruptive environment (e.g., during an argument). <li>Sheer Folly: In an extremely noisy or distracting environment (e.g., while being bombed or shot at). <li>Absurd: While in melee.
skills.notes: This skill is normally used to gain the subsequent manoeuvre bonus since there are many skills that can logically be aided by meditating. The difficulty of the meditation depends on the environment in which the meditation is being attempted. Modifier: [Elves:+25] [calm and sedate settings, etc:+30] [on-going battle & melee combat, etc:-70] [6-12 rounds (?1-2 minutes) spent in meditation:-30] [13-29 rounds (?2-5 minutes) spent in meditation:-10] [30-59 rounds (?5-10 minutes) spent in meditation:+0] [60-89 rounds (?10-15 minutes) spent in meditation:+5] [90-119 rounds (?15-20 minutes) spent in meditation:+10] [120-149 rounds (?20-25 minutes) spent in meditation:+15] [150-179 rounds (?30-35 minutes) spent in meditation:+20] [180+ rounds (?35+ minutes) spent in meditation:+25]

skills.name: Mental Control (Assault)
skills.description: A character's ability to focus his mind to the task of overcoming another mind is represented by this skill. If a successful static manoeuvre is made (modified by this skill), the character may add his number of ranks in this skill to any BAR for spells of a sub-type of 'm'. This skill should normally be classified as Restricted. However any Semi-spell user or Hybrid spell user with Mentalism as a realm may classify this skill as Normal. Pure spell users in the realm of Mentalism may classify this skill as Everyman.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: See Mentalism Companion 7.2

skills.name: Mental Control (Defense)
skills.description: Development of skill ranks in mental defense indicate an extra hardening of the mind's natural defences by the character. This skill is simply added to any RR made against spells with a sub-type of 'm' (no manoeuvre is required).This skill should normally be classified as Restricted. However any Semi-spell user or Hybrid spell user with Mentalism as a realm may classify this skill as Normal. Pure spell users in the realm of Mentalism may classify this skill as Everyman.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: See Mentalism Companion 7.2

skills.name: Metal-crafts
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for working with normal metals to create or repair desired objects (e.g., horse shoes, metal ornaments). Bonus for oven or kiln building, and doubling effects of fires.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Making a crude object (e.g., a nail or spike). <li>Easy: Making an object that requires bending a single piece of metal (e.g.,a horseshoe or ring). <li>Light: Designing a crude weapon (e.g., a simple Roman or Viking sword). Medium Smelting a metal. Producinga simple cast (required for many items). <li>Hard: Designing an average weapon or shield. Incorporating ornamentation. <li>Very Hard: Making an object that requires multiple pieces of metal and very careful precision (e.g., a suit of plate armour, a clock). <li>Extremely Hard: Designing an exquisite weapon (e.g., a katana or ornate rapier). <li>Sheer Folly: Designing a miniature object (e.g., a watch, armour for a fairy, etc.). <li>Absurd: Making an object whose technology is well beyond the current level.
