The craftsman must have access to the appropriate design skills (e.g., Gimmickry).
skills.notes: The difficulty of metalworking depends on the intricacy of the final product. Even a large, bulky product might require very detailed workmanship in order to function properly (e.g., a clock). Like many crafts skills, this skill assumes that the craftsman has an adequate supply of tools. Without the necessary implements, there is little a craftsman can do. (Increase all manoeuvres by at least 3 difficulty levels)

skills.name: Metal Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recognizing and identifying metals, alloys, metallic crystal structures, etc. Also will give information on famous, magical, historic, legendary, or cursed subcategories of metals. Skill must be developed separately for each culture or region as applicable to the GM's world scheme.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Identifying a metal. <li>Easy: Identifying a precious metal. (Silver, electrum and platinum are all very similar.) <li>Light: Identifying an alloy. <li>Hard: Determining the relative strength of an alloy. <li>Very Hard: Determining if a metal has any flaws (e.g., stress fractures, impurities, air bubbles, etc.). <li>Extremely Hard: Identifying an alloy that includes foreign metals. <li>Sheer Folly: Knowledge of any magical or supernatural properties inherent in a metal. <li>Absurd: Precise information about every known use for a metal.
skills.notes: The skill provides the character and player with knowledge about the metals found in a specific region. Unlike many Lore skills, the GM will probably not be able to provide the player with information prior to play. The rarity of a given metal must first be determined. Common metals (like iron) probably have a rarity of 1. Precious metals and alloys have a higher rarity rating, and magical and enchanted metals, the highest rarity rating. See ScHK Section 5.8 for more information about Lore manoeuvres.

skills.name: Midwifery
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for delivery and care of babies.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: See Healing, Section 4.0.

skills.name: Military Organization
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for organization of a military force, not the actual deployment into battle (which is Tactics). Includes knowledge of how to billet and supply a unit, posting of watch, running of patrols, etc.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: 1-5 people. <li>Easy: 6-10 people. <li>Light: 11-20 people. <li>Medium: 2140 people. <li>Hard: 41-80 people. <li>Very Hard: 81-160 people. <li>Extremely Hard: 161-320 people. <li>Sheer Folly: 32 1-640 people. <li>Absurd: 641+ people.
skills.notes: Military Organization is used in the day-today maintenance of a military force. Without sufficient military organization, a unit slowly degrades into chaos. A successful manoeuvre is required each month in order to maintain a unit. If the manoeuvre fails, the unit's morale and offensive bonus will begin to deteriorate. The difficulty of maintaining a force depends on the size of the unit. It is common practice to generate multiple command layers such that each leader is responsible for a smaller number of units.

skills.name: Mimery
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for conveying concepts or information without verbal communication or a codified sign language. This skill is useful when trying to span a language barrier, entertain others, etc. Also used when trying to imitate a particular action (i.e., a movement not requiring a manoeuvre).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Any stock routine (e.g., walking into the wind, trapped in a box, etc.). <li>Easy: Conveying a simple idea (e.g., riding a horse, fighting, etc.). <li>Light: Conveying specific information (e.g., a color, name, etc.). Think charades. Medium.- Communicating with the equivalent of 2 ranks of language. <li>Hard: Conveying a complex idea (e.g., an interaction, a battle plan). <li>Very Hard: Communicating with the equivalent of 3 ranks of language. <li>Extremely Hard: Conveying a theoretical idea (e.g., knowledge, philosophy). <li>Sheer Folly: Communicating with the equivalent of 4 ranks of language. <li>Absurd: Communicating with the equivalent of 5 ranks of language.
skills.notes: Mimery is often used for entertainment purposes. It can also be used to communicate with people with whom a character has no language in common. The difficulty of either manoeuvre depends on the complexity of the information being conveyed. In general, the manoeuvre will automatically fail if the audience is not familiar with the information.

skills.name: Mimicry
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for imitating sounds. This skill is useful when trying to imitate individuals, animals or even inanimate sounds (e.g., wind, stairs creaking, etc.).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Whistling. <li>Easy: Simple sounds (one note/tone). <li>Light: Animal sounds (e.g., a bear or dog). <li>Medium: Multi-tone sounds (birds trilling, etc.). <li>Hard: Very complex (comprehensive words). <li>Very Hard: Imitate another's vocal patterns. <li>Extremely Hard: Simple inanimate sounds. Multi-sided conversations. <li>Sheer Folly: Complex inanimate sounds. <li>Absurd: Alien sounds. Convincing a target that is intimately familiar with the vocal pattern.
skills.notes: The difficulty of a Mimicry manoeuvre depends on how easily a human voice can imitate the sound. The familiarity the audience has with the sound also modifies the difficulty. It is easier to convince a general audience that you sound like the king; it is much more difficult to convince the queen.

skills.name: Mingling
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to attempts to mix easily with a large urban population, whether for the purposes of remaining unnoticed, escaping pursuers, or simply moving easily through a crowd.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Disappearing in an immense crowd when the pursuit is well behind the character. <li>Easy: Moving through a large crows easily. <li>Light: interacting and blending with a mixed group of people. <li>Medium: Disappearing in a huge crowd when the pursuit is close behind <li>Hard: Interacting and blending with a specific group of people (e.g., sailors) <li>Very Hard: disappearing in a large crowd when the pursuit is close behind <li>Extremely Hard: Interacting and blending with a group that had obvious differences from the character. For example a fighter blending with a group of docters <li>Sheer Folly: Disappearing in a small crowd when the pursuit is close behind <li>Absurd: Interacting and blending with a group of a different race.
skills.notes: This skill allows characters to disappear into a crowd. This is particularly useful when evading authorities. A character can also use this skill to blend in with a mixed group. The people present will not consider the character's presence unusual.

skills.name: Mining
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for assessing the possibilities of mining in an area, and supervising the creation and running of the mine. Each type of mining process must be learned as a separate skill.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Extracting ore from a known vein. <li>Easy: Estimiating the amount of ore in a vein <li>Light: Organizing an open-pit/quarry mining operation <li>Medium: Identifying good locations for a mine in a mountain setting <li>Hard: Organizing a tunneling operation. Predicting the saftey of a mine <li>Very Hard: Identifying mine locations in a plains or deserts <li>Extremely Hard: Finding a good panning site <li>Sheer Folly: Identifying mine locations in a forest, jungle or swamp <li>Absurd: Finding mineral deposits in an extremely unfamiliar location (e.g., underwater or on the moon)
skills.notes: The skill is used to find good mining locations and extracting as much ore from the location as possible. The actual extraction of minerals generally assumes a large group of workers (miners). A miner can also use this skill for individual mining (e.g., panning), but the yield will be significantly less.

skills.name: Missile Deflecting
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for using the body or a weapon or a shield to deflect or even catch a thrown weapon or missile directed at the user.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Extremely Hard: thrown weapons<li>Sheer Folly: missile weapons.
skills.notes: To determine the effect of such an attempt, roll (open-ended) and add the Missile Deflecting skill bonus. Then refer to the Maneuver/Movement Table (T-4.1). If the result is a number, it is subtracted from the weapon's attack roll (in addition to the normal DB). If the missile or thrown object misses, the character has a chance of catching the item. Roll d100 (open-ended) and add the modification received earlier from the Movement/Maneuver Table; if the result is over 100, the item has been caught; if desired. The Missile Deflecting skill requires a 100% activity action. The roll is modified by -20 for each additional missile that the character wishes to try to deflect that round. Resolve each missile attack separately.

skills.name: Mnemonics
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recalling information through the use of memory aids, techniques and tricks.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: A short list (up to 10 items). <li>Easy: A short message or note. <li>Light: A moderately long list (up to 100 items). <li>Medium: A detailed message, up to letter length. <li>Hard: A long list (up to 1000 items). <li>Very Hard: A table of complex information (e.g., all of a country's rulers, their birth dates, age of coronation, etc.). <li>Extremely Hard: An epic length poem (whose rhyming pattern aids rote memorization). <li>Sheer Folly: An entire novel. <li>Absurd: The complete works of a prolific author.
skills.notes: This skill is used to memorize data. Memorizing data is not synonymous with knowledge. Mnemonics is used to memorize data of little relevance. Couriers and pages use this skill to remember messages. Characters may use this skill to memorize the words of an oracle until their meaning becomes obvious. The difficulty of the skill depends on the amount of information and the impact it has on the character. Modifiers: [Per week in the past:-5] [Carefully committed to memory:+30] [Impact on PC:-10 to +30]

skills.name: Mounted Combat
skills.description: This skill limits ones OB against an opponent while mounted. The OB of an attack made while mounted cannot exceed the attackers Mounted Combat skill bonus. A characters Mounted Combat skill cannot have more skill ranks developed than his Riding skill ranks.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Accelerating one pace category (e.g., from walk to jog). <li>Easy: Maintaining a walk. Decelerating two pace categories. <li>Light: Maintaining a jog. Making a 45? turn. <li>Medium: Maintaining a run. Making a 90? turn. Decelerating three pace categories. <li>Hard: Maintaining a sprint. Making a 135? turn. <li>Very Hard: Maintaining a fast sprint. Decelerating four pace categories. <li>Extremely Hard: Making a 180? turn. <li>Sheer Folly: Maintaining a dash. Decelerating five pace categories. <li>Absurd: Decelerating six pace categories.
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Music
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to writing, recognising or performing a piece of music. This skill may be used to determine the ability of the individual to play in concert with others, or to direct others in doing so. A successful manoeuvre roll by a conductor will give those he is conducting a bonus of +20 to their own use of this skill
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: A scale. <li>Easy: A simple melody or air. A jingle or ditty. <li>Light: A piece with limited appeal. Music with technical flair, but no emotion. <li>Medium: A good piece of music. Consistent work of this quality may earn the composer a sponsor. <li>Hard: A piece that appeals to those who enjoy the particular style. Catchy tunes like dances, arias, and concertos that portray a single emotion or idea. <li>Very Hard: A work with broad appeal. Complete works (nocturnes, improvisations, consolations, etc.) that tell a story, or convey a complex emotion. <li>Extremely Hard: A work that will be considered great many years from now. Masterpieces like operas, symphonies, etc. that capture a range of emotions. <li>Sheer Folly: A work that creates a new style of composition. <li>Absurd: A work that gains immediate recognition world-wide.
skills.notes: This skill can be used either to reproduce a piece of music (conducting) or to create a piece of music (composition). The difficulty of a Music (performance) manoeuvre depends on the greatness of the composition. A Music (performance) manoeuvre is equal to the difficulty of writing the work. A Music (composition) manoeuvre depends on the impact the piece is intended to have. Each Partial Success reduces the resulting fame by 20%, each Near Success, by 10%. An Absolute Success increases the fame by 20%. (See Section 5.1). This skill must be developed separately for each style of music to be learned. Examples include classical, baroque, romantic, jazz, rock, etc. Modifiers: [2-4 people:-5] [5-10 people:-10 ] [-20 people:-15] [21+ people:-20]

skills.name: Navigation
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for determining proper directions and distances when using a map in conjunction with various directional aids, such as a compass, sextant, clock, etc. This includes a concept of orienting, and is applicable on land, water or the stars. Note that this skill is far more precise and complex than Orienteering.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: While at a landmark whose location is clearly noted on a map (e.g., a port, city, etc.). <li>Easy: While in possession of all possible navigational tools and a map. <li>Light: At night.<li>Medium: On a clear day. <li>Hard: Following a storm. <li>Very Hard: While overcast. <li>Extremely Hard: Following a gale that pushed the ship far off course. <li>Sheer Folly: Without a map or compass. <li>Absurd: After being teleported.
skills.notes: This skill is used to prevent a character from getting lost while traveling. Use of this skill allows a character to travel from point A to point B without getting lost. The character must have the necessary equipment and maps (including at least a compass). As long as this skill is successful, a character will not get lost. (A manoeuvre should be made each day of travel.) Modifier [Light fog:-5] [Dense fog:-15]

skills.name: Nerve Strikes
skills.description: This skill provides an offensive bonus to strike an opponent precisely at a vulnerable nerve cluster. Depending on the resolution of the attack, the opponent can be put in extreme pain, temporary paralyszed, or even killed. This skill uses the Arms Law Martial Arts Strikes Attack Table with the Nerve Strikes Critical Table.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: This skill may not exceed the Degree 1 damage threshold unless a weapon style skill of a Martial Arts Style skill that allows the user to exceed this limitation accompanies it.

skills.name: Observation
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for noticing details about the environment for assimilation and analysis. This is normally only usable in an active fashion, and requires concentration. Note that this skill is different from Alertness, which represents a general and unconscious level of receptivity and awareness of events and details within one's immediate environment. This skill reflects the active observation, noting and appraisal of such details. For example, if a character were about to make camp in an unsafe location, the GM might make an Alertness manoeuvre for that character to determine whether or not he notices the danger. If the character indicated that he wished to examine the locatiOn for suitability, the character would instead make an Observation manoeuvre.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: The character knows exactly what he is looking for and is merely trying to verify some detail. For example, T'mar knows that the king has a mole on his right hand. While shaking the king's hand, he checks to make sure that this really is the king. <li>Easy: The information being sought is obvious provided any time is spent looking (e.g., noticing an object that has been hastily camouflaged). <li>Light: The character has excellent knowledge about some object (person, creature, etc.) and is looking for details in order to distinguish between two similar objects. <li>Medium: The information being sought by the character is general in nature (e.g., Are there any signs of recent habitation in the cottage?). <li>Hard: The character's knowledge of the subject is fair and he has some idea of what he is looking for. For example, a weapons master is attempting to assess his opponent's skill by watching him practice. <li>Very Hard: The information being sought is specific in nature. For example, there is debris everywhere, and a character is interested in determining if the door was ripped off its hinges or battered down. <li>Extremely Hard: The character's knowledge of the object is poor, and the character is not certain what he is looking for. (But he'll recognize it when he sees it!) <li>Sheer Folly: The information is trivial in nature, and not at all obvious. For example, determining if a vial ever held olive oil. <li>Absurd: The character has no knowledge about the subject of inquiry. The player is merely hoping to roll well enough to get some insight from the GM.
skills.notes: This skill has numerous applications. It is used to find people hiding in the brush. It is used to examine an object closely, looking for any anomalies. It is used to determine the number of enemies in the opposing army. As a result, it is not possible to describe even a fraction of the situations in which Observation could be used. Instead, broad general guidelines are provided. The level of difficulty should be based on the amount of information the character is seeking. The obviousness of the information can modify this difficulty by up to two levels. For example, determining the safety of the aforementioned campsite might be a Medium manoeuvre. However, the presence of a Troll's burrow nearby might be a subtle clue to look elsewhere for a campsite. This skill can be used to discover persons who are Stalking or Hiding. It can also be used to see through a disguise, notice a camouflaged object or realize that a voice is being mimicked. It cannot be used to find hidden objects, which requires the skill Locate Hidden.

skills.name: Operating Equipment
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to operate simple equipment, or specific set of complex equipment, such as miliworks, automatic looms, etc.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Only a technophobe would have difficulty operating the equipment (e.g., a padlock, a child-proof cap, etc.). Medium: Most complex machines (e.g., a loom, a bottle corker, etc.). <li>Extremely Hard: Very complicated and touchy machines (e.g., a human-powered ornithopter). Absurd: Alien machinery.
skills.notes: This simple skill is necessary to use any tool with more than a few moving parts. No skill is necessary to dig a hole with a shovel. Digging a hole with a post-hole digger is another story. The difficulty of the manoeuvre is based on the number of things that could go wrong. If the tool is being used for something other than its intended purpose, add three to the difficulty level. This skill does not necessarily provide any knowledge of how the device works, nor any knowledge of how to fix the device.

skills.name: Orienteering
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for using landmarks, the sun, stars and other simple navigational tricks in order to arrive at a desired location. Note that Orienteering provides only a general sense of the proper direction towards a location; hazards, obstacles, or distances are not learned. It is not capable of the sort of precise results that Navigation will provide, but it is sufficient to make one's way across the countryside.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Traveling through very familiar territory. <li>Easy: Traveling with excellent directions. <li>Light: On a clear day in open terrain. <li>Medium: On a clear day in a light forest. On a cloudy day in open terrain. <li>Hard: On a clear day in a heavy forest. On a cloudy day in a light forest. <li>Very Hard: On a moonlit night. On a cloudy day in a heavy forest. <li>Extremely Hard: In a dense jungle with multiple canopies. <li>Sheer Folly: On an overcast or moonless night. <li>Absurd: In complete darkness (e.g., during a storm on a moonless night).
skills.notes: Without this skill, a character is guaranteed to get lost if not following a road or river. Additional ranks will help a character avoid getting lost in heavy terrain or cloudy weather. A manoeuvre roll should be made every strategic turn (4 hours). Failure generally indicates that the character heads in a direction up to 600 degrees from the direction intended. Modifiers: [Light fog:-15] [Dense fog:45]

skills.name: Painting
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for creating graphic images. This may be on a flat medium such as sketching or painting with pigments, or painting on an object of some kind. Any activity that involves the creation of an image or deliberate design may benefit from this skill.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: A symbolic sketch using stock symbols (e.g., stick figures). Many cave paintings are of this quality. <li>Easy: A basic sketch that is recognizable as a poor representation of a specific location or person. <li>Light: A simple, elegant sketch that captures the essence of a location, item, or person. Many artists begin with such a sketch. <li>Medium: A simple painting, devoid of character or life, that accurately depicts its subject. <li>Hard: A detailed portrait that portrays every nuance of the subject in stark clarity. <li>Very Hard: An elegant painting that captures the spirit or essence of the moment. Persons viewing the work feel drawn into the painting. <li>Extremely Hard: A magnificent work that completely captures the painter's reaction to the subject in subtle ways without sacrificing the mood of the painting. <li>Sheer Folly: Designing a piece that inspires a new style. Such a work is refreshing in its approach to the subject. <li>Absurd: A masterpiece that inspires fear or awe, depending on the subject matter.
skills.notes: The goal of the painter is a representation of a real object, scene or person. This representation may be realistic, symbolic or emotive. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on the beauty and depth of expression of the piece of art to be produced. At the most basic level, a painter can produce sketches, or stylized images. As he gains in ability, he is able to infuse his works with a unique perspective or insight. The perceived greatness of the work depends to a large extent on the audience. For a painter to make a living, it helps to market one's skill well. Modifiers: [Unfamiliar medium:-30] [From posed image or person:+10] [From memory:-30 (+ Memory stat bonus x 3)]

skills.name: Paper-making
skills.description: Creation of various forms of thin writing material such as paper and papyrus.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Philosophy
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recognizing and identifying major aspects of philosophic doctrines. Each philosophy doctrine may be concentrated in and learned separately for in-depth knowledge and understanding.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Reciting the major tenets of a doctrine. <li>Easy: Memorizing examples that demonstrate the major tenets. <li>Light: Applying a philosophical belief to a simple situation (i.e., one in which there is an obvious correct answer). For example, demonstrating that it is wrong to cheat on a test. <li>Medium: Knowledge of more subtle facets of a philosophy. This includes a critical analysis of its weaknesses. <li>Hard: Applying a philosophical belief to a complex situation (i.e., one in which multiple parties have valid cases). <li>Very Hard: Familiarity with classic examples of conundrums that have been solved. (Is it wrong to tell a murderer that the person he is hunting is not in your house to protect the potential victim, even though you are lying?) <li>Extremely Hard: Resolving an untenable position. For example, finding a resolution (from a situational view) to a set of circumstances in which no alternative maximizes the outcome. <li>Sheer Folly: Producing a new school of philosophical thought that resolves one or more dilemmas. (New dilemmas will inevitably arise.) <li>Absurd: Demonstrating that all possible situations have been addressed, without contradiction.
skills.notes: Philosophy is the study branches of philosophy, all of thought. There are many of which strive for enlighten-ment and truth through the application of logic. (Even though logic itself is a philsophical field.) At the core of most doctrines is the search for morality, that which should be done for its own sake. The difficulty of a Philosophy manoeuvre depends on the amount of logic and faith to be applied to a given situation. Memorizing the tenets of a philosophy is much easier than applying those maxims accurately. Note that different philosophies will find different situations difficult. Most schools of philosophy fall into three major categories: Rule-based. Philosophy is the application of universal rules (or imperatives) to all situations; Situational. The proper course of action depends on the actual circumstances and the persons involved; Existential. Each person defines his own reality. Truth can only be perceived, and only applies to the person perceiving.

skills.name: Picking Locks
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for locking and unlocking locks and similar devices.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Picker has the key (and can therefore see the cut). <li>Easy: Picker can see the locking mechanism. <li>Light: Keyhole larger than a finger. Handcuffs or shackles. <li>Medium: Keyhole larger than a pencil (most medieval locks). Car door. <li>Hard:Padlock. <li>Very Hard: Sliding bolt. <li>Extremely Hard: Modern dead-bolt or combination lock. Multiple keys must be turned simultaneously. <li>Sheer Folly: Door is barred, not locked. <li>Absurd: Electronic lock.
skills.notes: The difficulty of this manoeuvre depends on the complexity of the lock. In general, smaller locks are more difficult to pick. Note that in a medieval setting, there are no locks that are Sheer Folly or Absurd. Modifiers: [Successful (Hard+) Lock Lore prior to attempt:+40] [Each time lock has been unsuccessfully attempted:-30] [Have picked lock before:+50] [Picker has picked this type of lock before:+25] [Picker has description of mechanism:+10]

skills.name: Picking Pockets
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for picking pockets. If successful, the contents are lifted and the skill bonus is applied against the victim's Alertness.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: The target is asleep. <li>Easy: The target is drunk. <li>Light: The pouch (or pocket) is outside of armour. <li>Medium: The pouch is outside of clothing. <li>Hard: The pocket is internal, but the item being stolen is (relatively) large, like a wallet. <li>Very Hard: Deep pockets and/or small items. <li>Extremely Hard: The pouch is worn below armour. <li>Sheer Folly: Removing rings from fingers. <li>Absurd: Stealing a weapon from a scabbard.
skills.notes: The difficulty of a Picking Pockets manoeuvre depends on how accessible the victim's pockets are. (Note that pockets are a fairly recent invention.) Money carried in a pouch is the easiest to gain access to. If the character must come into contact with the victim, the manoeuvre is much more difficult. There are many items which aid in Picking Pockets. Examples include palm knives (for slitting pouches), hollow canes, fake blindfolds, etc.

skills.name: Planar Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recognizing and navigating other planes of existence; it also provides knowledge about other planes.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Belief that other planes of existence are real. <li>Easy: Knowledge that other planes of existence are real. <li>Light: Knowledge of an adjacent plane (e.g., the ethereal). In most cases, this allows the character to identify the plane, how it relates to his plane, and basic survival techniques. <li>Medium: Identifying ways of entering and exiting an adjacent plane. <li>Hard: Knowledge of a plane two realms removed (i.e., the plane borders on the ethereal, but not this reality). <li>Very Hard: Identifying ways of entering and exiting a plane two realms removed. <li>Extremely Hard: Knowledge of a plane more than two realms removed. <li>Sheer Folly: Identifying planes that exist beyond reality (e.g., the home of the Chaos Demons). This knowledge invariably leads to insanity. <li>Absurd: Knowledge of havens in insanely dangerous planes of existence (e.g., hell).
skills.notes: This skill provides characters with knowledge about other planes of existence. The GM should discuss the extent of the character's knowledge with the player before play. The skill offers an understanding of how the planes of existence connect, how to travel from one to another, and how to survive on a plane whose environment is hostile or alien. During play, a character may use this skill to identify the quickest way home (if one exists), determine where a gate most likely leads, or recognize a multi-dimensional item. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on the proximity of the plane to the character's own.

skills.name: Plate Armour
skills.description: Each armour type has a Moving Manoeuvre Penalty (MMP) associated with it for untrained individuals. This penalty modifies Moving Manoeuvre rolls. The different armour subcategories are divided into five groups based upon the composition of the armour: type 1-4 = No Armor; subcategories 5-8 = Soft Leather; subcategories 9-12 = Rigid Leather; subcategories 13-16 = Chain; and subcategories 17-20 = Plate. There are no Moving Manoeuvre Penalties associated with No Armor, and therefore there is no need to apply skill ranks towards it. The Soft and Rigid Leather skills are both found in the Light Armor Skill Category; Chain is found in the Medium Armor Skill Category; Plate is found in the Heavy Armor Skill Category. Every encumbering armour has a minimum manoeuvre penalty associated with it. The skill bonus for manoeuvreing for a group of armour subcategories reduces the maximum penalty for manoeuvreing until the minimum manoeuvre penalty is reached. This limit represents the fact that weight and constriction of the armour will always hinder the character to some extent. These minimums may vary for certain superior or magical suits of armour. In addition, each armour type has a Quickness penalty associated with it. An Armor Quickness penalty can reduce or cancel a combatant's Quickness stat bonus for his DB (see RMFRP p. 33). It will not reduce a combatant's overall DB below the level that it would be at with a zero Quickness stat bonus.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Careful drop. <li>Easy: Standing while in AT 1-6 or 9. <li>Light: Rapid drop. Standing while in AT 10 or 13. <li>Medium: Standing while in AT 7, 14, or 17.<li>Hard: Standing while in AT 8, 11, or 12. <li>Very Hard: Standing while in AT 15, 16 or 18. <li>Extremely Hard: Standing while in AT 19. <li>Sheer Folly: Standing while in AT 20. <li>Absurd: Diving for cover.
skills.notes: The GM may require the character to make manoeuvre rolls for various activities in combat. The most common examples are standing up and dropping to the ground. It should be difficult to injure oneself by standing. It merely takes time. Conversely, a drop or dive is always successful, but the character may be injured in the process (+0 Fall).

skills.name: Play Instrument
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for using a specific instrument, such as flute, drum, lute, etc. It may also be used to recognize musical patterns or rhythms, notes, etc. Note that separate development is required for skill with each instrument.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: A scale. <li>Easy: Improvising off of a simple melody. <li>Light: Improvising from a common major chord progression. <li>Medium: Improvising off of a common melody. <li>Hard: Improvising from a known chord progression (e.g., minor, blues, etc.)<li>Very Hard: Improvising off of a melody just heard (used in dueling instruments).<li>Extremely Hard: Improvising from an unfamiliar chord progression.<li>Sheer Folly: Improvising a new chord progression.<li>Absurd: Improvising a complete work.
skills.notes: This skill can be used either to reproduce a piece of music or to improvise a melody. The difficulty of a performance manoeuvre depends on the greatness of the composition (see Music). A Play Instrument (performance) manoeuvre is equal to the difficulty of writing the work (when reproducing a composition). An Play Insturment (improvisation) manoeuvre depends on the complexity of the chord progression or melody. Each Partial Success reduces the resulting fame by 20%, each Near Success, by 10%. An Absolute Success increases the fame by 20%. (See Section 5.1).

skills.name: Poetic Improvisation
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for improvising or reading poetry. It may also be used to recognise poetical styles, forms, etc. Note that a minimum of 4 ranks in the spoken language utilized is required to use this skill.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: A limerick. <li>Easy: A sonnet or short series of heroic couplets. <li>Light: A short poem (2 or 3 verses). <li>Medium: An average length poem (4 to 6 verses, plus a possiblechorus). <li>Hard: A long poem (7 or more verses). <li>Very Hard: A (relatively) short epic. <li>Extremely Hard: A full epic.<li>Absurd: Improvising an epic.
skills.notes:
This skill is used by bards and historians to entertain royal courts, by Elves to praise one another, and by romantics wooing their lovers. The difficulty of the maneuver depends on the length of the poem being recited, or improvised. When reciting poetry, a strong meter and rhyme pattern reduces the difficulty by one level. When improvising, attempting to maintain both meter and rhyme increases the difficulty by one level.

Each rank of poetic improvisation indicates knowledge of one epic poem or equivalent amount of shorter material. Master bards can recite any number of epic poems.

Modifiers

    [Elves:+10] [7+ ranks in spoken language:+10][Improvisation:-30]

skills.name: Poetry
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for the writing of poetry, or any highly stylized form of writing. Note that the individual must have at least 4 ranks in the written language to be used. Note that this form of poetry is typically of a significantly greater quality than improvisational poetry.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: A slogan or jingle that rhymes. No self-respecting poet would ever write many of these. <li>Easy: A brief open-form poem that describes some subject without emotion. <li>Light: A short, structured poem that approaches its subject in an innovative manner. <li>Medium: An open-form poem that invokes a simple emotional response (e.g., sadness or laughter). <li>Hard: A perfectly metered and rhymed poem that inspirese a simple emotional response, perhaps in an innovative manner. <li>Very Hard: A long poem that touches on a number of emotional responses <li>Extremely Hard: A complete collection that honestly addresses a logical series of emotions (e.g., the author's journey from boy to man <li>Sheer Folly: An epic poem that causes the reader to identify strongly with the hero, feeling his pain and sharing in his triumph <li>Absurd: A masterpiece that allows the reader temporarily to experience the divine.
skills.notes: This skill is used to write a poem. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on the intricacy of the poem's structure (meter and rhyme) and depth of emotion. Modifiers: [Writing about a personal experience:+10] [Writing about an unfamiliar topic:-30] [8+ ranks in written language:+15]

skills.name: Poison Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recognizing and identifying poisons, as well as knowledge of proper application and usage techniques. (These may require a Using/ Removing Poison skill roll to actually carry through.)
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Knowledge of category (e.g., circulatory, respiratory, etc.). <li>Easy: Knowledge of climate/locale codes (e.g., m-U). <li>Light: Knowledge of form/preparation (e.g., root/paste). <li>Medium: Knowledge of specific effects (e.g., delivers 1-100 hits). <li>Hard: Knowledge of market cost and antidotes. <li>Very Hard: Knowledge of addiction factor and level. <li>Extremely Hard: Identifying a poison in its prepared state. <li>Sheer Folly: Knowledge of the combined effects of two poisons in the same category. <li>Absurd: Knowledge of the combined effects of two poisons in different categories.
skills.notes: The difficulty of locating a poison is indicated in RMFRP (p. 149). That provides the difficulty of finding such a poison in the wild. The number associated with the difficulty of finding a given poison indicates its rarity. If a character has 5 ranks in Poison Lore (i.e., knowledge level 4), he is familiar with jitsu (m-O4), including its specific effects. He knows that zaganzar (tM-6) can be found in temperate mountains and that silmaana (s-O-2) is a level 9 poison with no addiction factor.

skills.name: Poison Perception
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for perceiving the presence of poison in or on an item or object. Note that some poisons will simply be undetectable (e.g., a colorless, tasteless, odorless powder that dissolves completely in water will be very difficult if not impossible to detect).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Easy: Paste. <li>Medium: Liquid. <li>Very Hard: Powder
skills.notes: The difficulty of detecting a poison depends on the method of application (pastes are usually obvious) and the number of senses that can detect the poison. For example, cyanide has a distinctive odor, although if mixed with some food that masks the poison, it is more difficult to detect. The base difficulties-summary assume that the poison can be seen, smelled and tasted. For each sense removed, add one to the difficulty. For example, iocaine is a powder that is colorless, odorless and tasteless. It is an Absurd manoeuvre to detect this poison. Sharkasar is a paste that has an odor and is dark brown. Since it has no taste, it is a Light manoeuvre to detect this poison.

skills.name: Pole-vaulting
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for handling a pole to surmount or cross over an obstacle.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: 4'high or 4'wide. <li>Easy: 6'high or 6'wide. <li>Light: 8'high or 8'wide. <li>Medium: 10'high or 10'wide. <li>Hard: 12'high or 15'wide. <li>Very Hard: 15'high or 20'wide <li>Extremely Hard: 18'high or 30 <li>Sheer Folly: 22'high or 40'wide... <li>Absurd: 25'high or 50'wide.
skills.notes: Use of this skill assumes a sprint the round before. For each pace category above or below, the difficulty is increased by one. If the character does not have a proper pole (flexible, yet strong), the difficulty is also increased by one.

skills.name: Power Perception
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for seeing active Essence (blue), Channeling (red) and Mentalism (green) magic. If the GM allows players to develop the skill of Power Perception he should stipulate that Detect Magic spells will detect magic, active or inactive (e.g., waiting spells).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Deific magic <li>Easy: 50th level or higher spell/effect <li>Light: 37th - 49th level spell/effect <li>Medium: 26th - 36th level spell/effect <li>Hard: 17th - 25th level spell/effect <li>Very Hard: 10th - 16th level spell/effect <li>Extremely Hard: 5th - 9th level spell/effect <li>Sheer Folly: 2nd - 4th level spell/effect <li>Absurd: 1st level spell/effect
skills.notes: The difficulty of this manoeuvre depends on the power of the magic. Extremely powerful enchantments may be so overwhelming that it is difficult not to notice the presence of the spell. The distance from the location (center) of the spell, diminishes one's ability to detect the spell. Note that this skill reveals nothing about the level of the spell or effect. Modifiers: [Per foot over 10': -2] [Informational Spell: -10] [Elemental Spell: +20]

skills.name: Power Point Development
skills.description: A characters total Power Points (PP) is equal to his Power Point Development skill bonus. This skill allows a spell user to increase the total number of Power Points he may hold at any given time. The skill bonus progression for this skill is found the chart on page 85 of RMFRP. A hybrid spell caster averages his realm stat bonuses to obtain his stat bonus for this skill.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Power-striking
skills.description: This skill allows the use of a controlled burst of strength to increase the force of a blow, such as with a sword, hammer, or fist. The use of this skill requires a 40% activity action the round before the strike takes place. The round of the strike, the character receives a bonus to his OB according to how much force he puts into the blow, which in turn affects the difficulty of the manoeuvre.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: +1 OB modification. <li>Easy: +4 OB modification. <li>Light: +7 OB modification. <li>Medium: +10 OB modification. <li>Hard: +20 OB modification. <li>Very Hard: +30 OB modification. <li>Extremely Hard: +40 OB modification. <li>Sheer Folly: +50 OB modification. <li>Absurd: +60 OB modification
skills.notes: The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends only on the amount of extra OB sought.

skills.name: Power-throwing
skills.description: This skill allows the use of a controlled burst of strength to increase the range of a thrown object, such as a javelin, hammer, stone, etc. The use of this skill requires a 40% activity action the round before the throw takes place. The round of the throw, the character receives a bonus to his weapon range according to how much force he places into the throw, which in turn affects the difficulty of the manoeuvre.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: -5 OB / foot. <li>Easy: -3 OB / foot. <li>Light: -2 OB / foot. <li>Medium: -1 OB / foot+10% range. <li>Hard: -1 OB / 2 feet+25% range. <li>Very Hard: -1 OB / 3 feet+50% range. <li>Extremely Hard: -1 OB / 5 feet+75% range. <li>Sheer Folly: -1 OB / 10 feet+100% range. <li>Absurd: -1 OB / 20 feet+125% range.
skills.notes: If a large item is thrown as a weapon, the attack is resolved as a Fall/Crush attack (see RMFRP p. 226 or AL p. 75) with an OB of +1/10 pounds. The range modifier depends on the difficulty of the Power-throwing manoeuvre. The maximum distance an object can be thrown is 1 foot for every 2 unused pounds of lifting capacity (see Weightlifting).

skills.name: Prepare Herbs
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to successfully prepare a medicinal herb from its natural state into a usable form.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Below .01. <li>Easy: .01 - .1. <li>Light: .1 - .5. <li>Medium: <li>Medium: .5 - 1 <li>Hard: 1 - 2 <li>Very Hard: 2 - 4 <li>Extremely Hard: 4 - 7 <li>Sheer Folly: 7 - 10 <li>Absurd: 10 or more
skills.notes: Use of this skill supposes that the herbalist knows how the herb must be applied. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on how many ingredients are needed to purify the herb. As a general rule, divide the cost of the herb (in gold) by the rarity factor squared (cost ?) and reference below. (The GM may declare that some herbs are more or less difficult than this.)

skills.name: Prepare Poisons
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to successfully prepare a poison from its natural state into a usable form.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Below .01. <li>Easy: .01 - .1. <li>Light: .1 - .5. <li>Medium: .5 - 1. <li>Hard: 1 - 2. <li>Very Hard: 2-4. <li>Extremely Hard: 4-7. <li>Sheer Folly: 7-10. <li>Absurd: 10 or more.
skills.notes: Use of this skill supposes that the herbalist knows how the poison must be applied. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on how many ingredients are needed to prepare the poison. As a general rule, divide the cost of the poison (in gold) by the rarity factor squared (cost) and reference below. (The GM may declare that some poisons are more or less difficult than this.)

skills.name: Propaganda
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for influencing others through indirect means, rather than direct speech. Includes such ideas as starting rumors, as well as designing large advertising campaigns.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: A claim that is very reasonable. For example, Aeron is known for his sexual exploits. It is not difficult to convince the public that he is having an affair. <li>Easy: A claim that is truthful, but sounds implausible. Continuing the above example, it would be an Easy manoeuvre to convince the public that the allegations of impropriety are wrong. <li>Light: A claim that reinterprets the truth. Spin doctors attempt such manoeuvres to re-direct public attention to a different aspect of a situation. <li>Medium: A claim whose assertions cannot be verified. For example, there is a vast government conspiracy that includes the disappearance of its citizens. Thevery nature of the claim prohibits verification. <li>Hard: A claim that is contrary to the public's morals or beliefs. Convincing a tolerant public that Orcs are pond-scum would be a Hard manoeuvre. <li>Very Hard: A claim that requires the public to re-exam-me some core religious or cultural belief. The Protestant Reformation would be one example. <li>Extremely Hard: Inspiring the public to take action about some concern that is relevant to them and not con-trary to their beliefs. For example, a campaign to convince more people to bathe regularly. <li>Sheer Folly: Convincing the public to stop performing some mundane activity, including a successful prod-uct ban. <li>Absurd: Inspiring the public to take some action that goes against their core beliefs. Inciting a rebellion through propaganda alone, for example. (This would be much easier if a strong leader were to emerge.)
skills.notes: Propaganda is used to influence public opinion. It can be used to lower the public's opinion of their leader, justify a war, or anything a clever manipulator can dream of. Unlike advertising, this skill is not trying to sell a product. The effects of propaganda are more ethereal than profit (although the two are certainly related). The difficulty of the attempt depends on how much of a change is being attempted. This assumes, naturally, that the allegation, claim, or assertion is plausible. The more outrageous the statement, the more difficult it's going to be to sell it to the public. In general, successful use of this skill will modify public opinion by up to 5%. The following examples assume that a small number of people are being influenced, fewer than 100. For each factor of 100, the difficulty should be increased by one. Hence, a Propaganda manoeuvre intended to affect a country of 1,000,000 inhabitants would be increased by two levels of difficulty.

skills.name: Psychology
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recognizing and identifying major insanities (including manias, phobias, depressions, dementia, etc.) and attempting to heal or correct them. It must be developed either in-depth for a specific race or in general trends of multi-cultural racial makeup. Several races may be developed simultaneously provided research materials are available. See Gamemaster Law for more information on psychological disorders and their effects.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: See Healing, Section 4.0.

skills.name: Public Speaking
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for impressing, entertaining, or manipulating groups of people directly. Note that this is different from the Tale Telling skill, which is used on small groups, using stories and fables for entertainment and instruction. Public Speaking is for larger groups, is often more extemporaneous, and is used to manipulate the emotions or views of a crowd.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: The message reinforces common and strongly-held beliefs (e.g., a rallying speech prior to combat). <li>Easy: The audience worships the speaker, hanging on his every word (e.g., a beloved regent) <li>Light: The message reminds the audience of common beliefs that have been temporarily forgotten. This includes regaining morale following a defeat or reminding a congregation of the importance of charity <li>Medium: the audience is interested in what the speaker has to say. They will probably agree based solely off of their impression of the speaker (e.g., a hero returning to his homeland) <li>Hard: The message modifiers a common belief, but does not directly contradict it. For example, reminding people that a free and just society can harshly punish those who threaten freedom and justice <li>Very Hard: The audience is bored or disinterested <li>Extremely Hard: The message is contrary to the audience's beliefs. Convincing the audience that a crimnal should be released, or that they should voluntarily pay taxes <li>Sheer Folly: The audience is trying to ignore the speaker. Most street prophets must endure hostile audiences <li>Absurd: Converting people from one religion to another.
skills.notes: This skill is used to directly influence an audience (unlike Propaganda, which is used to indirectly influence the public). The difficulty of the attempt depends on how much attention the audience is paying, and how radical the recommendations of the speaker. In general, a Public Speaking manoeuvre will have direct effects on 10% of the audience, and indirect effects on the entire audience.

skills.name: Quickdraw
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for getting a weapon from a scabbard into battle very quickly. If successful, the weapon is out of the scabbard and in hand and moreover may make an attack and/or move the same round without the normal 20% activity required (-20 penalty) for drawing a weapon. If the skill check fails, he has dropped the weapon. On a Partial Success, the character takes the normal time (and penalty) to draw the weapon.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Readying a thrown weapon. <li>Easy: Readying a one-handed edged weapon. <li>Light: Readying a one-handed crushing weapon. <li>Medium: Readying a two-handed weapon. <li>Hard: Readying two weapons (both are one-handed edged). <li>Very Hard: Readying two weapons. <li>Extremely Hard: Readying a short bow or sling. <li>Sheer Folly: Readying a composite bow or long bow. <li>Absurd: Readying any other weapon (subject to GM approval).
skills.notes: This skill is nearly identical to Adrenal Quickdraw. If this skill is performed successfully, a weapon can be both drawn and used during the snap action phase (since drawing the weapon is a 0% action). If used with a thrown weapon, it is possible to throw two weapons in one round (provided one is already in hand). The GM may even wish to allow this skill to be used with missile weapons (representing Zen archery). The difficulty of the skill is based entirely on the size of the weapon.

skills.name: Racial Attack
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to use a natural weapon attack available to the character. The bonus of this skill is treated in all ways like a normal OB for purposes of attacking, parrying, using other special attacks, etc. Examples of natural weapon attack are horn attacks, claw attacks, tail lashes, or even biting attacks. Generally, all races with a special racial attack may learn this skill as an Everyman skill regardless of profession. The relative strength and effectiveness of each racial attack will vary by race and must be determined by the Gamemaster. See Sections 8.0 and 9.0 for more details on how to integrate racial attacks into weapon styles and martial arts styles.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Rappelling
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for rapidly descending from a height, using ropes and other equipment. If the Rappelling manoeuvre is unsuccessful, the individual has a chance of falling. Rappelling rate is equal to the individual's normal movement rate, with modifiers due to speed.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Smooth brick or concrete wall at a 75? angle. <li>Easy: Smooth brick or concrete wall. <li>Light: Rough brick wall. <li>Medium: Smooth cliff face with no extreme protrusion. <li>Hard: An uneven cliff face with some protrusions. <li>Very Hard: An extremely uneven surface. <li>Extremely Hard: An extremely uneven surface at a 120? angle.
skills.notes: The difficulty of a Rappelling manoeuvre depends on the quality of the surface being descended. Uneven surfaces with multiple protrusions are more difficult to rappel down than smooth brick walls. Modifiers: [Rope and climbing gear:+20] [Rope only:-15] [No rope or equipment:Use Climbing]

skills.name: Reading Tracks
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for gleaning information from a set of tracks or spoor. Detailed information about the tracks can be obtained, such as type of creatures, age of tracks, weight of creature, speed creature moving at, back tracking, etc. This skill is used for identifying the tracks and the Tracking skill is used for spotting and following the tracks.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Determining size of creature (tiny, small, medium, large, or huge). <li>Easy: Determining if tracks belong to a humanoid or nonhumanoid. <li>Light: Determining number of creatures. <li>Medium: Determining type of creature (e.g., dog, cat, Wyvern, etc.). <li>Hard: Determining speed. Determining age of tracks. <li>Very Hard: Determining race of humanoid. <li>Extremely Hard: Determining close approximation of weight. <li>Sheer Folly: Determining the frequency with which a specific type of creature uses a game trail. <li>Absurd: Determining if a known individual made the tracks.
skills.notes: The difficulty of this manoeuvre depends on the amount of information that the character is attempting to gain. The quality of the print will also modify the manoeuvre roll Modifiers: [Grass:-10] [Stone:-20] [Falling snow:-10 / hour] [Mud:+20] [Snow:+10]

skills.name: Read Runes
skills.description: The Read Runes skill enables a character to decipher and use magical runes (spells inscribed in suitable media). If the level of the spell on the rune is less than or equal to the level of the character attempting to use it to cast a spell, deciphering the rune is sufficient to use it (subject to the normal chances of spell failure). If the rune is a level above the character, or of a realm of magic other than the character's realm(s), a second roll, similar to the first, must be made successfully to cast the spell from the rune. Runes are generally not reusable, but the rune paper is. Each character should be given one chance to decipher a rune. If he fails, he may not try again until he improves his skill rank with Read Runes.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: Modifiers: [Realm of the spell is unknown:-20] [Realm of the spell is known:+10] [Spell is not known:-10] [Spell is known:+20] [Realm of the spell differs from character:-30] [Character can cast spell intrinsically:+30]

skills.name: Reality Awareness
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to determine if the natural order or reality has been or is going through turmoil, (e.g., Demonic gate opening or closing, power fluctuation which is disturbing or causing the fabric of this dimension to shift, holes in the space-time continuum, residual powerful magic, etc.). Note that this skill may be severely limited in its availability.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Within 10'. <li>Easy: 11'-30'. <li>Ught: 31'-100'. <li>Medium: 101'-300'. <li>Hard: 310'-500'. <li>Very Hard: 501'-1000'. <li>Extremely Hard: 1001'-3000'. <li>Sheer Folly: 3001'-1 mile. <li>Absurd: 1 mile+.
skills.notes: The further the character is from the warp in reality, the more difficult this maneuver is. If the maneuver attempts to detect the opening or closing of a warp, add the level of the spell required to create the warp to the Reality Awareness maneuver roll. If the spell level is not known, assume that opening or closing a warp requires a 20th level spell. Once a warp is open the spell level does not modify the maneuver roll.

skills.name: Region Lore
skills.description: This skill provides knowledge about the geography of a specific region. Note that skill for each region must be developed separately. All characters begin with ranks in Region Lore for their own region.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Identifying the major cities in an area. <li>Easy: Identifying the most important landmarks. <li>Light: Identifying the significant of medium-sized cities <li>Medium: Identifying the historical significance of an area. Identifying a location that matches a general set of criteria (e.g., Where is there a good inn?) <li>Hard: Identifying small towns includng their most prominent features <li>Very Hard: Identifying minor landmarks <li>Extremely Hard: Identifying a location that matches a very specific set of sriteria (e.g., Where is there an inn that has a secret chamber and a back door?) <li>Sheer Folly: Identifying every feature of the GM's map including details of such locations <li>Absurd: Knowledge of most buildings larger than an abode in the region.
skills.notes: This skill provides characters and players with information about a single region. This allows the character to identify landmarks and other significant features (like havens, etc.). This skill is useful for determining which location best meets certain criteria. All characters begin with a rudimentary knowledge of their home region, enough to identify major landmarks.

skills.name: Religion
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recognizing and identifying major aspects of religious doctrines. Each religion may be concentrated in and learned separately for in-depth knowledge and understanding.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Simple faith <li>Easy: Knowledge of common beliefs and rituals. <li>Light: Understanding of how a person should live one's life, based on the tenets of a faith. Predicting the behavior of a fanatic or zealot. <li>Medium: Resolving common religious dilemmas (e.g., can a peaceful person defend himself?). <li>Hard: Knowledge of uncommon rituals and an understanding of how the beliefs relate to one another. <li>Very Hard: Intimate understanding of how the religion fits into a cultural and historical context. Predicting the behavior of a highly spiritual person. <li>Extremely Hard: Resolving difficult religious dilemmas (e.g., when can a peaceful faith declare war?). <li>Sheer Folly: Predicting the behavior of a devout follower. Creating a new religious doctrine that incorporates aspects of one or more other doctrines. <li>Absurd: Predicting the behavior of the common follower whose decisions are only slightly modified by his beliefs.
skills.notes: This skill provides characters with knowledge of one or more religions. The GM may want to provide the player with some information prior to play. Knowledge of religion is useful in understanding motivations and beliefs, which can be heavily influenced by religion. A successful Religion manoeuvre might provide a character with insight into a religious leader's reaction to an event, or how to motivate a congregation into action. This skill can also be used to defend the tenets of a faith within a certain context. (If God is good, why is there evil in the world?) Note that this skill is used to defend a belief, not create it.

skills.name: Research
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for using multiple sources of reference to assimilate the knowledge and information necessary to solve a problem, support a creative effort, or otherwise answer questions important to the individual. It includes the skills necessary to organize a search through reference material, and collate the results. Note that skill is necessary for the creation of new spell lists. If appropriate materials are available, a successful manoeuvre using appropriate materials will give up to a +40 (twice normal subsequent manoeuvre bonus) modification to a related Lore manoeuvre.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Researching a modification to a knownspell <li>Easy: Researching a spell that will exist on a spell list the character has. <li>Light: researching a spell from another list to be inserted into a spell list the character has. <li>Medium: Researching a new spell that will exist independent of any spell list <li>Hard: Researching a new spell whose effects are very dissimilar from anything with which the reasercher is familiar <li>Very Hard: Reasearching a spell list that is a modification of a known spell list. <li>Extremely Hard: Researching a spell list that would be classified as a Base List for the character's Profession <li>Sheer Folly: Researching a new spell list within the character's realm <li>Absurd: Researching a new spell list of a different realm.
skills.notes: This skill can only be used to research information that already exists. Except for spell lists, this skill cannot be used to generate new knowledge. Some other Science/Analytic skill must be used for that. The difficulty of a Research manoeuvre depends on the difficulty of the Lore manoeuvre being researched. Whereas Lore skills produce results much more quickly, a good researcher need learn only one skill (provided he has access to a good reference library). When researching new spells or spell lists, the difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on the similarity of the attempt to what the researcher already knows. A significant amount of time and materials will also be necessary. (See Spell Law.)

skills.name: Reverse Stroke
skills.description: This skill provides a limit for applying oneÒs melee OB against an opponent to oneÒs flank or rear without turning or changing position. The OB of an attack made in this fashion cannot exceed the attackerÒs Reverse Stroke skill bonus. Note that this skill must be developed separately for each weapon category.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No Notes

skills.name: Riding
skills.description: A single rank is necessary to keep from constantly falling off the animal being ridden. Higher skill ranks enhance the chance of controlling the animal (of the type for which the skill is developed). This skill must be developed separately for each different type of animal.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Walk. <li>Easy: Canter/Run. A slow turn. <li>Light: Gallop (Sprint or faster). Walking up an incline or stairs. <li>Medium: Trot/Jog. Jumping a low obstacle. Convincing a carnivore to attack. <li>Hard: Crossing water. <li>Very Hard: Jumping an obstacle the height of the mount's chest. A controlled rear. Charging. <li>Extremely Hard: Approaching an obvious danger (e.g., fire, combat, etc.). Convincing an herbivore to attack. <li>Sheer Folly: Swimming. <li>Absurd: Approaching an awesome danger (e.g., a Dragon or Demon).
skills.notes: Note that this skill involves convincing an animal to perform a specific manoeuvre. The mount performs the actual moving manoeuvre. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on the degree to which the mount naturally wants to perform the action. Natural horse actions include walking, eating, fleeing danger, etc. A horse can accelerate up to three pace categories per turn (e.g., from walk to sprint). It can decelerate a like amount. The difficulty of such a manoeuvre depends on the target pace. A GM may decide that some manoeuvres performed in the saddle qualify as Athletic - Gymnastic manoeuvres. For example, standing in the saddle (Tightrope Walking), riding along the side of the horse (Contortions), leaping from horse to horse (Jumping and/or Acrobatics), etc. Modification is based on the % activity used for riding: [5%: -30] [10%: -25] [20%: -20] [30%: -15] [40%: -10] [50% -5] [60%: 0] [70%: +5] [80%: +10] [90%: +15] [100%: +20]

skills.name: Rigid Leather Armour
skills.description: Each armour type has a Moving Manoeuvre Penalty (MMP) associated with it for untrained individuals. This penalty modifies Moving Manoeuvre rolls. The different armour subcategories are divided into five groups based upon the composition of the armour: type 1-4 = No Armour; subcategories 5-8 = Soft Leather; subcategories 9-12 = Rigid Leather; subcategories 13-16 = Chain; and subcategories 17-20 = Plate. There are no Moving Manoeuvre Penalties associated with No Armour, and therefore there is no need to apply skill ranks towards it. The Soft and Rigid Leather skills are both found in the Light Armour Skill Category; Chain is found in the Medium Armour Skill Category; Plate is found in the Heavy Armour Skill Category. Every encumbering armour has a minimum manoeuvre penalty associated with it. The skill bonus for manoeuvring for a group of armour subcategories reduces the maximum penalty for manoeuvring until the minimum manoeuvre penalty is reached. This limit represents the fact that weight and constriction of the armour will always hinder the character to some extent. These minimums may vary for certain superior or magical suits of armour. In addition, each armour type has a Quickness penalty associated with it. An Armour Quickness penalty can reduce or cancel a combatant's Quickness stat bonus for his DB (see RMFRR p. 33). It will not reduce a combatant's overall DB below the level that it would be at with a zero Quickness stat bonus.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Careful drop. <li>Easy: Standing while in AT 1-6 or 9. <li>Light: Rapid drop. Standing while in AT 10 or 13. <li>Medium: Standing while in AT 7, 14, or 17. <li>Hard: Standing while in AT 8, 11, or 12. <li>Very Hard: Standing while in AT 15, 16 or 18. <li>Extremely Hard: Standing while in AT 19. <li>Sheer Folly: Standing while in AT 20. <li>Absurd: Diving for cover.
skills.notes: The GM may require the character to make manoeuvre rolls for various activities in combat. The most common examples are standing up and dropping to the ground. It should be difficult to injure oneself by standing. It merely takes time. Conversely, a drop or dive is always successful, but the character may be injured in the process (+0 Fall).

skills.name: Rope Mastery
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for knot recognition, knot tying, braiding, rope splicing, or throwing a line.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Tying shoes or boots. <li>Easy: Braiding three ropes together. <li>Light: Securing an inanimate object. Mediuim: Tying two ropes together to increase their length without decreasing the amount of load that can be suspended. <li>Hard: Securing a person or creature (provided they are unconscious or otherwise subdued). <li>Very Hard: Attaching two ropes of different sizes. Splicing two ropes together. <li>Extremely Hard: Securing an animate target using a lasso (the target gets an RR: level vs. number of ranks of Rope Mastery). <li>Sheer Folly: Attaching two cables to one another. <li>Absurd: Securing an animate target using a chain.
skills.notes: This skill covers any manoeuvre attempted with a rope that does not involve the character moving. Such manoeuvres are covered by Climbing or Acrobatics. The skill is useful for securing prisoners or tying a boat to a dock.

skills.name: Rowing
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for the propulsion of watercraft through the use of paddles, oars, or poles. It combines the skills required to control and guide the craft with the coordination to work with others in rhythm (when necessary), in addition to the marshaling and pacing of internal resources to last throughout the journey.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Accelerating one pace category (e.g., from walk to jog). <li>Easy: Maintaining a walk. Decelerating two pace cat egories. <li>Light: Maintaining a jog. Making a 45'turn. <li>Medium: Maintaining a run. Making a 90 turn. Decelerating three pace categories. <li>Hard: Maintaining a sprint. Making a 135'turn. <li>Very Hard: Maintaining a fast sprint. Decelerating four pace categories. <li>Extremely Hard: Making a 180 turn. <li>Sheer Folly: Maintaining a dash. Decelerating five pace categories. <li>Absurd: Decelerating six pace categories.
skills.notes: Rowed vehicles are, in general, not particularly manoeuvreable, but they are more manoeuvreable than a sailing vehicle. It is possible to make relatively tight turns since each side of the vehicle can act independently of the other. Attaining speed in a rowed vehicle is more difficult than with a sailing vehicle, however. The difficulty of a rowing manoeuvre is dependent on two factors: the speed of the vehicle and how sharp the manoeuvre is. Also, smaller vehicles (like rowboats) are more manoeuvreable than long ships. The size of the vehicle may modify the difficulty of the manoeuvre by one level. The following examples assume that the vehicle is moving at a walking pace. Faster paces result in correspondingly more difficult manoeuvres. Partial and Near Successes indicate that the vehicle begins to rock and might take on water. Failure indicates that the vehicle performs no manoeuvre and slows by one pace category. Absolute and Spectacular Failures may indicate that the vehicle tips. It takes one round to accelerate one pace category (e.g., from jog to run). These examples also assume a complete crew. Fewer rowers than normal will reduce the base speed by a similar amount. For example, a long ship that requires 30 rowers has only 15. It moves at half speed. If there are fewer than one fourth of the necessary crew, the ship cannot move.

skills.name: Sailing
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for manoeuvreing a watercraft with one or more sails. It includes the skills required to control and guide such a craft as well as perform routine maintenance.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Accelerating one pacecategory (e.g., from walk tojog). <li>Easy: Turning up to 15 degrees. <li>Light: Slowing down one pacecategory (e.g., from run to jog). <li>Medium: Controlling a boat that sideswipes another (either intentionally or not). Turning up to 30 degrees. <li>Hard: Slowing down two pace categories (e.g., from run tostop). <li>Very Hard: Controlling a vehicle that rams another (either intentionally or not). Turning up to 45 degrees. <li>Extremely Hard: Slowing down three pace categories (e.g., from sprint to walk). <li>Sheer Folly: Making a right-angle turn. <li>Absurd: Slowing down four pace categories (e.g., from sprint to stop).
skills.notes: Sailing vessels are, in general, not manoeuvreable, but they are much faster than rowed vessels. Even when sailing into the wind, many sailing vessels can move quite rapidly. The difficulty of a Sailing manoeuvre is dependent on two factors: the speed of the vessel and how sharp the manoeuvre is. Also, smaller vessels (like river boats) are more manoeuvreable than galleys or long-ships. The size of the vessel may modify the difficulty of the manoeuvre by one level. The following examples assume that the vessel is moving at a walking pace. Faster paces result in correspondingly more difficult manoeuvres. If a Sailing manoeuvre fails, the boat fails to manoeuvre; it continues in the direction it was heading the previous round, decelerating one pace category, to a minimum of a walk. Absolute and Spectacular Failures might cause the ship to be damaged or capsized. Partial and Near Successes probably indicate that the boat takes on water. The maximum attainable pace depends on whether or not the vessel is moving with the wind (dash), against the wind (jog), or perpendicular to the wind (sprint). Modifiers: [No wind:The boat cannot manoeuvre] [Light Breeze:+10 (x0.5 movement)] [Strong Breeze:+5 (x0.75 movement)] [Light Wind:0 (x1.0 movement)] [Strong Wind:-10 (x1.25 movement)] [Gale:-25 (x1.5 movement)]

skills.name: Sanity Healing
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to attempts to recognize and treat various forms of mental disorder. This skill must be developed separately for each race.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Scaling
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for climbing manoeuvres of extended duration, including the climbing of mountains, long stairways, etc. It combines the skills required to climb safely and the marshaling and pacing of internal resources to last throughout the entire climb.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Scaling a 30 incline. <li>Easy: Climbing a long staircase. <li>Light: Scaling a 45'incline. <li>Medium: Scaling a 60'incline. <li>Hard: Scaling a stone wall. <li>Very Hard: Scaling a rough wall (like a cliff face). <li>Extremely Hard: Scaling a 105'incline. <li>Sheer Folly: Scaling a smooth wall (designed to have minimal hand-holds) or 120'stone surface. <li>Absurd: Scaling a 120'smooth surface or a 135 stone surface.
skills.notes: There are two major factors that determine the difficulty of a Scaling manoeuvre: the grade (angle) of the climb and the frequency of hand-holds. This skill is not as strenuous as Climbing, but slower and more difficult. (This prevents characters from performing sustained climbs on the ceiling.) Add one difficulty level if the surface is sandy, two if wet, three if oily and four if icy.

skills.name: Scribing
skills.description: This skill gives proficiency in secretarial skills, including calligraphy, taking dictation and librarian skills.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Copying a printed page. <li>Easy: Generating a barely legible work. <li>Light: Dictation from a slow, precise speaker. <li>Medium: Copying a work written neatly, by hand. <li>Hard: Generating a neat, clear work with crisp lettering. <li>Very Hard: Dictation from a speaker who mumbles, stutters, or rephrases things frequently. <li>Extremely Hard: Generating a work with ornate illumination. <li>Sheer Folly: Copying a text that has been severely damaged by time and was poorly written originally. <li>Absurd: Dictation in a language with which the scribe is not familiar. A phonetic representation of the words is produced.
skills.notes: The difficulty of a Scribing manoeuvre may depend on a number of factors: the clarity of the work being copied, the clarity of the speaker (dictation), the intricacy of the lettering being used, and the scribe's familiarity with the language. Modifiers: [3-5 ranks in written language:-10] [8+ ranks in written language:+10]

skills.name: Scrounging
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus in being able to come up with the location of a particular needed item, part or ingredient. This skill is normally used in an urban type of setting. This does not cover locating food or water.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Locating an item that is frequently discarded (e.g., clothing). <li>Easy: Locating a specific common item or part. <li>Light: Locating an illegal good that is common and for which the penalty for possession is minor. <li>Medium: Locating a discarded item with a minor resale value. Locating an uncommon item or part. <li>Hard: Locating a discarded item of little or no value. <li>Very Hard: Locating an illegal good that must be smuggled into the area at some risk. <li>Extremely Hard: Locating a discarded item of moderate value. Locating a specific rare item or part. <li>Sheer Folly: Locating an illegal good, possession of which is dangerous. <li>Absurd: Locating an illegal good that is closely guarded (e.g., military technology).
skills.notes: This skill is generally used to locate items that have been discarded (and are therefore free) or are illegal. In either case, the difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on the rarity of the item. If scrounging for a discarded item, the item's value must be taken into consideration; if scrounging for an illegal item, the penalty for selling the item is a key factor. In some cases, the GM may require a character to make a Scrounging manoeuvre in order to locate a part or component (since most dealers located using Contacting are purveyors of new merchandise).

skills.name: Sculpting
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for the manipulation of a malleable material or the carving of a resilient material into a desired three-dimensional shape. This skill does not confer the ability to work materials normally unworkable (e.g., the individual must have the means to mold and form copper if the sculpture is to be formed of that metal). Note that this skill may also be used to identify styles of sculpture and to imitate other sculptures.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: A simple bowl or plate. <li>Easy: A crude representation that is recognizable as a person, animal, mushroom, etc. <li>Light: A stylistic representation of an object. Many primitive religious items are of this quality. <li>Medium: An accurate representation of a person or object, that lacks any depth or spirit. <li>Hard: A precise representation that displays every aspect in stark detail. <li>Very Hard: A moving sculpture that incorporates a touch of the subject's essence or spirit. Viewers gain insight into the target's nature. <li>Extremely Hard: An impressive piece that fully captures nuances in the subject's nature. The artist's relation to the subject is subtly incorporated. <li>Sheer Folly: Designing a piece that inspires a new style. Such a work is refreshing in its approach to the subject. <li>Absurd: A masterpiece that inspires fear or awe, depending on the subject matter.
skills.notes: The sculptor's goal is the representation of a real object, scene or person. This representation is usually realistic, but may be symbolic or emotive. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on the beauty and depth of expression of the piece of art to be produced. As a sculptor gains skill, he is able to incorporate greater detail. Some sculptors allow the stone or wood to express itself naturally; the sculptor is not sure of the final product until it is completed. The perceived greatness of the work depends to a large extent on the audience. Without a rich sponsor, a sculptor leads a meager existence. Modifiers: [Unfamiliar medium:-30] [From posed image or person:+10] [From memory:-30 (+ Memory stat bonus x 3)]

skills.name: Second Aid
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for performing minor surgery, including sewing closed wounds, removing diseased or mangled limbs, bone setting and any other minor surgery operation.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Easy: Cauterizing a Wound.
