Cauterizing will stop bleeding to any degree, provided 1-10 points of burning damage are inflicted for every hit/rnd of bleeding. <li>Medium: Suturing a Wound, Open wounds have a chance of becoming infected. If a wound is not cleaned, sewn and bandaged, the character must make an RR against a bubonic disease (infection). The level of the infection is 1/2 the penalty for the wound, plus the hits/rnd the wound was originally bleeding. In hot moist climes, the RR is at -30.<li>Hard: Setting and Casting Fractures. This action will heal a fracture, and allow recovery to begin.
skills.notes: See Healing, Section 4.0.

skills.name: Seduction
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus when attempting to emotionally, sensually, or sexually manipulate someone. Note that this is not limited to sexual seduction! Manipulation of a person's sensual sensibilities, urging a person to indulge in some fantasy or desire, and convincing a person of some tenet on emotional rather than rational grounds can all be classified as seduction.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Convincing someone to do something he was probably going to do anyway. For example, enticing a john. <li>Easy: Swaying a target to your side in a conflict, when that target is unsure of his own position. <li>Light: Causing a target to fulfill a strong desire with no chance of discovery. <li>Medium: Convincing someone to succumb to a normal desire when there is little risk or chance of discovery. <li>Hard: Swaying a target to your side, provided the target has little stake in the outcome. <li>Very Hard: Convincing a target to succumb to a normal desire when there is a significant chance of discovery. This includes any political is at stake. <li>Extremely Hard: Swaying a target to your side, when the target has an investment in the outcome (e.g., his family is in danger, he has deep philosophical beliefs, etc.). <li>Sheer Folly: Seducing a target with little interest in the offer. <li>Absurd: Convincing a target to do something that is dangerous or lethal. Some cults seduce their members into suicide pacts.
skills.notes: Seduction is used to convince the target to succumb to his desires. If the target does not have a specific desire, no amount of seduction will change his mind. Unfortunately, there are very few people who do not have any base desires; fewer still who can repress these desires when faced with temptation. The difficulty of a Seduction manoeuvre depends on the strength of the desire and the seriousness of the action. Some people cannot withstand the slightest temptation, while others can resist almost anything.

skills.name: Sense Ambush
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to detect animate traps, ambushes or assassination in progress. Note that this is a passive skill, and should not be used when the player has indicated that he is actively searching for signs of ambush or assassins. Range is 10' per skill rank. The existence of this as an acquirable skill indicates one's ability to train one's level of sensitivity to such things, but more active observation should be handled by the skills of Observation and/or Situational Awareness.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: This skill provides a penalty to Ambush manoeuvres. This skill can also be used to detect traps as they are being triggered. If the result of the manoeuvre is some level of success, the character may be able to react before it's too late.

skills.name: Sense Awareness
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to the individual's ability to discern detail and information through the use of a particular sense (i.e., sight, touch, etc.). Note that skill for each sense must be developed separately.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Sight: On top of a mountain, Sound: in complete silence <li>Easy: Sight: On an empty plain. Sound: In a quiet alley <li>Light: Sight: On a deserted city street. Sound: While walking normally. <li>Medium: Sight: On a plain with occasional trees. Sound: While moving in metal armour. <li>Hard: Sight: At twilight. Sound: During a conversation <li>Very Hard: Sight: In light fog. Sound: During a storm. <li>Extremely Hard: Sight: In a forest or swamp. Sound: During melee <li>Sheer Folly: Sight: In dense fog. Sound: During a rock concert <li>Absurd: Sight: On a moonless night. Sound: While a Dragon is roaring nearby.
skills.notes: Sense Awareness is used automatically to detect features of the environment. The difficulty of this manoeuvre depends on the size or strength of the stimulus in relation to background stimuli. A Dragon on the horizon is more noticeable than a pickpocket in a crowd. Even a Dragon cannot be seen, however, if it is far enough away. Each factor modifies the manoeuvre by ?10: are provided for sight and sound. Other senses can be extrapolated from the examples given. Sight: An average human can spot a single man-sized figure at a distance of 500 yards. Below are the average distances at which various objects can be discerned. Details cannot be discerned until the object is one category closer Object Size/Average Distance to Discern Minute - 10 feet; Tiny - 100 feet; Small - 100 yards; Man-Sized - 500 yards; Large - 1000 yards; Huge Creature - 1 mile; Small Dwelling - 1 mile; Medium Dwelling - 3 miles; Huge Dwelling - 5 miles; For example, spotting a Dragon at a range of one half mile gets a bonus of +10; Noticing a minute detail at 30' gets a penalty of -20. If the object is moving, there is an additional bonus of +10. Sound: An average human can discern a normal conversation from 50 feet away. Below are the average distances at which various volumes can be discerned. Details cannot be discerned until the object is one category closer. Each factor modifies the manoeuvre by ?10: Type of Sound/Average Distance to Discern Very Quiet Sound - 5 feet; Whisper - 10 feet; Normal Conversation - 50 feet; Yelling - 50 yards; Trumpet or Drum - 200 yards; Gun-shot - 500 yards; Small Airplane - 1 mile;

skills.name: Service
skills.description: This skill gives a bonus to performing service duties, such as those of a valet, maid, butler, etc.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Serving an optimist. <li>Easy: Serving a cheerful person <li>Light: Serving someone having a bad day <li>Medium: Serving an average person, such that the person is pleased with the service <li>Hard: Serving someone having a really, really bad day <li>Very Hard: Serving a dour or cranky person <li>Extremely Hard: Serving a pessimist <li>Sheer Folly: Serving a condescending noble <li>Absurd: Serving a Demon.
skills.notes: The difficulty of a service manoeuvre depends on the demeanour of the person being served. Cheerful people are much easier to please than are cranky codgers. Note that a manoeuvre is made only if the server is interested in pleasing the target. Otherwise, treat the manoeuvre as an automatic failure.

skills.name: Setting Traps
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for setting traps. Traps can be lethal or non-lethal. The traps used by this skill are either very simple snares or pre-built mechanisms that are set into place.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Traps triggered by a rope strung across a corridor. <li>Easy: Traps triggered by pressure plates (e.g., a bear trap or mine). <li>Light: Traps triggered by weight (e.g., a pit trap). <li>Medium: Traps triggered by turning a door knob or opening a latch. <li>Hard: Traps whose effect spans a large area (e.g., a collapsing wall or flooding room) unless the trigger islisted above. <li>Very Hard: Gas traps. <li>Extremely Hard: Traps whose trigger is on the other side of a door. <li>Sheer Folly: Traps whose trigger is specific to a given individual. <li>Absurd: Traps whose trigger is specific to a given individual and well removed from the trap.
skills.notes: The difficulty of this manoeuvre depends on the amount of effort involved in hiding the trigger. The difficulty of this manoeuvre determines the difficulty of the Detect Traps manoeuvre needed to discover the trap.

skills.name: Sewing
skills.description: This provides a bonus to static manoeuvres involving sewing. These skills include fashioning garments, blankets, etc. as well as repairing such items.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Replacing a button. <li>Easy: Darning a sock. <li>Light: Sewing a familiar, simple pattern (e.g., a tunic or surcoat). <li>Medium: Sewing a familiar pattern (e.g., a shirt or jacket). <li>Hard: Sewing a familiar, complex pattern (e.g., a formal gown or ceremonial garb). <li>Very Hard: Sewing an unfamiliar pattern. Designing a new pattern (e.g., a shirt that contains a hidden pouch). <li>Extremely Hard: Designing a complex pattern (e.g., a ceremonial robe whose encumbering pieces can easily be removed by ripping them off, for example to facilitate fighting). <li>Sheer Folly: Sewing with unconventional materials (e.g., metal, plastic, etc.). <li>Absurd: Designing clothing for a creature that has never been seen by the designer.
skills.notes: The difficulty of a Sewing manoeuvre depends on the intricacy of the final product. The durability of the garment also modifies the difficulty of the manoeuvre.

skills.name: Shield-making
skills.description: This skill is utilized by the character for attempts at constructing shields.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: The goal of this skill is to fashion one or more shields from available materials. The difficulty depends on the type and weight of the final shield along with the construction materials. This skill skill assumes the character has all the necessary tools for the craft in question. Without the necessary implements increase the difficulty by 3.

skills.name: Ship-building
skills.description: This skill is utilized by the character for the successful engineering, construction and repair of ships.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: assembling a simple flotation aid. (e..g, log with an outrider or raft) <li>Easy: constructing a non-keeled lake boat (e.g. coracle) <li>Light: constructing a flat water (lakes & slow moving rivers) vessel, size 50' <li>Medium: constructing a river boat, size 75' <li>Hard: constructing a coastal vessel size 100' (e.g., Trireme) <li>Very Hard: constructing a sea going vessel, size 100' (e.g., Viking longboat) <li>Extremely Hard: constructing an ocean going vessel, size 200' (e.g., Frigate, Clipper) <li>Sheer Folly: constructing an ocean going vessel, size 300' <li>Absurd: constructing an ocean going vessel, size 400'
skills.notes: The dificulty is based on the type of hull. This skill assumes that the appropriate tools are available, otherwise increase the difficulty by 3 levels Modifiers: [Dry dock:+10] [Ship yard:+30] [Sails:-20] [Increased speed:-1 / 1%]

skills.name: Siege Engineering
skills.description: Allows the user knowledge of conducting all aspects of a siege. Includes proper and best positioning of siege weapons, determining weaker portions of a wall (for siege weapon assault and/or sapping), basic engineering knowledge for building ramps, digging trenches and horse traps (for opposing cavalry), etc.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: A straw hut. <li>Easy: A wooden dwelling. <li>Light: A stone dwelling. <li>Medium: An outpost or wooden palisade. <li>Hard: A palace. <li>Very Hard: A city wall. <li>Extremely Hard: A fortress. <li>Sheer Folly: A heavily fortified keep. <li>Absurd: A complex built out of a mountain (rather than on).
skills.notes: The difficulty of this manoeuvre depends on the quality of the structure under siege. Successful siege engineering will (over time) result in the destruction of the building's defenses. Each successful week of siege engineering reduces the DB of the structure by 5. If the DB is ever reduced to -50, the building is demolished. A successful siege engineering manoeuvre can also prevent attempts to re-supply.

skills.name: Signaling
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus when using any form of signal communications. This skill is a specialized form of linguistics and linguistics guidelines apply.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: Treat this skill as a language, subject to the following modifications: <li>Halve the number of skill ranks when referencing the Language Rank Table T4.7 (RMFRP p. 115). <li>Both the sender and the receiver must make successful manoeuvres. If either fail, the information is garbled. Neither can temporarily provide the other with additional ranks. <li>Like Language, each form of Signaling must be developed separately.

skills.name: Silent Attack
skills.description: This skill is used in conjunction with an Ambush manoeuvre. A successful Ambush manoeuvre followed by a successful static manoeuvre using this skill (0% activity) result in the target being unable to make a sound during the attack. Note that this skill also requires that the attacker approach the foe undetected and strike before he can react. If an instant kill or immobilization result is obtained on a critical chart, the target does not make a noise.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Neither party is wearing armour; the floor has pillows or thick carpeting. <li>Easy: The attacker is wearing leather armour. <li>Light: The victim is wearing leather armour, <li>Medium: Both the attacker and victim are wearing leather armour. <li>Hard: The attacker is wearing metal armour. <li>Very Hard: The victim is wearing chain armour. <li>Extremely Hard: The victim is wearing plate armour. <li>Sheer Folly: Both the attacker and victim are wearing metal armour. <li>Absurd: The victim is a construct or other automaton.
skills.notes: The difficulty of a Silent Attack manoeuvre depends on how armoured the attacker and victim are. It is also facilitated by a cushioned surface.

skills.name: Singing
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for vocally reproducing musical tunes and/or words. Note that although one may perform a song in an unfamiliar language, this skill does not provide any understanding of the language; this skill merely allows the memorization and reproduction of a song.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: A scale. <li>Easy: A simple melody or air. A jingle or ditty. <li>Light: A piece with limited appeal. Music with technical flair, but no emotion. <li>Medium: A good piece of music. The audience is entertained, but not moved. <li>Hard: A piece that appeals to those who enjoy the particular style. A single emotion or idea can be communicated. <li>Very Hard: A performance with broad appeal. Complex emotions or multiple ideas can be conveyed. <li>Extremely Hard: A performance that will be considered great many years from now. A masterpiece that conveys an entire story or emotional interaction. <li>Sheer Folly: A performance that reinterprets a masterpiece. <li>Absurd: A performance that gains immediate recognition world-wide
skills.notes:
A singer attempts to reproduce, faithfully and emotionally, a piece of music. The intensity of the emotion and musical complexity of the song determines the difficulty of the maneuver. The impact of the performance is limited by the greatness of the composition, although a talented singer can increase the impact of even a simple song.

Each Partial Success reduces the resulting fame by 20%, each Near Success, by 10%. An Absolute Success increases the fame by 20%. (See SoHK Section 5.1).

This skill must be developed separately for each style of music to be learned. Examples include classical, baroque, romantic, jazz, rock, etc.

Modifiers: [Per rank in spoken language below 4:-10] [Improvisation:-10]

skills.name: Situational Awareness
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to the individuals ability to notice and assimilate information from the environment in a specific type of situation. This is a combination of active and passive skills specifically trained for maximum effectiveness within a given situation. For example, Scouting Awareness is used by the point man in a squad of soldiers to be alert to possible enemy approaches, traps; Sleep Awareness might aid in sleeping lightly to prevent being taken unawares; Urban Awareness might aid in staying alert for muggers, oncoming vehicles, etc. Skill with Situational Awareness must be developed for each situation as determined by the GM.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: A trivial change occurs (e.g., a new combatant joins a fray). <li>Easy: Avoiding surprise while traveling at a slow pace <li>Light: A huge change occurs (e.g., the ground is ripped in two) <li>Medium: Avoiding surprise <li>Hard: A major change occurs (e.g., one side or the other flees). After a Leaving spell to a place you can see. <li>Very Hard: Avoiding surprise while traveling at a fast pace. After a Long door spell to a place you can see <li>Extremely Hard: A minor change occurs (e.g., one's opponent becomes stunned) <li>Sheer Folly: After a Long Door of Leaving spell to a place you cannot see. <li>Absurd: After being teleported.
skills.notes: This skill is used primarily for orientation rolls and to avoid surprise. When in a potential surprise situation, each character should make a Situational Awareness manoeuvre. The total of the manoeuvre roll indicates the amount of activity that character has to use during the round of surprise. The difficulty is generally Medium. An orientation roll is required whenever a situation changes dramatically (e.g., following a teleport, the arrival of a new combatant, etc.). The total of the manoeuvre roll indicates what percentage of activity the character can devote to a reaction. His remaining activity must assume that no change has occurred. The difficulty depends on how dramatic the change was. Note that it is reasonable for both sides of an encounter to be surprised by the other. Note also that a character who fails this manoeuvre can only act during the deliberate phase. Near and Partial Success indicates that the character can act during the normal phase. A complete Success allows the character to act during any phase.

skills.name: Skating
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for Skating manoeuvres. This may also (at GM's discretion) be used to help one stay upright on slippery or icy surfaces without skating equipment.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Decelerating two pace categories. <li>Easy: Accelerating 3 pace categories. Turning 45? <li>Light: Decelerating 3 pace categories. Skating backwards <li>Medium: Accelerating four pace categories. turning 90? <li>Hard: Decelerating four pace categories. maintaining balance after colliding with another skater <li>Very Hard: Accelerating 5 pace categories. Dodging a small object <li>Extremely Hard: Decelerating 5 pace categories. Dodging a man-sized object <li>Sheer Folly: Accelerating 6 pace categories <li>Absurd: Decelerating 6 pace categories.
skills.notes: This skill is used to perform moving manoeuvres while on skates. If the character's goal is artistic, the Dancing skill should be used, modified by the character's Skating manoeuvre. The difficulty of a Skating manoeuvre depends on the speed of the skater and the sharpness of the manoeuvre. Each 180? of rotation while manoeuvring adds one to the difficulty level. For example, a triple rotation adds six to the difficulty. A character can decelerate one pace category per round or accelerate two pace categories without a manoeuvre roll.

skills.name: Skiing
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for skiing manoeuvres. This may also (at GM's discretion) be used to help one stay on one's feet when sliding down an incline without skiing equipment.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Turning 30?. Skiing a flat surface. <li>Easy: Decelerating one pace category. Skiing a smooth slope. <li>Light: Turning 60?. Remaining standing following a short jump. <li>Medium: Decelerating two pace categories. Skiing a rough slope. <li>Hard: Turning 75?. Remaining standing following a medium jump. <li>Very Hard: Decelerating three pace categories. Skiing an extremely uneven surface (eg., a mogul hill). <li>Extremely Hard: Turning 90?. Skiing an extremely steep slope. <li>Sheer Folly: Decelerating four pace categories. Remaining standing following a long jump. <li>Absurd: Turning 135? - Skiing a nearly vertical surface.
skills.notes: The goal of a skier is navigating a slope without falling. Whereas this sounds simple, it can be quite difficult when the slope is steep or uneven, or when the skier is trying to slow down or turn. Accelerating is not difficult, but the maximum pace depends on the grade of the slope.

skills.name: Skinning
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for removing, preparing, treating and caring for animal skins. Note that while this would allow a simple drape to be fashioned, this does not provide the sewing skills necessary to create normal garments.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Obtaining an intact tail. <li>Easy: Skinning a cow or pig. <li>Light: Obtaining an intact pelt from a poisoned animal. <li>Medium: Skinning a deer. <li>Hard: Obtaining an intact pelt that includes the head. <li>Very Hard: Skinning an alligator or snake. Extremely. <li>Hard: Obtaining an intact pelt ready for stuffing. <li>Sheer Folly: Skinning a Dragon. <li>Absurd: Obtaining an intact Dragon pelt.
skills.notes: This skill is used either to remove a skin in order to turn it into leather or to remove a pelt intact for direct sale. The difficulty of the former depends on the toughness of the hide. The difficulty of a Skinning manoeuvre depends on the frailty of the hide and the amount of the pelt to be preserved.

skills.name: Sleep Trance
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for decreasing the amount of time one needs to fully recover. The sleep time is increased/decreased by the amount the static manoeuvre roll is over 100 as a percentage times the racial sleep requirement. Physical prodding allows one to make a static manoeuvre to leave the trance, as does a painful strike (modify by +25).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: An isolated and sound-proof room. <li>Easy: A quiet room in which all of the occupants are sleeping. <li>Light: A still setting with some noise, but no activity (e.g., in a peaceful glen). <li>Medium: A relatively sedate setting in which there is some activity, but it is muffled. A normal wilderness setting. <li>Hard: While in aroom where two people are having a conversation. <li>Very Hard: An active setting in which there is a great deal of movement. <li>Extremely Hard: In a noisy or disruptive environment (e.g., during an argument). <li>Sheer Folly: In an extremely noisy or distracting environment (e.g., while being bombed or shot at). <li>Absurd: While in melee.
skills.notes: This skill does not use the normal static manoeuvre resolution procedure. Instead, the manoeuvre is successful if the result of the manoeuvre roll is above 100 and fails (i.e., the character requires extra sleep) if the manoeuvre is below 100. Note that Elves usually sleep by using this skill.

skills.name: Soft Leather Armour
skills.description: Each armour type has a Moving Manoeuvre Penalty (MMP) associated with it for untrained individuals. This penalty modifies Moving Manoeuvre rolls. The different armour subcategories are divided into five groups based upon the composition of the armour: type 1-4 = No Armor; subcategories 5-8 = Soft Leather; subcategories 9-12 = Rigid Leather; subcategories 13-16 = Chain; and subcategories 17-20 = Plate. There are no Moving Manoeuvre Penalties associated with No Armor, and therefore there is no need to apply skill ranks towards it. The Soft and Rigid Leather skills are both found in the Light Armor Skill Category; Chain is found in the Medium Armor Skill Category; Plate is found in the Heavy Armor Skill Category. Every encumbering armour has a minimum manoeuvre penalty associated with it. The skill bonus for manoeuvreing for a group of armour subcategories reduces the maximum penalty for manoeuvreing until the minimum manoeuvre penalty is reached. This limit represents the fact that weight and constriction of the armour will always hinder the character to some extent. These minimums may vary for certain superior or magical suits of armour. In addition, each armour type has a Quickness penalty associated with it. An Armor Quickness penalty can reduce or cancel a combatant's Quickness stat bonus for his DB (see RMFRR p. 33). It will not reduce a combatant's overall DB below the level that it would be at with a zero Quickness stat bonus.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Careful drop. <li>Easy: Standing while in AT 1-6 or 9. <li>Light: Rapid drop. Standing while in AT 10 or 13. <li>Medium: Standing while in AT 7, 14, or 17. <li>Hard: Standing while in AT 8, 11, or 12. <li>Very Hard: Standing while in AT 15, 16 or 18. <li>Extremely Hard: Standing while in AT 19. <li>Sheer Folly: Standing while in AT 20. <li>Absurd: Diving for cover.
skills.notes: The GM may require the character to make manoeuvre rolls for various activities in combat. The most common examples are standing up and dropping to the ground. It should be difficult to injure oneself by standing. It merely takes time. Conversely, a drop or dive is always successful, but the character may be injured in the process (+0 Fall).

skills.name: Spatial Location Awareness
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for allowing one to be aware of his surroundings without the aid of sight. Blindness accrues a -100 modification to all manoeuvres; Spatial Location Awareness provides a bonus to offset that penalty (the adjusted modification may actually rise as high as +10 through the use of this skill). This skill is usually used by the blind. If a non-blinded individual possesses this skill, they must reorient to use this skill (requires minimum of one round). If the individual fails this roll, he is treated as blinded for that round. Each round that the individual uses 80% of his action of +5 to his Spatial Location Awareness skill bonus. For each continuous, uninterrupted round of concentration, this modification increases by +5 (to a maximum of +50). The use of this skill is blocked by intervening barriers.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided.
skills.notes: This skill can be used to sense objects at a distance of 2' per skill rank. There are no other modifications to the skill; it is used only to offset the penalty for blindness. The GM may still decide that some skills cannot be performed while blind (e.g., Stone Evaluation).

skills.name: Spell Artistry
skills.description: This skill is primarily used by illusionists to create more vivid illusions with greater detail and similarity to real life
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: Spell Artistry allows an illusionist to mimic specific individuals down to minute details or to make scenes blend flawlessly with the surrounding environment. A secondary use of this skill is to allow all spells to have adjustable visual effects upon casting. The actual parameters of a spell cannot be changed, but the basic appearance can be modified in an artistic or unique way. For example, a fire bolt could sprout wings and a fiery dragon's head as it flies at its target. The spell will do no extra damage and have no additional effect but to increase the style of the casting to impress and frighten viewers.

skills.name: Spell Concentration
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to extending concentration upon a spell, to maintaining concentration in the face of distractions of various kinds, and to regaining the correct state of mind for resuming concentration upon a spell.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: See Mentalism Companion 7.1

skills.name: Spell Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to recognize and understand a spell. When a character realizes that he has been targeted by a spell, this skill enables him to recognize the spell being used against him. When attempting to recognize an unfamiliar written spell, the character must be able to read the language used.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Easy: The spell's realm is the same as the realm of the character making the Spell Lore maneuver Medium: Essence spell (not same realm as maneuverer). <li>Hard: Channeling spell (not same realm as maneuverer). <li>Very Hard: Mentalism spell (not same realm as maneuverer). Extremely. <li>Hard: Hybrid spell (not same realm as maneuverer). <li>Sheer Folly: Arcane spell (not same realm as maneuverer).
skills.notes: This skill requires 100% activity the round it is used. A character can reduce this to a minimum of 60% by taking a penalty of -1 for every percentage point below 100%. This skill cannot be used to read runes, although it can be used to assist a character in deciphering a magical tome or libram. The realm of the spell determines the difficulty of the manoeuvre. Use of this skill assumes that two rounds were spent preparing the spell. If more or less time is spent preparing the spell, the difficulty of the manoeuvre is modified by one difficulty level for every round of difference. Instantaneous spells have a straight -30 mod.

skills.name: Spell Mastery
skills.description: This skill allows the user to modify spells within or beyond basic parameters. Each individual spell list requires separate skill development (as with Riding or Weapon skills). This skill might be used to change the orientation upon arrival of the target of a Teleport spell, or it might be used to allow a spell user to attempt to alter a bolt spell into a ball spell. The character should use the Power Manipulation Static Manoeuvre Table SM-7.17 (p. 141) to resolve Spell Mastery manoeuvres. The result may indicate success or failure, as well as provide a modifier to any related Spell Casting static manoeuvres.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Changing a minor aspect of a spell (e.g., turning a Shock Bolt green or purple). <li>Easy: Adding a minor illusion or sensation (e.g, causing discomfort with a Grow or Shrink spell). <li>Light: Adding a large illusion (e.g., adding illusionary wings to a Fly spell). <li>Medium: Lessening the effect of a spell (e.g., using a Fire Bolt to light a campfire without igniting the surrounding woods). <li>Hard: Adding a parameter with random effects (e.g., a Wall whose height changes every round). <li>Very Hard: Fine control of a spell (e.g., using a Fire Bolt to light a pipe). <li>Extremely Hard: Adding a minor new parameter (e.g., a Wall that can move 10'/ round if the caster concentrates). <li>Sheer Folly: Minute control of a spell (e.g., using a Fire Bolt to shave). <li>Absurd: Adding a raical new parameter (e.g., casting an Absolution spell that does not destroy the target's soul, but traps it in a glass botle
skills.notes: This skill is often used to increase the range, duration or area of effect of a spell, although there are a number of different uses. This skill can be used to incorporate a visual illusion into the spell. (For example, a Shock Bolt with the head of an eagle or Demon.) It can be used to tweak the effects of a spell. (For example, modifying a bolt so that it strikes the target directly, without arcing from the caster to the target.) This skill can also be used to add new parameters to a spell. (For example, a wall that can slowly advance.) Spell Mastery can be used to lessen the effects of a spell, or to improve the caster's control over the spell's force. The possibilities are limited only by the spell caster's imagination (and the GM). The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on how dramatic the change is. In addition, the following modifiers may also be applied: Change to Parameter/Modifier x2 range, duration, area of effect, or damage -20 x3 range, duration, area of effect, or damage -30 x4 range, duration, area of effect, or damage -40 x5 range, duration, area of effect, or damage -50 Each additional x1 -10 ====== Change to Range/Modifier Self to touch or touch to 10' -30 ====== Change to Duration/Modifier None to 1 round -50 Concentration to 1 minute/level(c) -50 Concentration to 1 round/level(c) -20 ====== Change to Area of Effect/Modifier +1 target -30 Target to 10'R -50 ====== Change to Damage/Modifier +1 critical severity -30

skills.name: Spell Trickery
skills.description: This skill provides the ability to prepare and cast spells unobtrusively
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: This covers all secretive casting from casting, from a hiding place to casting on someone with whom you are conversing. The total skill roll minus 100 is the penalty applied to a target's chance of observing the spell casting attempt. Modifiers: [Instantaneous Spell:+25] [Each round of preparation:-5] [Hiding:modified by hiding maneuver roll] [Less than 10' away:-15] [In conversation:-50] [No verbal:+10] [Whisper:0] [Normal:-10] [Shout:-75] [Somaticist:-20 if visible] [Arcane Spell:-20] [Channeling Spell:0] [Essence Spell:0] [Mentalism Spell:+30]

skills.name: Spinning
skills.description: This skill is used for the spinning of fibres into a thread.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Sprinting
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for maximizing one's speed over short distances, including marshaling and pacing one's resources (exhaustion point expenditure) and running in a safe and non-injurious manner.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Medium: open road <li>Hard: Trail or open plains <li>Very Hard: Rocky or broken ground, forest <li>Extremely Hard: Soft ground (e.g., snow, sand, etc) <li>Sheer Folly: Up a 30 degree slope <li>Absurd: Up a 45 degree slope, steeper slopes require climbing
skills.notes: Using this skill to manoeuvre on a flat, smooth surface (like a race-track) is detailed in Sec. 16.0 of RMFRP (p. 51). Unfortunately, characters rarely find themselves on ideal running surfaces. The following examples assume that a character is dashing with a weight penalty of -l to -10 (normally a Medium manoeuvre). Adjust other situations accordingly.

skills.name: Stalking
skills.description: Stalking is the ability to move using silence, camouflage, and shadows to conceal your presence; Hiding is the same ability used when not moving.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Stalking across pillows or thick carpeting <li>Easy: Stalking over moss <li>Light: Stalking across thin carpeting <li>Medium: Stalking ascross a wooden floor <li>Hard: Stalking through leaves <li>Very Hard: Stalking through underbrush <li>Extremely Hard: Stalking across squeaky floorboards or gravel <li>Sheer Folly: Stalking while carrying a large bag of coins, or other noisy object <li>Absurd: Stalking while carrying a living being (e.g., another person, an animal, etc)
skills.notes: This skill involves moving from one location to another without being seen or heard. A character attempting to stalk should make two manoeuvre rolls, one for sound and one for sight. Should either fail, the thief has been spotted. In some situations, only one manoeuvre roll may be necessary (e.g., approaching a target from behind, while silenced, while invisible, etc.). The difficulty of remaining unseen should be referenced under Hiding. The difficulty of remaining silent depends on how armoured the thief is, and how noisy the ground is. This manoeuvre roll should be modified by double the Missile Attack Penalty (RMFRP p. 215) of the armour worn

skills.name: Star-gazing
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for determining dates, directions, and locations when the stars are visible. May provide a bonus to one's Navigation skill.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Recognizing major constellations. <li>Easy: Recognizing major stars and planets. <li>Light: Identifying a specific direction. <li>Medium: Recognizing mahor stars and planets <li>Hard: Determining the current time <li>Very Hard: Recognizing minor stars <li>Extremely Hard: Determining one's location on the planet <li>Sheer Folly: Knoeledge of when to expect meteor showers, comets, etc <li>Absurd: Identifying all named stars
skills.notes: This skill is commonly used to provide a subsequent manoeuvre bonus to Navigation or Orienteering. In addition, this skill can be used to recognize constellations, tell time, or provide a bonus to Astrology. This skill cannot be used if there is significant cloud cover, and does not provide nearly the detail provided by Astronomy.

skills.name: Stilt-walking
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for manoeuvreing on stilts or other extensions to one's height.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: 1heels. <li>Easy: 1- 3heels. <li>Light: 3- 6extensions. <li>Medium: 0.25x character's height. <li>Hard: 0.5x character's height. <li>Very Hard: 0.75x character's height. <li>Extremely Hard: 1.0x character's height. <li>Sheer Folly: 2.0x character's height. <li>Absurd: 4.0x character's height.
skills.notes: The difficulty of walking on stilts depends on the height of the stilts (as a ratio of the character's height). Divide the height of the stilts by the character's height and reference the result below. If the ground is uneven or rocky, the manoeuvre may be modified by up to two difficulty levels.

skills.name: Stone-crafts
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for working with stone and creating sculptures, writings, or any other form of inscription or relief.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Making a crude object (e.g., a brick). <li>Easy: Making an object that requires a single stone, and no detailed crafting (e.g., quarrying). <li>Light: Cutting a stone into a shape with nonright angles (e.g., a triangle). <li>Medium: Building a simple stone wall. <li>Hard: Cutting a gem stone into a basic shape (this does not add any value to the stone). <li>Very Hard: Building a structure that has many arches, domes or other challenging portions. <li>Extremely Hard: Cutting a gem stone into an exquisite shape in order to increase its value. <li>Sheer Folly: Building an architect's masterpiece that includes dramatic curves and careful attention to detail. <li>Absurd: Cutting a magical or enchanted gem stone (like laen).
skills.notes: The difficulty of stone-working depends on the intricacy of the final product. Even a large, bulky product might require very detailed workmanship in order to function properly (e.g., an ornate carving). Like many Crafts skills, this skill assumes that the craftsman has an adequate supply of tools. Without the necessary implements, there is little a craftsman can do. (Increase all manoeuvres by at least 3 difficulty levels.)

skills.name: Stone Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recognizing and identifying stones. Also will give information on famous, magical, powerful, historic, legendary or cursed subcategories of stone. Skill is developed separately for each culture or region as applicable to the GM's world scheme.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Identifying a precious stone <li>Easy: Identifying a sedimentary stone <li>Light: Identifying a metamorphic or igneous stone <li>Medium: Determining the purity of a stone <li>Hard: Determining the relative strength of a mineral <li>Very Hard: Determining if a stone has any flaws (e.g., stress fractures, impurities, etc) <li>Extremely Hard: Identifying a stone from another area of the world <li>Sheer Folly: Knowledge of any magical or supernatural properties inherent to a stone <li>Absurd: Precise information about every known use for a stone.
skills.notes: The skill provides the character with knowledge about the stones found in a specific region. Unlike many Lore skills, the GM will probably not be able to provide the player with information prior to play. The rarity of a given stone must first be determined. Common rocks (like sandstone or clay) probably have a rarity of 1. Precious stones have a higher rarity rating, magical and enchanted stones, the highest rarity rating. See Section ScHK 5.8 (p. 17) for more information about Lore manoeuvres.

skills.name: Streetwise
skills.description: Awareness of events and protocol in the street society and underworld and the ability to interact with the individuals who run and live in the common or underworld society. Note that this skill does not necessarily enable a character to find such individuals.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: The criminal is a petty thief or pick-pocket. <li>Easy: The criminal is a street thug. <li>Light: The criminal is a member of an organized gang. <li>Medium: The criminal is part of a formal criminal organization. <li>Hard: The criminal has been busted recently. <li>Very Hard: The criminal runs his own organization, or is guilty of one or more serious offenses (like murder or rape). <li>Extremely Hard:The local authorities are actively pursuing the criminal. <li>Sheer Folly: The criminal runs a large organization with multiple investments and rackets. <li>Absurd: The criminal is insane
skills.notes: This skill is used to win the trust of a criminal or underworld society. It includes knowing the slang, who to hate and who to respect. A successful manoeuvre is required when a character interacts with a person who has legitimate reason to fear the law. If the manoeuvre is not successful, the criminal will not interact with the character for fear of discovery. Law enforcement officials need this skill to infiltrate criminal organizations. Once a character is a member of a given organization, he need make a manoeuvre roll only when interacting with other organizations, or with the leaders of his own organization. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on how much the criminal has at stake. (The guildmaster of the assassin's guild probably doesn't trust anyone.) The GM may adjust the difficulty of the manoeuvre if the character has been particularly faithful to the organization or individual. This skill would be modified by the familiarity of character the city/town/village in question, if the character is unfamiliar with the particular location then he would receive a negative modifier. The modifiers below are based on a city, the negative modifier should be reduced by 10 for each level of size (city, large town, town, village), noting that the familiarity modifier may never be a positive value. Familiarity Modifers: [First day in city:-40][1 week:-30][1 month:-20][3 months:-10]

skills.name: Stunned Manoeuvreing
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for manoeuvres attempted while stunned. If this bonus is used to modify a stunned manoeuvre, the normal modifier of triple SD stat bonus is not used.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Stun Removal
skills.description: This skill enables an individual to throw off the effects of stunning blows.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Medium:1 round of stun.<li>Hard:2 rounds of stun.<li>Very Hard:3-4 rounds of stun.<li>Extremely Hard:5-7 rounds of stun.<li>Sheer Folly:8-9 rounds of stun.<li>Absurd:10+ rounds of stun.
skills.notes: A successful static maneuver using this skill will remove one or more rounds of stun from the maneuverer. Failure may result in greater disorientation than before the use of this skill.,This skill can be attempted once per round. If the result of the maneuver roll is at least Near Success the character may act that round. Additional rounds of stun are removed from the end (i.e. a character must make a Stun Removal maneuver each round until there are no rounds of accrued stun.) Results: [Spectacular Failure:+3 rounds of stun] [Absolute Failure:+2 rounds of stun] [Failure or Unusual Failure:+1 round of stun] [Partial Success:No effect] [Near Success:-1 round of stun] [Success:-2 rounds of stun] [Absolute Success:-3 rounds of stun] [Unusual Success:-5 rounds of stun]

skills.name: Subdual
skills.description: This skill allows an individual to immobilize or render unconscious a target by applying a sharp blow to a precise point on the victim's upper body. The foe is assumed to be of kind (usually humanoid) and not Large or Super Large. The OB of a subduing attack cannot exceed the attacker's Subdual skill bonus (e.g., a Fighter with an OB of +120 and a Subdual bonus of +70 would only be able to apply +70 OB to his attack). Instead of rolling criticals on the critical table indicated by the weapon attack table, the AL Subduing Critical Table 4.9 (p. 102) should be used.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No Notes

skills.name: Summoning
skills.description: This skill allows a caster to specify an exact creature to be summoned with a summoning spell
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: This allows the caster to summon a horse as opposed to a four legged hoofed animal. A failure indicates the caster summons a generic creature of the type specified. Absolute failure indicates a random summoning (GM's choice). If the caster gets an absolute success

skills.name: Surfing
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to Surfing manoeuvres. This includes body, board, and channel surfing.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Body surfing a small wave <li>Easy: Manoeuvring while lying on a surfboard <li>Light: Body surfing a large wave <li>Medium: Riding a wave while standing <li>Hard: Changing orientation while riding a wave <li>Very Hard: Riding beneath the crest of a wave <li>Extremely Hard: Completing a full rotation under a wave <li>Sheer Folly: Recovering after falling <li>Absurd: Jumping from wave to wave
skills.notes: The goal of a surfer is the successful completion of a manoeuvre performed while suspended above the surface of the water. The surfer is largely at the whim of the waves, but he can change orientation within the waves, The difficulty of any manoeuvre depends on the height of the wave and the complexity of the manoeuvre performed inside the wave. Increase the difficulty of the manoeuvre by one for every 5 feet of waves.

skills.name: Surgery
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for performing major surgery, which includes performing exploratory surgery, organ transplants, acupuncture, and organ and limb repairs. Use of this skill is done with simple equipment (e.g., scalpel, anesthesia, hemostats, respirators etc.).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Light: Exploratory Surgery. Internal injuries may require exploratory surgery to make a successful Diagnostics roll. <li>Very Hard: Major Vessel Repair. Stops bleeding of a wound that is more than 5 hits/rnd. Muscle or Tendon Repair. Does not repair destroyed tissues, only torn or cut ones. <li>Extremely Hard: Organ Damage. Repairs damage to an organ, restoring its function. <li>Absurd: Minor Nerve Repair. Temporary stat penalties result, depending on the nerve damaged. Reattach Limb. Limb is functional again in 100 days. Both temporary and permanent stat penalties will result, depending on the limb. Organ Transplants. This does assume that a donor organ is available.
skills.notes: See Healing, Section 4.0.

skills.name: Surveillance
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for keeping watch over a person, place or object. Also includes the ability to determine the best approach and technique in solving a crime.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Casing an abandoned establishment <li>Easy: Guarding a small object <li>Light: Casing an establishment with regular, predicatble guard rotation <li>Medium: Following an unawaretarget. Guarding a man-sized object <li>Hard: Casing an establishment that is patrolled regularly, but at random intervals <li>Very Hard: Following a target who is actively avoiding pursuit, Guarding a large object <li>Extremely Hard: Casing an establishment whose guards are hidden or otherwize obscured <li>Sheer Folly: Guarding a huge object. (Huge objects are usually guarded by multiple persons so that each person is responsible for a smaller area <li>Absurd: Casing an establishment whose entrances are secret gates.
skills.notes: This skill is useful in a number of different contexts. It can be used by criminals or spies to case an establishment; the criminal is seeking information about the frequency and consistency of various activities. Conversely, guards use this skill to maintain an extended watch. As long as the guard is attentive, he can use his Surveillance skill to notice potential disturbances. This skill is also used to tail another person. The pursuer maintains a safe distance in order not to be seen. A successful manoeuvre indicates that the target has not been lost, and has no (additional) reason to suspect anything. Failure indicates that the target has shaken his tail (the pursuer). Partial and Near Successes indicate that the pursuer has not lost the target, but the target may notice his tail.

skills.name: Survival
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for living in a specific dangerous or hostile environment. Note that this skill encompasses only those methods needed to stay alive against the actively dangerous elements of an environment (e.g., blistering heat, cold, pressure, unusual animals typical of the environment, etc.). It does not include gathering food, although it does include the knowledge necessary to find water. Skill must be developed in each type of environment (e.g., desert, jungle, arctic, water, etc.). The GM may rule that unusually hostile environments may also be covered by this skill (e.g., vacuum, underwater, elemental planes of fire, etc.).
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: The climate is uncomfortable, but not dangerous. <li>Easy: The climate is only dangerous after extended exposure. This might include a warm or cool climate that has more extreme temperatures at noon or midnight. (A manoeuvre roll should be made once each week.) <li>Light: The climate is warm or cool and wet or dry. The difficulties-summary of such an environment include insects, exposure, etc. (A manoeuvre roll should be made once each week.) <li>Medium: The climate is hot or cold, but there is an appropriate amount of water. Threats might include dangerous plants, exposure, etc (A manoeuvre roll should be made once a day) <li>Hard: Teh climate is hot or cold and wet or dry (jungle, desert, tundra, etc). Threats include any of the above plus dangerous terrain (like sinkholes, quicksand, etc). (A menvuer roll should be made once a day) <li>Very Hard: The climate is harsh. If the character does not have adequeate shelter and clothing, death is certain (A manoeuvre roll should be made once each strategic turn. <li>Extremely Hard: The climate is harsh and the terrain is dangerous. (A manoeuvre roll should be made once each strategic turn) <li>Sheer Folly: Survival is not normally possible. The climate of the polar regions or harshest deserts qualify. (A manoeuvre should be made once an hour) <li>Absurd: the climate/terrain exceeds human capabilities. Extreme circumstances must exist (e.g., an elemental plane, a vacuum, etc.). the character has only limited survival equipment (A manoeuvre should be made once an hour)
skills.notes: The difficulty of a Survival manoeuvre depends on the harshness of the environment. The more dangerous the environment, the more frequently the character must make a manoeuvre to avoid taking damage. This manoeuvre should be made at least once a week, and no more frequently than once an hour.

skills.name: Swashbuckling
skills.description: This skill allows an individual to perform elaborate manoeuvres with his weapon, including flourishes and feats of weapon control. This skill may, at the GM's discretion, be used to recover control of a fumbled weapon (only possible if a fumble result has indicated that the wielder has lost control of a weapon, not dropped it), and may be used to perform unusual manoeuvres with one's weapon. Note that fumbles resulting from swashbuckling attempts may not be negated by further use of this skill.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Drawing a weapon with flourish <li>Easy: Tossing a weapon from hand to hand, with style. Executing a rehearsed sequence of manoeuvres <li>Light: Slicing through a candle without knocking it over. Spinning a weapon over your hand <li>Medium: Recovering a fumble <li>Hard: Carving initials into a soft substance (like dirt). Scratching an opponent without harming him <li>Very Hard: Shredding an opponent's shirt without scratching him. Kicking a weapon from the ground to your hand <li>Extremely Hard: Carving initials into a victim's chest <li>Sheer Folly: Throwing a sword in order to cut a rope (thereby dropping a chandelier or portcullis for example( <li>Absurd: throwing a sword in order to pin an opponent to a wall
skills.notes: This skill can be used in a number of ways. The most obvious is the recovery of a fumbled weapon. This skill can also be used for fantastic weapon flourishes. This can be used to intimidate an opponent or impress them with your skill.

skills.name: Swimming
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to swimming manoeuvres. Skill rank 1 will prevent the character from drowning in water over his head, provide there are no encumbrance or other penalties. Further skill ranks will enable thecharacter to make head way against a current, to stay afloat for longer periods of time without touching ground, to swim long distances, to move faster in the water, and to make manoeuvres in the water.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: An indoor pool. <li>Easy: A smooth lake. <li>Light: Against a slight current. <li>Medium: Heavy clothes. Swimming underwater. <li>Hard: Soft leather. Against a strong current. <li>Very Hard: Rigid leather. In rapids. <li>Extremely Hard: Chain armour. Against a powerful undertow. <li>Sheer Folly: Extremely fast and treacherous rapids. <li>Absurd: Plate armour.
skills.notes: The difficulty of a Swimming manoeuvre depends on the current and height of the waves. Note that a character can hold his breath for a number of rounds equal to his Constitution stat divided by 10.

skills.name: Symbol Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for manipulating and using symbols in conjunction with the appropriate symbol spells. It also allows a spell user to pursue non-magical research in defining and identifying new symbols to add to his repertoire of symbol spells. Note that the GM may decide to allow this skill to help interpret dreams.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Recognizing a symbol as magical. <li>Easy: Identifying the approximate power of a symbol. <li>Light: Identifying the realm of a symbol. <li>Medium: Learning a very low level (1-5) symbol. <li>Hard: Learning a low level (6-10) symbol. Identifying a symbol's trigger. <li>Very Hard: Learning a medium level (11-15) symbol. <li>Extremely Hard: Learning a high level (16-20) symbol. <li>Sheer Folly: Learning a very high level (21-50) symbol. <li>Absurd: Learning an extremely high level (51+) symbol.
skills.notes: Symbol Lore is used to identify the spell imbedded in a symbol by another caster. The GM might also allow this skill to be used to design new symbols. Reduce the difficulty level by one if the caster is attempting to identify the spell, not learn it. Note that a caster can memorize one symbol for every rank of Symbol Lore, plus his Memory bonus. (For example, if T'mar has an Memory bonus of +4 and 5 ranks of Symbol Lore, he could memorize 9 different symbols.)

skills.name: Tackling
skills.description: This is the skill of diving at a person in order to bring them to the ground in the intent of momentarily immobilizing them. Injury is more common than with wrestling (although part of this skill is avoiding injury to oneself during the tackle), and is used in moving situations such as chases, sports activities, etc. The Martial Arts Strikes Attack Table 4.5 (AL, p. 98) is used with a maximum result equal to an equivalent Striking Degree 1 attack, and Grappling criticals are used. If a struggle continues after a successful attack, the Wrestling skill should be used instead.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Tactical Games
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for playing games that contain very little element of chance, such as Chess or Go.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: Resolving a Tactical Games manoeuvre is different from resolving other manoeuvres. It is not possible to perform a Tactical Games manoeuvre unless one has an opponent. Each player should secretly determine the difficulty of the manoeuvre they are attempting. Whichever player succeeds at the most difficult manoeuvre, wins a point. A Partial Success reduces the difficulty by two levels, a Near Success, by one. An Absolute Success increases the difficulty by one level, an unusual by two. A given game may require the accumulation of multiple points before a winner is determined. Example: Laern and Taelen are playing Genesis (the game of L?fe). This game is played to three points. On the first round, both players attempt a Medium manoeuvre. Both succeed; neither gains a point. On the second round, both attempt a Hard manoeuvre. Laern succeeds; Taelen does not. Laern gets a point. The next round, Laern attempts a Light manoeuvre, and Taelen, a Hard manoeuvre. Laern gets an Absolute Success, increasing his manoeuvre to Medium. Taelen gets a Partial Success, reducing his manoeuvre to Light; Laern wins a second point. Finally, both attempt a Very Hard manoeuvre. Laern gets a Near Success and Taelen a Partial Success. Laern wins a third and final point.

skills.name: Tactics
skills.description: These skills provide bonuses for perceiving and planning appropriate and effective strategy in tactical military situations. Skill with each tactical situation must be developed separately.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: The situation is obviously in favour of the tactician (e.g., he outnumbers his opponents by a factor of 5:1) <li>Easy: The tactician has studied this situation (or a very similar one) very closely <li>Light: The odds are in favour of the tactician. <li>Medium: The odds are relatively even <li>Hard: The odds are against the tactician <li>Very Hard: The tactician is in an unfamiliar situation <li>Extremely Hard: The situation is definitely against the tactician <li>Sheer Folly: The situation is worthy of immediate surrender <li>Absurd: The situation is truly hopeless
skills.notes: This skill is used to provide an army or group of combatants with a bonus to their OB. If the manoeuvre roll is successful, the combatants can receive the subsequent manoeuvre bonus as a bonus to their OB, provided they follow the tacticians' plans. The difficulty of such a manoeuvre depends on the odds against the tactician. Like Tactical Games, only one side or the other can gain any benefit from this skill. Whichever side succeeds (Partial Success or better) the more difficult manoeuvre gets the subsequent manoeuvre bonus. If the manoeuvres are of equal difficulty, neither side get the indicated bonus. The examples below indicate the simplest manoeuvre that a tactician can attempt (i.e., he can voluntarily increase the difficulty of the manoeuvre).

skills.name: Tale Telling
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for conveying information in the form of stories or fables in an engaging manner. This is primarily for the purpose of entertainment or subtle instruction; attempts to inform or influence large groups of people should use Public Speaking instead. This skill may be used for improvisation or to relate memorized stories. This may (GM's discretion) also be used when attempting to memorize a new story.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Retelling an epic tale, full of fencing, fighting, torture, poison, true love, hate, revenge, giants, hunters, bad men, good men, beautiful ladies, snakes, spiders, beasts of all natures and descriptions, pain, death, brave men, coward men, strong men, chases, escapes, lies, truths, passion, and miracles. <li>Easy: Telling a bar of revelers about an adventurer's latest heroics. <li>Light: Telling an abbreviated first-hand account of an adventure (particularly useful when talking to one's parents). <li>Medium: Narrating a tale with occasional slow points. <li>Hard: Telling someone else's story with a complicated plot. <li>Very Hard: Relating an epic tale, full of the usual redundancies and long lists of places visited or people met. <li>Extremely Hard: Telling a story concerning mundane activities. <li>Sheer Folly: Enriching a legal or philosophical treatise. <li>Absurd: Reciting a genealogical list in an entertaining manner.
skills.notes: This skill is used for entertaining an audience. The ultimate goal is successfully conveying a story in an entertaining manner. Longer, less exciting stories are more difficult to tell, Only a true showman can make a lecture about genealogy interesting. character can generally memorize one epic adventure for every skill rank of Tale Telling. Modifiers: [7+ ranks in spoken language:+10] [Elves:+10] [Halflings:+15] [Improvisation:-30]

skills.name: Tattooing
skills.description: Creating marks on flesh using needles and ink.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: For larger or complex designs multiple sessions (and thus rolls) may be required.

skills.name: Teaching
skills.description: A character with teaching has a knack for explaining difficult concepts in an understandable way.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: This skill should be used whenever the character wishes to convey a concept, idea, theory or plan that could otherwise confuse the target. In general, this gives a bonus for the amount of material successfully taught to a target. Bonuses or penalties may be used as modifiers depending upon language barriers, cultural or racial differences, intelligence of student, complexity of material, distractions, etc. This skill must be used any time a character wishes to impart specific knowledge to another. This skill also allows a target to learn taught material faster than normally would be allowed.

skills.name: Tightrope-walking
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for manoeuvreing along narrow surfaces.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: 3' wide. <li>Easy: 2' wide. <li>Light: 1' wide. <li>Medium: 6 inches wide. <li>Hard: 3 inches wide. <li>Very Hard: 1 inch wide. <li>Extremely Hard: .5 inch wide. <li>Sheer Folly: .25 inch wide. <li>Absurd: .125 inch wide.
skills.notes: The difficulty of this manoeuvre depends entirely on the width of the surface upon which the character is walking and the speed of the wind. Modifiers: [Balancing Pole:+10] [Tightrope Sole :+10] [Surface (GM discretion):+30 to -70 (Sticky to Icy)] [Light Breeze:-10] [Strong Breeze:-20] [Light Wind:-30] [Strong Wind:-50] [Gale:-100]

skills.name: Time Sense
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for determining the time of day or how much time has passed over a specific period. This is a combination of the ability to estimate internally the passage of time, as well as using external references such as the sun, stars, etc. When no external references are available (e.g., underground, in a jail cell, etc.), it is significantly more difficult to estimate the passage of time. Also, after sleep or unconsciousness one typically requires the use of external reference to reset one's internal clock; the lack of same will hinder the use of this skill. This skill may be used to attempt to wake oneself from sleep at a predetermined time.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Medium: Normal manoeuvre. <li>Very Hard: Right after sleep/unconsciousness. <li>Sheer Folly: No external references.
skills.notes: A Time Sense manoeuvre has few difficulty modifiers. If the manoeuvre is successful, subtract the amount of the manoeuvre roll over 100 from 100 (e.g., 125 results in 100-25 = 75). Treat results below 0 as 0. The result is the accuracy of the information provided by the GM. (Continuing the above example, ?75%.) The GM should not provide a range, since that might offer more information than is appropriate.

skills.name: Tracking
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for Tracking manoeuvres: following a trail left by someone or something such as foot prints, broken branches, crushed grass, hanging pieces of cloth, etc. The Reading Tracks skill gives the tracker more detailed information about the tracks.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: In dust or thick mud. The person being tracked left bloody of muddy footprints <li>Easy: in snow <li>Light: Over dirt <li>Medium: Through a forest <li>Hard: Over grass <li>Very Hard: Through a swamp <li>Extremely Hard: Through a narrow stream <li>Sheer Folly: Across stone or wood <li>Absurd: Across a body of water
skills.notes: This skill is used to find and follow a set of tracks. No other information is provided by this skill. This skill should also be modified as if it were an Athletic manoeuvre with regards to pace modifiers (i.e., plus one difficulty level per pace above walk). The difficulty of this manoeuvre depends on the freshness of the tracks and the surface in which the track was made. For each hour that has elapsed since the track was made, subtract 10 from the manoeuvre roll.

skills.name: Trading
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for transactions involving a bargained exchange of money or goods, particularly with respect to rolls on the purchase and resale price charts found in Gamemaster Law.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Most people commonly purchase the goods. <li>Easy: Many people purchase the goods on a regular basis <li>Light: The goods are produced locally <li>Medium: Some people regularly purchase the goods <li>Hard: The goods are imported <li>Very Hard: Only a few people purchase the goods <li>Extremely Hard: The goods are rarely purchased, even by those who do purchase them <li>Sheer Folly: The goods are extremely rare. <li>Absurd: The goods have extremely limited utility (e.g., a boat in the middle of a desert)
skills.notes: This skill is detailed fully in Gamemaster Law., Section 12.0 p95

skills.name: Trading Lore
skills.description: This skill provides knowledge of trade-related affairs. Trade routes, customs laws, exchange rates, traditions and rituals, etc. are all encompassed by this skill.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Knowledge of today's prices locally. <li>Easy: Knowledge of current market prices in the area. <li>Light: Knowledge of current market prices. <li>Medium: Knowledge of general exchange rates in various locales. <li>Hard: Predicting tomorrow's market prices and exchange rates. <li>Very Hard: Predicting one week from now. <li>Extremely Hard: Predicting one month from now. <li>Sheer Folly: Predicting one year from now. <li>Absurd: Predicting five years from now.
skills.notes: This skill provides characters and players with knowledge about economic and market forces. This knowledge can be used to invest wisely, or determine the best market for a particular good. Additional knowledge provides the character the ability to make long term predictions. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on how familiar the character is with the market, and how far ahead the character is speculating.

skills.name: Transcend Armor
skills.description: The characters total skill bonus in Transcend Armor is applied against any Spell Casting Static Manoeuvre penalties accrued from wearing armour, wearing a helmet, or carrying equipment (similar in fashion to the way that Armor skills apply against manoeuvre penalties) to a maximum of a +0 modifier. If the penalty is reduced to zero, the character must still make the Spell Casting static manoeuvre.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: No notes

skills.name: Trapping
skills.description: This skill provides bonus to trapping skills, including setting simple snares, identifying animal runs, and a knowledge of the values of various furs, skins, etc.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Finding animals in a stocked preserve <li>Easy: Finding animals in an area where most of the natural predators have been killed <li>Light: Finding animals in a young forest <li>Medium: Finding animals in a mature forest; the lack of undergrowth lmiits the supply of food <li>Hard: Finding animals in plains <li>Very Hard: Finding animals in an area that has been hunted heavily ( or the game scared off by impending danager) <li>Extremely Hard: Finding animals in a tundra or other sparsely populated region. <li>Sheer Folly: Finding animals in a normal desert <li>Absurd: Finding animals in an especially arid desert.
skills.notes: This skill is similar to Hunting. The character uses this skill to identify good locations in which to trap animals whose fur can be sold for profit. A successful manoeuvre indicates that the trapper has found a suitable location; a Setting Traps manoeuvre is necessary to actually trap the animals. As a general rule, a trapper can obtain enough food for one person for one day every strategic turn. If the trapper is interested in a specific pelt, he will obtain one pelt every week of salable quality for every strategic turn he spends checking his traps each day. (Thus, a trapper that spends 8 hours a day working will obtain 2 pelts per week.)

skills.name: Trap Building
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus to build complex mechanisms designed to injure or immobilize other creatures. Note that this skill is the actual building of the mechanism, not the effective placement or setting of a trap.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: A simple trap involving no moving pieces (e.g., a pit). <li>Easy: A simple trap with a single moving piece (e.g., a falling net or cage). <li>Light: A simple portable trap (e.g., mouse-trap, bear-trap, etc.). <li>Medium: A trap involving counterbalances (e.g., covered pits, pressure plates, etc.). <li>Hard: A spring loaded trap. <li>Very Hard: A trap with many moving pieces (e.g., the classic rolling stone trap). <li>Extremely Hard: A trap with multiple moving pieces (e.g., a room with walls that crush its occupants). <li>Sheer Folly: Portable traps with multiple moving pieces (e.g., a trap that flings oil on its victim, followed by a piece of flint striking steel). <li>Absurd: A trap that has numerous pieces all of which must move in perfect coordination for th trap to work
skills.notes: The difficulty of this manoeuvre depends on the complexity (number of moving pieces) in the trap. Simple traps include a pit trap. Complex traps might involving a room rotating above a pool of acid after all entrances automatically lock. After 10 minutes, the trap resets itself. A Setting Traps manoeuvre may be required before or after the trap is built depending on the circumstances.

skills.name: Trickery
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for any manoeuvres involving slight-of-hand, confusing sight tricks, and other diversions.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Making a coin disappear <li>Easy: making a small object appear in one's hand <li>Light: Pulling a scarf out of an empty sleeve <li>Medium: Performing simple card trick that involve marking cards or forcing a selection <li>Hard: Distracting a target with a simple trick, while the character's other hand perrforms some other manoeuvre (like drawing a weapon) <li>Very Hard: Shuffling a deck of cards such that particular cards are dealt to specific players. The shuffler must know the exact location of the desired cards <li>Extremely Hard: Pulling a small animal out of thin air, or causing such an animal to disappear. Rabbits and doves are often used because of their docility <li>Sheer Folly: Distracting a target to allow another person to attack with surpise. the target still gets a Situational Awareness Manoeuvre to determine how surprised he is <li>Absurd: Causing an object the size of a sword to disappear. The character must be wearing very loose-fiting clothing or have some other prop.
skills.notes: Trickery is most commonly used by stage magicians to make objects appear or disappear, as if by magic. It can also be used to distract an opponent or to improve one's chances of cheating. The difficulty of the manoeuvre depends on the size of the object being hidden, and the dexterity required to cause the object to reappear. Spectacular tricks require specially designed props.

skills.name: Tumbling
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for horizontal dives, rolling, vaulting manoeuvres, or swinging on stationary objects. It can also used to decrease the damage one takes from a fall. A character could fall safely up to 2'/skill rank if a successful manoeuvre roll is made.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Performing a somersault <li>Easy: Diving to the ground to privide an additional +50 DB versus missile attacks <li>Light: Performing a cartwheel. Leaping from a prone position to standing as a 20% manoeuvre <li>Medium: Diving to saftey. If the character is currently behind cover and successfully tumbles to another position with cover, he cannot be targeted by missile weapons. If the cover is not complete, he can still be shot at while behind cover, but not while tumbling <li>Hard: Reducing the damage froma fall. A falling character can make a Tumbling Manoeuvre. the character falls safely if the fall distance is less than (2 x tumbling skill ranks) x (Tumbling manoeuvre result from Moving Manoeuvre Table / 100). If the fall distance is more than the above result, reduce the height of the fall by that amount. For example, E'Roll (who fell out of the 35' high crow's nest) attempts to tumble away safely. He has 20 ranks in Tumbling, but his result on the Hard column of the Moving Manoeuvre table is 60. He negates 2' x 20 x 60 / 100 or 24' of the fall. He still suffers the results of a +11 fall/crush attack. This is not his day. <li>Very Hard: tumbling into an opponent. If this manoeuvre is successful, the target must make an RR (ranks in Tumbling vs level) or be stunned for 1 round / 10 failure <li>Extremely Hard: Hanging off of the side of a moving object (e.g., a horse, vehicle, etc.) Either to remain unseen or to avoid falling off. <li>Sheer Folly: Leaping from a prone position to standing as a 0% manoeuvre <li>Absurd: Dropping prone and regaining your footing immediately. Friendly archers can thereby shoot over your head without running the risk of hitting you.
skills.notes: This skill is used to complete a Gymnastics manoeuvre while on the ground. Whereas this is often done gracefully, a successful Tumbling manoeuvre does not indicate how beautiful the manoeuvre was. If beauty and grace are important, a Dancing manoeuvre should be made. The difficulty of a Tumbling manoeuvre depends on the surface upon which the character is tumbling and the amount of physical strength and agility required to complete the manoeuvre. Adding extra tricks to the following manoeuvres increases the difficulty by one for each such trick. Modifiers: [Padded mat:+10] [Flat ground:0] [Rough ground:-10] [Numerous obstacles:-25]

skills.name: Tumbling Evasion
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for evading attacks by using tumbling maneuvers.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficultues provided
skills.notes: The skill rank (not the skill rank bonus) is added to the tumbler's DB for all other attacks. The Tumbling Evasion maneuver is resolved during the round it is actively used and it requires a 60% activity action. Individual may not parry, use a shield, or attack while using this skill.

skills.name: Two-weapon Combat
skills.description: This skill allows a combatant to fight with two weapons simultaneously. He is allowed to make two weapon attacks for each melee attack action, and may engage two opponents providing neither opponent is receiving any positional combat modifiers for their OB (e.g., If either opponent is receiving a +15 for flank attack or +20 for rear attack the individual cannot attack both opponents in the same round). Two-weapon Combat skill must be developed for each individual two-weapon combination (e.g., short sword/ hand axe, rapier/dagger, etc.). A characterÒs skill rank with a two-weapon combination may not exceed his skill rank of either of the individual weapons (e.g., if a Fighter has 5 skill ranks with a dagger and 9 skill ranks with a short sword, he may only have 5 skill ranks with his short sword/dagger two-weapon combination). The OB for each weapon attack is equal to the skill bonus for the Two-weapon Combat skill for the combination of those two weapons.
skills.difficulties-summary: No difficulties-summary provided
skills.notes: <li>Against 1 Opponent: There is no negative attack modification against one opponent. <li>Against 2 Opponents: There is -20 modification to both attacks. <li>Parrying: The user must reduce both weapon OBs by the same amount (i.e., the amount of his parry). Against one opponent, the user increases his DB by the amount of his parry. Against two opponents, the amount of his parry must be split between the two opponents as the user sees fit. <li>Using the off-hand: Each weapon combination is considered to have been developed for each specific weapon in a specific hand. For example, a Rogue trained in a rapier/ dagger combination might have decided to use the rapier left-handed and the dagger in his right. Switching either weapon to the other hand incurs the normal -20 penalty for use with the off-hand.

skills.name: Undead Lore
skills.description: This skill provides a bonus for recognizing and (with the proper magic and materials) creating Undead.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Identifying a creature as an undead <li>Easy: Knowledge of the major subcategories of Undead and their general differences <li>Light: Identifying a specific type of Undead. Knowledge of most general abilities <li>Medium: Knowledge of each type of Undead's specific abilities. Knowledge of Undead hierarchy; status is roughly approximate to an Undead's type <li>Hard: Knoeledge of Undead society and organization. This includes knowing which undead are likely to be encountered in the presense of other Undead <li>Very Hard: Knowledge of which Undead bear enmity towards other Undead. this might allow one actually to survive an encounter with a large number of Undead <li>Extremely Hard: Knowledge of Undead history as well as all of the major undead, including their names and personalities <li>Sheer Folly: A complete understanding of the intricacies of Undead culture, goals and habits. This level of understanding might threaten a character's physical health <li>Absurd: Knowledge of a specific minor Undead, by name alone.
skills.notes: This skill provides a character with information about Undead, their abilities and their activities. Successful use of this skill may allow a player to read certain portions of Creatures & Monsters (or at least receive a summary from the GM). This skill is useful in identifying Undead and their motivations, attack patterns, etc. A scholar may even be able to recognize Undead activity from indirect evidence (e.g., an increase in physical illness).

skills.name: Using Prepared Herbs
skills.description: This skill allows the user to properly apply magical herbs that have already been prepared for use.
skills.difficulties-summary: <li>Routine: Herbs that are ingested Medium: Herbs that are brewed or applied.
